programme_description: The Adriatic-Ionian area aligns with the perimeter of the EU strategy of the Adriatic-Ionian Region (EUSAIR), embracing a unique mix of EU partner countries, Western Balkans and third countries.

The programme will facilitate the conditions for strong effective cooperation and good relations among partner countries. It will provide a constructive contribution to the EU enlargement process, reduce disparities and improve social cohesion with non-EU countries, as well as supporting the implementation of EUSAIR as such.

The programme aims at addressing the challenges that the countries of the Adriatic-Ionian region share. These range from the safeguard of biodiversity and climate change to sustainable transport. By way of innovative methods the programme will act as a pivotal instrument for the identification of common solutions and it will contribute to making the region smarter, greener and stronger in the face of economic shocks.
Its main objectives are:

The new programme aims for a central Europe with less social and economic disparities, one which cooperates to become smarter, greener, and better connected. Its mission is to bring regions and cities together beyond borders to find fitting solutions for their citizens in a fair and equal way.

The chosen priorities include economic transition processes, climate change, and the long-term socio-economic consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic. The programme supports businesses to become more innovative; and communities - climate-neutral and resilient to climate change risks. It also fosters ideas on how to improve transport connections of rural and peripheral regions in central Europe.

In practice, the programme brings together public organisations, the private sector and civil society and finances transnational projects, which develop, test and implement solutions that are urgently needed to make central Europe more resilient and attractive. The programme supports these partnerships also with guidance and knowledge.

The Alpine region is disproportionally affected by climate change, loss of biodiversity and natural hazards. The transnational Interreg programme aims to address these challenges, making the region greener and more resilient through the implementation of the EU Green Deal in one of the most innovative regions in Europe.
The programme has divided its actions in four complementary objectives, namely:

The programme supports the implementation of the EU Strategy for the Danube Region (EUSDR), fostering transnational actions across fourteen countries, including nine EU member states and five partner countries.
The programme region is characterized by its cultural diversity and territorial and socio-economic disparities. Therefore the Interreg programme aims at creating a shared ‘Danubian’ space.

The first objective of the programme is to make the Danube region smarter, with projects devoted to enhancing innovation and technology transfer. This will require efforts to develop new skills for industrial transition and smart specialisation. In addition the programme contributes to increase the use of renewable energies, preserve the biodiversity with ecological corridors and support joint actions on management of risks related to climate change.

Moreover, the programme allows EU Member States to work together with candidates and potential candidate countries, to reach common goals and to improve standards for an efficient public administration.

The programme endeavors to achieve a resilient and connected cross-border region where sustainable development underpins economic growth, protects biodiversity, and ensures the social well-being of all inhabitants. The programme envisages joint cross-border actions to understand new needs and threats and improve the resilience and adaptability of people, organisations, and communities, by making the region greener and digital.

The main aim of the programme is to address environmental challenges linked to climate change and to the protection of nature and biodiversity. The programme will support preparation for and response to climate change in the cross-border area.

Support will be given to cross-border pilot activities for introducing and managing green infrastructure. It will protect and promote cultural heritage and tourism. This will include support for the diversification of services, in line with the emerging needs of tourists/visitors, by increasing investment in cross-border education and training.
Local SMEs will receive help in improving their competitiveness by adapting to the digital transition and supporting the green transition, especially in tourism.

The programme seeks to involve residents in finding solutions to social and territorial issues. In light of the COVID-19 pandemic, building trust and a positive mind-set, and having residents take responsibility for a better future in the cross-border region, is a must.

The vision of this cross-border programme is a border region that makes full use of its environmental, natural and cultural values. This will be achieved by promoting the preservation and sustainable utilisation of the region’s resources for tourism, and by establishing it as an attractive green tourism destination.

The main aim of the programme is to address environmental challenges linked to climate change, and to protect nature and biodiversity. Support will be given to joint cross-border projects that protect biodiversity, foster joint water and disaster management and reduce pollution.

The programme will protect and promote cultural heritage and sustainable and harmonised cross-border tourism. This will lead to a more integrated cross-border economy, one that will contribute to increased local tourism income and employment.

Actions in these priorities are supplemented by small-scale, people-to-people, trust-building projects, which are of high importance in the cross-border area as they foster closer cooperation and contribute to creating an integrated border region.

The programme focuses on a limited number of thematic areas. It will pool resources to find joint solutions to emerging challenges and it will seize every opportunity to improve the capacity for cooperation capacity.
The overall objectives of the cooperation programme are:

EU funds will also contribute to the green and digital transitions. They will address environmental issues, in particular biodiversity, and the growing challenges related to climate change and the circular economy.
The programme enshrines the protection of cultural heritage and the and promotion of tourism, while increasing investments in cross-border education and training to improve skills and competences.

Finally, the actions will be complemented by efforts to promote closer cooperation in legal and administrative matters and people-to-people actions to build trust to create a fully integrated border region.
Improving coordination and cooperation in the border area helps to reduce border barriers and unlock the potential for a resilient and competitive region.

The Programme area is extremely diversified in terms of territory and population density. It features densely populated areas on the Italian side and more rural areas on the Slovenian side. Ongoing depopulation trends affect the area, especially on the Italian side. The area’s economic performance does not fare much differently than EU standards with the Italian side being slightly above the EU average of GDP per capita and the Slovenian side being slightly below.

Interventions will focus on introducing digitization, making natural and cultural heritage more accessible for a wider public.  Moreover, enhancing Green Infrastructure Networks and fostering shared approaches, improve the management and promotion of protected areas. There is a need to promote linguistic minorities and cultural heritage at large by supporting creative industries and sustainable, accessible tourism. In the latter sector, interventions will support the shaping of an integrated approach encompassing transport, culture, education, innovation, and sustainable development. Such actions will create the conditions to increase tourism flows to peri-urban and rural areas towards sustainable approach to tourism. The programme will provide direct support to the European Capital of Culture 2025 (Nova Gorica - Gorizia), namely via a small projects fund.

The programme seeks to finance people-to-people actions to strengthen mutual trust and to overcome existing obstacles. Furthermore, it will favour collaboration in the area through the implementation of joint pilot actions, joint tools and monitoring systems, coordinated protocols, innovative joint solutions and the exchange of best practices. Additionally, joint cross-border strategies will seek to capitalise on good practices stemming from the previous Interreg Italy-Slovenia Programme(s).
Finally, Programme will promote synergies with EU EUSAIR and EUSALP Strategies.

The Urbact IV programme focuses on supporting cities in implementing solutions to tackle the green, just and digital transitions in particular, through collaboration, capacity building and expertise. The purpose is to promote integrated sustainable development in cities, improve city’s policies and improve the effectiveness of Cohesion policy in cities.

Its supports the delivery of key principles of sustainable urban development on the ground, such as good governance, integrated and place-based approaches, all making the link to the urban and territorial dimension of Cohesion policy and to its minimum requirements as per the 2021-2027 regulatory provisions.

The Programme will cover the EU 27 Member States, Norway, Switzerland as well as some countries benefitting from the Instrument for Pre-Accession (IPA) such as Albania, Montenegro, Serbia, Republic of North Macedonia, and Bosnia-Herzegovina.The URBACT programme covers the entire territory of the participating countries and is open to cities of all sizes. It will pay particular attention to cities benefitting from Cohesion policy in order to support them by increasing cooperation with other cities to find solutions, by supporting them with dedicated tools and expertise to improve their capacity to develop and implement integrated strategies and plans, to transfer innovative solutions and practices, to share and build knowledge and to find funding for planned investments and projects.

The mission of ESPON is to deliver evidence, data and advice.  Given the main territorial challenges at stake and the EU policy framework, ESPON intends to support policy makers at all levels by providing territorial evidence and knowledge to inform policy responses to strengthen EU territories’ resilience and recovery of from crises by achieving a green transition to climate-neutral economies while ensuring just living conditions in all places.
With a total budget of EUR 60 Million , (EUR 48 Million EU funding) , the Programme will cover all 27 EU Member States in partnership with Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

ESPON research and activities are highly relevant for cohesion policy programming and implementation, and as part of the interregional programmes family it particularly contributes to cohesion policy effectiveness. In addition, key areas supported through research and evidence include  the European Green Deal, Just Transition and Recovery, the Territorial Agenda 2030 (TA2030) process and implementation.

ESPON supports these processes through policy briefs, territorial evidence reports, territorial monitoring tools and other dedicated studies and outreach events, both arranged on demand of respective ESPON member countries, European cooperation partners, and the relevant intergovernmental networks. ESPON also supports macro-regional strategies, sea-basin strategies, as done in the past, with data and monitoring tools and responding to ad-hoc support requests.

It creates opportunities for organisations to connect and work together regardless of borders. With the Programme support, transnational cooperation projects drive the transition to a green and resilient region under 4 priority that encompass:

On a macro-regional level, the Programme helps implement the objectives of the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region.

The Programme seeks to strengthen and diversify the production system of Ionian Islands, by adopting a strategy for the broadening of the tourism product, enhance entrepreneurship and strengthen regional innovation. It includes actions to help small and medium enterprises to become stronger and more competitive, develop digital applications for both public and private sector and promote the regional economy.

The green transition of the region is also supported through energy saving in public buildings, actions to prevent and manage climate-related risks, support to energy communities and improved solid waste, wastewater and water management system.

Through the ERDF and ESF+ funds, the EU supports the region to upgrade the Technological and Educational Equipment in Primary and Secondary education and improve the regional educational, social and health care facilities and services for the benefit of the citizens. Moreover, the programme aims to improve the conditions of the professional integration of vulnerable social groups, encourage the participation of people with disabilities in active social life and support the modernisation of social protection systems.

Finally, it also comprises actions to regenerate urban and coastal areas of the region, promote cultural wealth and improve the citizen’s quality of life through the implementation of Integrated Territorial Investments.

programme_description: The Programme aims to support the development of Western Macedonia through research and innovation, support to start-ups, social cohesion and prosperity for all. It will assist the green and digital transition of the region and will contribute to making it more competitive, better connected, more social and inclusive, and closer to citizens and their needs.

Through the ERDF and ESF+ funds, the EU supports the region to invest in greener energy solutions, protect the environment and strengthen social cohesion. People will benefit from improved energy efficiency in public buildings, upgraded water and wastewater facilities, mitigating measures to tackle climate change, better, more inclusive and accessible education, social and health care services. Attention is given to the vulnerable population.

In addition, the programme seeks to help small and medium enterprises to become stronger and innovative in order to tackle the region’s high unemployment rate, create better quality jobs and be more prepared to compete in the global market. Training measures and interventions to support social entrepreneurship are also envisaged.

Finally, it also comprises actions to regenerate urban and rural areas of the region, promote natural heritage and cultural wealth and improve the citizen’s quality of life through the implementation of Integrated Territorial Investments.

programme_description: The Programme seeks to upgrade the role of the Region, in its economic, social and environmental dimension, promoting as development catalysts the linking of research and innovation with entrepreneurship, the development of a strong innovation ecosystem, digital economy, socio-economic inclusion, touristic and cultural identity and sustainable urban development.

Through the ERDF and ESF+ funds, the EU supports the region to invest in greener energy solutions, protect the environment and mitigate the effects of climate change, strengthen social cohesion and labour market integration of various disadvantaged groups such as Roma, elderly people and persons with disabilities. Citizens will benefit from energy efficiency upgrade in public buildings, upgraded water and wastewater facilities, extended use of digital public services, improved educational facilities and equipment for all age groups and better access to quality social and health care services.
In addition, the programme aims at enhancing small and medium enterprises to become more competitive and extrovert, closer to the global market.

Finally, it also comprises interventions to implement Integrated Territorial Investments both in urban and non-urban areas under the responsibility of local authorities improving the citizen’s quality of life.

programme_description: The ESF+ ‘Human Resources and Social Cohesion’ Programme is the largest cohesion programme in Greece for the period 2021-2027. It will contribute to the fair, green and digital transitions through projects promoting up- and re-skilling and lifelong learning. The programme will also support important initiatives – such as the new active national labour market policies, the delivery model for primary healthcare reform, reforms in vocational education and training, inclusive education and adult learning.

The programme will support actions that improve quality, efficiency and accessibility of labour market institutions, education and training systems and social services. Funding will be provided to develop action plans, studies, tools and trainings in areas such as deinstitutionalisation, inclusive education, tackling child poverty, primary healthcare, and integration of third-country nationals and Roma. These will contribute to the
of decreasing the number of persons at risk of poverty or social exclusion by at least 7.3%.

The ESF+ national programme for Greece will create employment opportunities for jobseekers, with a focus on supporting the long-term unemployed, women, and unemployed people aged 30 to 44. Dedicated measures will expand upskilling and reskilling, hiring incentives and entrepreneurship support, advancing the social economy. ESF+ investments will play a crucial role in achieving the 2030 national target of at least a 71.1% employment rate.

Dedicated measures to foster youth employment will focus on increased training, certification and work experience in growing sectors – including the green and blue economy. Outreach will be enhanced to young people not in education, employment or training – in particular those aged 25-29.

The programme will support projects that ensure equal and inclusive access to all levels of education, as well as the modernisation and increased effectiveness of labour-market institutions and education and training systems. It will contribute to increasing the responsiveness of the vocational education and training system to labour market needs, focusing on meeting the 2030 national target of at least 40% of the population being engaged in adult learning.
ESF+ investments at national level will finance social innovation actions that focus on employment and social inclusion. The programme will also support the
(ALMA) initiative for disadvantaged young people not in employment, education or training.

The programme includes actions that provide food aid and material assistance, combined with advice and initial support that can advance the social and labor-market inclusion of the most vulnerable. Special attention will be paid to children from disadvantaged families.

Through ERDF and ESF+ the programme will significantly contribute towards materialising the vision for a Digital Greece and the promotion of the country's overall economic transformation.

The EU will co-finance actions aiming at providing new and upgraded public digital services and applications to businesses and citizens ensuring the interoperability of digital systems and services and developing digital business support platforms.

Investments will be made in the digital transformation of all the municipalities of the country and in support for entrepreneurship in sectors such as tourism, culture and shipping. Furthermore digital technologies will be deployed in modernising Greece’s administrative justice and auditing services as well as in the provision of electronic health services and the enhancing of independent living.

This programme also includes investments to develop cloud infrastructures, to implement disaster sites solutions, and to create public points for wireless broadband internet access. The supported actions will be utilising and integrating cutting-edge technologies.

In addition, through the ESF+ the programme seeks to significantly contribute to the development of digital skills in the general population, including for the use of government services. It will also invest in the reskilling and upskilling of both the Government and private sector employees, including in innovative, advanced digital technologies and cyber security.

Finally, Greece’s Digital Transformation programme will significantly enhance connectivity including through investments in ultra-fast broadband infrastructure, awareness raising of local bodies on broadband issues and the updating of the National Broadband Plan.

The Programme seeks to increase the productivity and promote the internationalisation of the Greek economy. It is the main tool for the implementation of the National Smart Specialisation Strategy with its 13 Regional branches, linking research and innovation with entrepreneurship, and strengthening national and regional competitive advantages.

The programme allows small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to increase innovative productive investments and promotes the establishment of collaborative clusters. It promotes the collaboration of enterprises and start-up companies with research centres and the development of entrepreneurship through applying research results to the market and supporting innovation.
In addition, the programme aims to increase the digitization of SMEs and strengthen research on digital technologies.

It also supports SMEs by improving their access to bank financing through the use of financial instruments, allowing them to increase their size, enhance their competitiveness and become more extroverted in international markets with particular focus to the promotion of green transformation of businesses.

Finally, the programme will improve access to employment for all job seekers especially young and long-term unemployed and inactive people, promoting self-employment and small-scale entrepreneurship. It will target the development of specialised skills for industrial transition and entrepreneurship to strengthen the role of the human capital and of social investments.

programme_description: The programme aims to support the region of Eastern Macedonia-Thrace in its economic and digital development and create new jobs. It seeks to strengthen upskilling of workforce in new technologies, promote research and innovation, help small and medium businesses to become stronger and promote the smart and innovative digital transformation of both the public and private sector.

Through ERDF and ESF+ funding, the EU also supports the region’s green transition through investments in green skills related to the energy transition, energy efficiency of public buildings and the promotion of renewable energy, especially geothermy. People will also benefit from upgraded water and wastewater infrastructure, as well as mitigating actions to tackle climate change, such as anti flood and coastal protection projects.

In addition, the programme seeks to upgrade education and health infrastructure and services and promote equal access and accessibility of social protection and inclusion structures for marginalized communities and disadvantaged groups.

Finally, it also comprises actions to upgrade intra-regional connectivity and improve road safety, as well as actions to regenerate urban and non urban areas spanning throughout the region of Eastern Macedonia and Thrace through the implementation of Integrated Territorial Investments.

programme_description: The Programme seeks to improve transport connectivity, ensuring an environmentally sustainable transport sector, providing accessibility and social inclusion and strengthening security and safety of transport systems. By implementing critical infrastructure projects that have a large multiplier for the economy it aims to make the daily life of citizens better.

The programme includes investments in sustainable urban transport, the rail network and the main road network, multimodal transport, continental and island connectivity, and transport safety. Through the programme is expected the implementation of major investments: the new Line 4 of the Athens Metro, the construction of the Northern Road Axis of Crete in the section Chania - Hersonissos, the renewal of bus fleets in Athens, Thessaloniki and in important municipalities in the Regions, the upgrading of the intercity/suburban railway network at regional level with emphasis on quality, level of service and greening of public transport systems, the development of small island port infrastructures and improvement of island accessibility by development of a maritime public transport system, and 50% reduction in road accidents.

These investment will radically change the image of the country by “greening” transport, making transport safer and creating equal conditions for sustainable development, for all regions of the country.

programme_description: The programme aims at strengthening and modernising of the managemen and coordination capacities of local bodies and executive structures. It also supports the implementation of Cohesion policy interventions undertaken by the other regional programmes. It is composed of five priorities, each one translating three specific objectives.
The first three priorities (through the ERDF, ESF+ and Cohesion Fund) will focus on strengthening the programmes implementation procedures while strengthening administrative structures.

Priorities 4 and 5 (through ERDF and ESF+) aims at strengthening the effectiveness of the actors and beneficiaries involved. Both priorities will serve the needs of beneficiaries in specific areas where shortcomings have been observed. Such areas include the Municipal and Inter-municipal Water and Sewerage Companies (DEYA), Solid Waste Management Agencies (FODSA), municipalities and regional / local authorities (cases of Integrated Spatial Investments).

As an element of novelty, Greece will develop an Administrative Capacity Building (ACB) Roadmap. Its objective is to improve the administrative capacity of national and local beneficiaries and other stakeholders, thus increasing their involvement in implementation of EU funds.

The Programme seeks to strengthen and diversify the production system of South Aegean, by adopting a strategy for the broadening of the tourism product, ensuring sustainability of resources and strengthening territorial and social cohesion for the benefit of its residents and visitors. It includes actions to strengthen local research, develop digital applications in the fields of culture, tourism and tele-medicine, promote the digitalisation of SMEs and support entrepreneurship.

The green transition of the region is also supported through actions to upgrade the energy efficiency for public buildings, support of anti-flood and coastal erosion projects, projects to upgrade the water supply network and completion of wastewater treatment infrastructure.

Through the ERDF and ESF+ funds, regional education, social and healthcare services will also be reinforced, with actions aiming to improve quality and accessibility of services and actions to support the most vulnerable groups. Priority is given to improve employability, boost equal access to and inclusion in education and to actions for the integration of third-country nationals into the labour market.

Finally, the Programme comprises actions to upgrade intra-regional mobility and improve road safety, actions to regenerate urban and non urban areas of the region and promote culture and tourism through the implementation of Integrated Territorial Investments, thus improving the citizens’ quality of life.

programme_description: The programme aims to address the socio-economic and environmental consequences stemming from the decarbonisation of fossil fuel-dependent regions and help them to transition to a greener economy. The most affected territories in Greece are Western Macedonia and the wider area of Megalopolis where the energy transition results from the closure of the lignite plants and the islands of North-South Aegean and Crete where it results from the gradual phasing-out of the autonomous thermal plants using fuel oil/diesel.

The central objective of the Programme is to diversify and modernize the economy of the affected regions, to restore lost jobs, and to empower the human resources through reskilling and upskilling including interventions that cover a wide range of sectors, such as entrepreneurship and energy.

The region of W. Macedonia will emerge as an Alternative Energy Hub, due to the strong energy identity of the region and the global context in renewable energy sources and energy storage. In the area of Megalopolis, the local production system will be strengthened and diversified through the exploitation of the inherent advantages of the region, turning it into a pole of business development, with emphasis on supporting new businesses in dynamic sectors of national importance.

For the islands, the aim is to support the RES penetration and to transform the island economies (today mainly dependent on tourism and blue economy) into sustainable and innovative paradigm models (sustainable tourism, sustainable blue economy) based on the local specificities.
Just Transition Fund

The programme supports Schleswig-Holstein in its efforts to improve its research and innovation capacity and increase its attractiveness as a research hub in the areas which showed promise in the past funding period (e.g. medical robotics, sustainable marine transport, bio-economy, renewable energies). The programme will also support small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) to explore new methods, greener and aim for new markets.

Digitalisation will be improved by bundling the regional capacities to plan and implement projects and by creating hubs for artificial intelligence. The “Digital Learning Campus” will bring together businesses, educational facilities, and citizens.

Schleswig-Holstein excels in renewable energy production with wind, sun and biogas. 40% of the EU contribution will go to climate protection measures. Besides investments in energy efficiency in public buildings, EU funds will showcase innovative ways to increase efficiency, effectiveness, and storage capacity of renewables and thus accelerate the energy transition. In the field of environmental protection, key measures include resource efficiency through circular economy, decontamination as well as land restoration for future green infrastructure.

The programme will support sustainable urban mobility and sustainable integrated development of tourism in structurally weak rural areas. This will strengthen the involvement and ownership of local communities.

The North Sea region is one of the most innovative regions in Europe. It has an exemplary track record in its transition towards the generation of renewable energy generation. Nonetheless, the region is affected by a strong urban-rural divide, while the coastline will become vulnerable to the projected rise of sea levels. This latter challenge, alongside the geographical predisposition of the region, puts the European renewable energy objectives at risk.
The programme has divided its actions in four complementary objectives, namely:

The new programme aims for a central Europe with less social and economic disparities, one which cooperates to become smarter, greener, and better connected. Its mission is to bring regions and cities together beyond borders to find fitting solutions for their citizens in a fair and equal way.

The chosen priorities include economic transition processes, climate change, and the long-term socio-economic consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic. The programme supports businesses to become more innovative; and communities - climate-neutral and resilient to climate change risks. It also fosters ideas on how to improve transport connections of rural and peripheral regions in central Europe.

In practice, the programme brings together public organisations, the private sector and civil society and finances transnational projects, which develop, test and implement solutions that are urgently needed to make central Europe more resilient and attractive. The programme supports these partnerships also with guidance and knowledge.

Since the industrial revolution, North-West Europe has been at the vanguard of industrialisation and economic development in Europe. However, this century of growth came at a great cost: for the environment, for people, for territorial inequalities. The programme is looking for ways to contribute to compensate for such costs.

The overall aim of the programme and of its actions is to contribute to a balanced development across the North-West Europe programme area, regardless of the type of territory, helping to make it greener, more innovative, and more inclusive.

Through the programme, the EU supports the North-West Europe regions to be more resilient to climate change, to strengthen ecological connectivity, to reduce pollution and CO2 emissions, to transit towards greener solutions, such as renewable energy and circular economy. At the same time the EU will accompany both public and private players in the region while they develop their capacity for innovation capacity.

The programme contributes also to a more effective, inclusive, and quality labour market. In fact, it helps vulnerable groups, and it supports the emergence of available, accessible, inclusive, and resilient healthcare systems for all citizens.
Finally, it contributes to strengthen economic development, social inclusion and social innovation enhancing the role of culture and sustainable tourism.

The Alpine region is disproportionally affected by climate change, loss of biodiversity and natural hazards. The transnational Interreg programme aims to address these challenges, making the region greener and more resilient through the implementation of the EU Green Deal in one of the most innovative regions in Europe.

The programme supports the implementation of the EU Strategy for the Danube Region (EUSDR), fostering transnational actions across fourteen countries, including nine EU member states and five partner countries.
The programme region is characterized by its cultural diversity and territorial and socio-economic disparities. Therefore the Interreg programme aims at creating a shared ‘Danubian’ space.

The first objective of the programme is to make the Danube region smarter, with projects devoted to enhancing innovation and technology transfer. This will require efforts to develop new skills for industrial transition and smart specialisation. In addition the programme contributes to increase the use of renewable energies, preserve the biodiversity with ecological corridors and support joint actions on management of risks related to climate change.

Moreover, the programme allows EU Member States to work together with candidates and potential candidate countries, to reach common goals and to improve standards for an efficient public administration.
The programme aims to reach a greener region, a better-connected region, a more social region, a smarter region and a region closer to citizens.

Strategically, the programme will provide funding to projects in the many areas in which there is a potential for cooperation. This includes all areas which concern the daily lives of citizens, such as employment (as there are more than 100.000 frontier workers), education, health, as well as culture and tourism.

It also concerns the cross-border infrastructures and services, be it for the provision of energy (like the joint heating system between Strasbourg in France and Kehl in Germany) or for mobility (especially through several cross-border train lines).
Regarding the protection of the environment and climate change adaptation, several actions are envisaged, for instance concerning water management and restoration of wetlands.

In addition, the programme will support innovation, thus bringing about many opportunities for businesses and boosting competitiveness of enterprises. The programme will dedicate a significant part of its budget (almost 10%) to improving cross-border governance, by removing legal and administrative obstacles, and fostering people-to-people projects directly addressed to citizens.

The programme contributes to the climate and environment objectives of the EU, these objectives representing 25% and 27% of expenditures respectively. Eventually, the contribution towards these objectives is expected to be even higher.
The development of the programme strategy paid particular attention to finding synergies with the two relevant macro-regional EU strategies - Alpine Space (EUSALP) and Danube Region (EUSDR).

The mission of ESPON is to deliver evidence, data and advice.  Given the main territorial challenges at stake and the EU policy framework, ESPON intends to support policy makers at all levels by providing territorial evidence and knowledge to inform policy responses to strengthen EU territories’ resilience and recovery of from crises by achieving a green transition to climate-neutral economies while ensuring just living conditions in all places.
With a total budget of EUR 60 Million , (EUR 48 Million EU funding) , the Programme will cover all 27 EU Member States in partnership with Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

ESPON research and activities are highly relevant for cohesion policy programming and implementation, and as part of the interregional programmes family it particularly contributes to cohesion policy effectiveness. In addition, key areas supported through research and evidence include  the European Green Deal, Just Transition and Recovery, the Territorial Agenda 2030 (TA2030) process and implementation.

ESPON supports these processes through policy briefs, territorial evidence reports, territorial monitoring tools and other dedicated studies and outreach events, both arranged on demand of respective ESPON member countries, European cooperation partners, and the relevant intergovernmental networks. ESPON also supports macro-regional strategies, sea-basin strategies, as done in the past, with data and monitoring tools and responding to ad-hoc support requests.

The Urbact IV programme focuses on supporting cities in implementing solutions to tackle the green, just and digital transitions in particular, through collaboration, capacity building and expertise. The purpose is to promote integrated sustainable development in cities, improve city’s policies and improve the effectiveness of Cohesion policy in cities.

Its supports the delivery of key principles of sustainable urban development on the ground, such as good governance, integrated and place-based approaches, all making the link to the urban and territorial dimension of Cohesion policy and to its minimum requirements as per the 2021-2027 regulatory provisions.

The Programme will cover the EU 27 Member States, Norway, Switzerland as well as some countries benefitting from the Instrument for Pre-Accession (IPA) such as Albania, Montenegro, Serbia, Republic of North Macedonia, and Bosnia-Herzegovina.The URBACT programme covers the entire territory of the participating countries and is open to cities of all sizes. It will pay particular attention to cities benefitting from Cohesion policy in order to support them by increasing cooperation with other cities to find solutions, by supporting them with dedicated tools and expertise to improve their capacity to develop and implement integrated strategies and plans, to transfer innovative solutions and practices, to share and build knowledge and to find funding for planned investments and projects.

programme_description: The programme supports Berlin in strengthening the economy, tackling environmental challenges and creating equal living conditions and opportunities for all citizens in the growing city.

To help the capital region of Berlin to become economically stronger, the EU finances research & development activities and innovation in Berlin’s companies. EU funds support small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) in the area of technology, creative industries and social impact. The EU and Berlin also finance companies with business models in the services sector.

Climate change has a significant impact on the environment, health and the economy. Large cities such as Berlin face particular challenges due to dense construction, much traffic and limited public space. The programme helps to improve energy efficiency in buildings and enterprises and to reduce carbon emissions through sustainable urban mobility measures. Citizens benefit from better public green spaces and reduced pollution.

Population growth in recent years requires adjustments in the areas of social, educational, green and transport infrastructure. EU-funds will support the Berlin neighbourhoods through sustainable urban development measures. Citizens can enjoy new or modernised cultural offers in libraries, music schools, youth art schools, regional museums, playgrounds and municipal galleries. SMEs benefit from location marketing, development of local economic networks and cooperation projects between several small companies.

The programme invests in key sectors for the benefit of the people and businesses in Saxony. It supports the region to address economic, environmental and social challenges.

Key investments in research and innovation as well as small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) support the region to become smarter and more competitive. In particular, they strengthen technology transfer from academia to the business sector, improve the innovation capacity and enhance research infrastructure. The investments put emphasis on sectors such as energy, health and adaptation to climate change.

EU-funds also support the Saxon economy to become greener and less carbon intensive. The focus of investments lies on energy efficiency and district heating, the modernization of the public transport sector, circular economy and waste prevention. EU resources also help the region to adapt to climate change and protect Saxon citizens from natural risks such as flooding.
Sustainable urban development measures support the Saxon cities in their efforts to adapt to economic, social and demographic challenges and to climate adaptation.

As part of the programme, funding from the Just Transition Fund will alleviate the socio-economic consequences of the climate transition. The related funding will be allocated to the Lausitzer Revier, the Mitteldeutsches Revier and the city of Chemnitz. They are part of the area which will be most severely affected by the phasing-out of lignite mining for electricity generation and the transition to a climate neutral and circular economy.

programme_description: For the Euregio Meuse-Rhine area, this programme is the sixth to be implemented in the triangle of the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany around the main cities of Maastricht (NL), Liège, Hasselt (BE) and Aachen (DE).The regions are building upon a well-established partnership, based on joint experience and mutual trust.

The cross-border region features numerous high quality universities and research institutes. For this reason, the programme emphasises the development and enhancement of research and innovation capacities while featuring prominently the transition towards a net zero carbon economy. The aim of the programme is to make a clear contribution to the green and digital transitions by strengthening R&D activities, economic growth and even better exploitation of research results through targeted innovation.

The activities foreseen in this context will contribute to the development of cross-border innovation processes and applied research, involving enterprises (in particular SMEs), in order to create a strong and competitive cross-border research and innovation landscape.
The programme builds on the theme of renewable energy and energy efficiency while addressing environmental issues and challenges related to climate change and the circular economy.

The programme also focuses on quality education and attractive lifelong learning opportunities, which are not only the basis for personal development, but also an essential prerequisite for a well-functioning economy and the innovative strength of a region. The programme also focuses on ensuring equal access to healthcare and enhancing the role of culture and sustainable tourism in economic development.

In addition, a rich cultural offer and sustainable tourism are a significant driving force and an important economic factor in the Meuse-Rhine area. Interventions will be complemented by efforts to promote closer cooperation in legal and administrative matters and people-to-people actions to increase trust in order to create a fully integrated border region.

Global structural trends such as changes in value chains, digitalisation or the energy and climate transition are major challenges for Saxony-Anhalt. Economic structural change as well as digital and demographic developments are transforming the economy and society in the region. The EU supports Saxony-Anhalt in becoming greener, smarter, more competitive and closer to citizens.

The development of innovation capacities and uptake of advanced technologies are very important for the growth and competitiveness of enterprises. The programme therefore supports transformative processes and innovation in enterprises, particularly related to digitalisation. The programme focuses on small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) and helps to reinforce their growth and competitiveness in a sustainable manner.

EU funds will also help to transform Saxony-Anhalt into a greener and more sustainable region. The programme supports projects focussing on energy efficiency, intelligent networks, flood protection, climate change adaption and sustainable urban mobility.

Sustainable urban and regional development can help address the challenges of demographic and climate change. Saxony-Anhalt is the only German region where both rural and urban areas will be supported through community-led local development (CLLD). This approach includes local actors and thus brings Europe closer to the citizens.

The JTF support in Saxony-Anhalt focuses on direct business support to create and safeguard jobs and mitigate the expected transformation effects of the lignite phase-out. Measures include diversification and modernisation of the local economy as well as investments in renewables based on energy and sustainable raw materials supply. EU funds will help to maintain and develop the energy and circular economy as key sectors in the region.

The programme supports Brandenburg in strengthening innovation and economic performance, addressing the environmental challenges ahead, and creating equivalent living conditions and opportunities in urban areas as well as structural change regions.

To help Brandenburg become stronger and economically competitive the EU supports research & development and innovation in companies as well as knowledge transfer between business and science. To reap the benefits of the digital transformation, the EU supports Brandenburg in digitalising businesses, the health sector as well as the public administration.

To achieve the region’s climate change objectives, Brandenburg aims at increasing energy efficiency. The EU will support energy efficiency measures in companies and municipal swimming pools. Hydrological extremes increase the risk of damage caused by floods. Municipalities have a key role to play in preparedness, response and repair. The programme supports these efforts and finances strategic green risk management for historical gardens and parks.

Brandenburg is characterised by large regional structural differences. Cities around Berlin are likely to cope well with the consequences of population growth. Many smaller cities in the periphery will need to adapt their infrastructure to declining populations, while maintaining and improving their attractiveness and function as a place of business and life. EU-funds support the urban areas in Brandenburg through sustainable urban development measures.

The phasing out of fossil energy triggers a structural change in the most affected regions in Brandenburg: Lausitzer Revier and Uckermark. The Just Transition Fund will support Brandenburg in retaining employees and businesses in these regions. EU funds will help making the regions more attractive for resettlement and support start-ups in emerging sectors such as renewable energy, circular economy and bio economy.

The cooperation programme addresses the most important cross-border challenges in northern Germany-Poland. This maritime, peripheral region is characterised by existing socio-cultural and linguistic barriers. The programme is one of the three cross-border cooperation programmes between Germany and Poland.

The programme will focus on four priorities. These are divided into a further seven specific objectives. Within this framework, the programme supports cross-border cooperation between public institutions, the private sector and civil society.

Strategically, the programme will promote cooperation between research institutions and innovation and technology transfer on both sides of the border, to exploit the region’s full economic potential. At the same time, it will address environmental issues, in particular biodiversity and climate change. It will protect and promote cultural heritage and tourism and increase investment in cross-border education and training. These actions will be complemented by closer cooperation between public authorities and people-to-people projects to increase trust and create an integrated border region.

The programme aims to mitigate the consequences of climate change in the Mediterranean sea and its negative effects on all the territories bordering the basin and far beyond. The necessary challenge of the Green deal will also be accompanied by an effort of supervision, coordination, technical and political cooperation that will span the entire the Mediterranean basin.
Moreover, the programme aims to reinforce the potential for innovation that, with the exception of capitals and main cities, remains low across the region.

To reach these objectives, the programme has a strong climate and environment orientation. It contributes to the EU climate targets with 35% of the programme allocation and to environmental objectives - with 66% of its resources. More than 10% of the budget is devoted to tackling biodiversity issues.

The programme also plays an important role in the implementation of the Western Maritime Initiative as it shares parts of its cooperation area with the West Mediterranean area. It will allow involvement of partners beyond the programme area, thus creating links and activating synergies within and across the sea basin regions.

Finally, with the exception of Serbia, the programme area also covers the area of the Adriatic and Ionian Macro regional strategy (EUSAIR). Other Interreg programmes concerning the Adriatic Sea are expected to contribute to the Programme for the priorities related to the EUSAIR. Thus, the programme entails coordination and cooperation mechanisms to interact with other interreg programmes active in the MED area, capitalising on project outputs and results and increasing their territorial impact.

programme partners identified the transition to a greener and more social Europe as their main common challenge and opportunity. Thus, common climate risks, and the common biodiversity features are specifically addressed in the programme: 43% of the financial resources are allocated to climate objectives, while 23% of the financial resources are dedicated to biodiversity.

The programme, will support the Joint Action Plans for the prevention of risks and protection against disasters (e.g. floods, fires, desertification, coastal erosion, drought). The Plans include investments in research and innovation networks, exchange of good practices, know-how, etc.. Building on previous experiences of cross-border cooperation will be key in developing solutions and achieve results in the area of intervention. These joint action plans will mitigate the vulnerability of disaster prevention/management systems, thus improving resilience to climate change.

To contribute to the protection of the maritime environment, the programme will support actions to collect maritime data through a WEBGIS platform and provide it to a wide range of user groups (citizens, public institutions, researchers).

Tourism and culture are two important sectors for the programme area and cooperation brings added value to a number of fields that the programme will support. Actions will promote alternative forms of tourism, building on common cultural heritage and identity.
Furthermore, bulding on previous results, the programme will enure that cultural and tourist sites are accessible to vulnerable groups, including persons with disabilities.

The programme area is confronted with large flows of migrants, therefore the programme capitalises on previous experience to support an integrated system of maritime border surveillance, improving the maritime and aerial surveillance of the cross border area.

programme_name: (Interreg VI-B) Interreg NEXT Black Sea Basin
programme_description: The programme offers a unique platform for cooperation between Member States and non-EU partner countries in the Black Sea Basin area. This applies to countries like Ukraine and Moldova that were recently granted accession status and Georgia which was granted the European perspective.

Such a cooperation, which allows neighbours like Turkey and Greece to sit around the same table and join forces on the implemention of common projects is rare and highly appreciated by all stakeholders.

Although geographically eligible, Russia was suspended from all cooperation and from this programme after its unprecedented and unjustified aggression against Ukraine. The adoption of the programme was possible because of all interested parties' high commitment, including Ukraine's who took part despite its highly challenging circumstances.

The programme is prepared in line with the priorities of the EU Common Maritime Agenda. DG MARE facilitated the sea-basin strategy to address the major environmental and climate-related issues that the Black Sea Basin and its coastal areas face.

It will focus two thirds of its resources on tackling the impact of climate change and enhancing the protection of biodiversity. The remaining funds will contribute to the blue economy and smart solutions.

Through the adoption of this programme the Commission sends a strong signal of support mainly to Ukraine and the Republic of Moldova. The programme may undergo adjustments, in accordance with further develepments and the area's evolving needs in the future.

programme_name: (Interreg VI-B) NEXT Mediterranean Sea Basin (NEXT MED)
programme_description: The programme fosters fair and sustainable cooperation between 7 EU Member States and 8 partner countries in the Southern Neighbourhood (i.e. Algeria, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, Tunisia and Türkiye). The participating countries jointly developed the programme based on the principle of equal footing. There is a strong and shared understanding that many of today’s challenges in the Mediterranean Sea Basin are common across the countries in the region and that there is an urgent need to find common solutions.

The largest part of EU funding (42%) will be allocated to projects that address climate change and environmental challenges. these include energy efficiency measures, sustainable water use, climate change adaptation, circular economy as well as risk prevention.

Secondly, the programme aims to create a more competitive and smarter Mediterranean by providing support and improving conditions for SMEs. Such actions should pave the way for greater internationalisation, transnational research-business cooperation as well as reducing disparities and gaps in research and innovation across the Mediterranean.

The third aim is to foster a more social and inclusive Mediterranean by providing better quality and access to education and training. This will concern young people and disadvantaged groups in particular. Health represents a key factor in the reduction of economic and social inequalities. Therefore, project partners will focus on developing innovative digital and services that improve the delivery and efficiency of health services.

Finally, the programme aims to improve the cooperation governance across the Mediterranean through a number of tools, including joint capacity building actions for public authorities as well as transnational cooperation between citizens, civil society actors and public institutions based on bottom-up and participatory approaches.
The programme has a particular focus on young people and it will ensure a strong system of complementarities and synergies with other EU funding streams operating in the Mediterranean.

The programme aims to improve the lives of citizens who live in the border region between Greece and Albania. The programme will support people from both sides of the border in coming together to make the region greener, better connected and more inclusive.

More generally, the EU supports regions to reduce energy emissions and to transit towards greener solutions, such as renewable energy, railways and sustainable urban mobility. It also helps small and medium enterprises to become stronger and innovative to create better quality jobs and be more prepared to compete within a global market.
Finally, it is designed to better answer to citizens’ needs, through a participative mechanism at local level, which ensures more effective financial support and impact.

With regard to the digital transition, cross-border cooperation will contribute by enhancing the area’s potential in the application of digital technologies in key sectors such as creative industries and culture, agro-food industry, environment, etc…

Supporting cooperation for a greener and low carbon area addresses the potential and the needs of the region. The programme will support measures for cross-border management of climate related risks, along with measures to preserve nature and biodiversity.

The programme will facilitate the conditions for strong effective cooperation and good relations among partner countries. The programme aims at addressing the challenges that the countries of the Adriatic-Ionian region share. These range from the safeguard of biodiversity and climate change to sustainable transport. By way of innovative methods the programme will act as a pivotal instrument for the identification of common solutions and it will contribute to making the region smarter, greener and stronger in the face of economic shocks.

More specifically, the EU supports cooperation between border regions to transit towards greener solutions and protect natural resources. It helps medical staff and patients by improving e-health and social services, and invests in human capital and skills to improve cultural, touristic and entrepreneurial links across the border. It also supports authorities and decision-makers from both sides of the border to jointly improve public services and better respond to the needs of citizens in the cross-border region.

Finally, the EU supports the establishment of a new border crossing check point between Greece and North Macedonia to improve regional connectivity, improve opportunities through tourism and boost economic growth of the cross-border area.

The Brandenburg-Lubuskie area forms the central part of the German-Polish border. The programme is one of the three cross-border cooperation programmes between Germany and Poland.

The programme addresses the most important cross-border cooperation challenges along the German-Polish border, in line with the five policy objectives and the Interreg-specific objective defined in cohesion policy 2021-2027. The programme will focus on four priorities. These are divided into a further seven specific objectives. Within this framework, the programme supports cross-border cooperation between public institutions, the private sector and civil society.

Strategically, the programme promotes cooperation between research institutions and innovation and technology transfer on both sides of the border, to exploit the region’s economic potential. At the same time, it addresses environmental issues, in particular biodiversity and climate change. It will protect and promote cultural heritage and tourism and intensify investment in cross-border education and training. Projects will be complemented by closer cooperation between public authorities, and with people-to people actions, to increase trust and create a fully integrated border region.

Strategically, the programme will promote digitisation and cooperation between SMEs and research institutions, and technology transfer to exploit the region’s economic potential. At the same time, it will address environmental issues and climate change. Particular attention will be paid to promoting renewable energy, sustainable water management and the transition to a circular and resource-efficient economy.
The programme will protect and promote cultural heritage and tourism. Actions will be complemented by closer cooperation between public authorities and stakeholders.
The programme will make a significant contribution to the implementation of the EU strategy for the Baltic Sea region.

Strategically, the programme will promote cooperation between research institutions and innovation and technology transfer on both sides of the border, to exploit the region’s full economic potential. These actions will be complemented by closer cooperation between public authorities and people-to-people projects to increase trust and create an integrated border region.

The Urbact IV programme focuses on supporting cities in implementing solutions to tackle the green, just and digital transitions in particular, through collaboration, capacity building and expertise. The purpose is to promote integrated sustainable development in cities, improve city’s policies and improve the effectiveness of Cohesion policy in cities.

Its supports the delivery of key principles of sustainable urban development on the ground, such as good governance, integrated and place-based approaches, all making the link to the urban and territorial dimension of Cohesion policy and to its minimum requirements as per the 2021-2027 regulatory provisions.

The Programme will cover the EU 27 Member States, Norway, Switzerland as well as some countries benefitting from the Instrument for Pre-Accession (IPA) such as Albania, Montenegro, Serbia, Republic of North Macedonia, and Bosnia-Herzegovina.The URBACT programme covers the entire territory of the participating countries and is open to cities of all sizes. It will pay particular attention to cities benefitting from Cohesion policy in order to support them by increasing cooperation with other cities to find solutions, by supporting them with dedicated tools and expertise to improve their capacity to develop and implement integrated strategies and plans, to transfer innovative solutions and practices, to share and build knowledge and to find funding for planned investments and projects.

In the field of innovation the Świętokrzyskie region is still underperforming. Therefore, In line with regional smart specializations, the programme sets up measures to encourage the cooperation between enterprises and research and development facilities.

In the area of environment and climate,  the programme will continue its actionsto protect biodiversity and in the management of drinking and waste-water. Moreover, to develop environmental risk forecasting and warning systems, the programme will favour municipal climate change adaptation projects. In the same vein, it will support advisory systems fostering climate neutrality. Further interventions are to drive the replacement of conventional energy sources with renewables.

programme_description: The mission of ESPON is to deliver evidence, data and advice.  Given the main territorial challenges at stake and the EU policy framework, ESPON intends to support policy makers at all levels by providing territorial evidence and knowledge to inform policy responses to strengthen EU territories’ resilience and recovery of from crises by achieving a green transition to climate-neutral economies while ensuring just living conditions in all places.
With a total budget of EUR 60 Million , (EUR 48 Million EU funding) , the Programme will cover all 27 EU Member States in partnership with Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

ESPON research and activities are highly relevant for cohesion policy programming and implementation, and as part of the interregional programmes family it particularly contributes to cohesion policy effectiveness. In addition, key areas supported through research and evidence include  the European Green Deal, Just Transition and Recovery, the Territorial Agenda 2030 (TA2030) process and implementation.

ESPON supports these processes through policy briefs, territorial evidence reports, territorial monitoring tools and other dedicated studies and outreach events, both arranged on demand of respective ESPON member countries, European cooperation partners, and the relevant intergovernmental networks. ESPON also supports macro-regional strategies, sea-basin strategies, as done in the past, with data and monitoring tools and responding to ad-hoc support requests.

Good governance and adequate administrative capacity are central to the successful implementation of cohesion policy.
The programme “Technical Assistance for European Funds 2021-2027” will help all institutions involved in the implementation of 2021-2027 Cohesion Policy to increase their administrative capacity.
The aim of the programme is to ensure an effective system for the implementation of the cohesion policy. The most important interventions provided for in the programme are:

The Programme will focus on supporting implementation of horizontal principles of equal treatment, non-discrimination and respect for the Charter of Fundamental Rights. It will focus in particular on eliminating barriers for people at risk of discrimination. It will pay attention to their needs through expert support, training, and thematic conferences. Moreover, it will audit existing solutions, assessing their effectiveness in developing tools and mechanisms for the effective implementation of those horizontal principles in spending EU funds.

Regarding communication of 2021-2027 Cohesion Policy, the programme will play a strategic role and will focus on one hand, on strengthening the awareness of EU funds and their possibilities among potential applicants and beneficiaries. On the other hand, it will increase the knowledge of European funds and their benefits for the development of Poland, but especially for its regions and their citizens. The communication activities will emphasise climate change mitigation and the green transformation, while informing about the functioning of the EU and the role and its importance in Poland.

programme_name: Investing in a smarter and greener Europe
programme_description: The programme encourages investments in digitalisation and new technologies. The European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) will support the digitalisation of businesses, including the development of pilot projects in the healthcare sector. The ERDF will support greater cooperation between the University of Luxembourg and the business sector. This will play a role in the internationalisation of small businesses and the enhancement of their capacity for research and development in synergy with Horizon Europe.

Research and innovation are also among the priorities of the programme, with support to key sectors to implement a Smart Specialisation Strategy in Luxembourg. The strategy includes measures to facilitate the industry 4.0, sustainable buildings, health and communication technologies, logistics as well as spatial and urban planning. Start up projects as well as further diversification of national businesses will result from this focus on innovation.

Furthermore, funds will encourage buildings' energy efficiency, in line with the national objective of enhancing efficiency by 40-44% before 2030. With the goal of achieving decarbonisation, investments will support renewable energy sources, like hydrogen.

The entire territory of Luxembourg is eligible to receive JTF funding, especially in the South, where CO2 emissions are higher. To this end, a pilot project will support energy recovery for heat production in the municipality of Differdange. The results will benefit citizens, businesses, as well as the Luxembourg Science Centre based in the town.

This project is in line with the EU's goal to reach a total of 100 smart and climate-neutral cities by 2030. Within the JTF specific objectives, separate actions will support energy efficiency, the reconversion of former industrial sites and the reskilling of workers in relevant sectors.

Since the industrial revolution, North-West Europe has been at the vanguard of industrialisation and economic development in Europe. However, this century of growth came at a great cost: for the environment, for people, for territorial inequalities. The programme is looking for ways to contribute to compensate for such costs.

The overall aim of the programme and of its actions is to contribute to a balanced development across the North-West Europe programme area, regardless of the type of territory, helping to make it greener, more innovative, and more inclusive.

Through the programme, the EU supports the North-West Europe regions to be more resilient to climate change, to strengthen ecological connectivity, to reduce pollution and CO2 emissions, to transit towards greener solutions, such as renewable energy and circular economy. At the same time the EU will accompany both public and private players in the region while they develop their capacity for innovation capacity.

The programme contributes also to a more effective, inclusive, and quality labour market. In fact, it helps vulnerable groups, and it supports the emergence of available, accessible, inclusive, and resilient healthcare systems for all citizens.
Finally, it contributes to strengthen economic development, social inclusion and social innovation enhancing the role of culture and sustainable tourism.
The programme aims to fund projects in the many areas in which there is potential for cooperation. Examples are:
The expected results include a health observatory and the implementation of 6 cross-border, integrated territorial strategies.

programme_name: (Interreg VI-A) The Netherlands-Belgium-Germany (Euregio Maas-Rijn/ Euregio Meuse-Rhin/Euregio Maas-Rhein)
programme_description: For the Euregio Meuse-Rhine area, this programme is the sixth to be implemented in the triangle of the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany around the main cities of Maastricht (NL), Liège, Hasselt (BE) and Aachen (DE).The regions are building upon a well-established partnership, based on joint experience and mutual trust.

The cross-border region features numerous high quality universities and research institutes. For this reason, the programme emphasises the development and enhancement of research and innovation capacities while featuring prominently the transition towards a net zero carbon economy. The aim of the programme is to make a clear contribution to the green and digital transitions by strengthening R&D activities, economic growth and even better exploitation of research results through targeted innovation.

The activities foreseen in this context will contribute to the development of cross-border innovation processes and applied research, involving enterprises (in particular SMEs), in order to create a strong and competitive cross-border research and innovation landscape.
The programme builds on the theme of renewable energy and energy efficiency while addressing environmental issues and challenges related to climate change and the circular economy.

The programme also focuses on quality education and attractive lifelong learning opportunities, which are not only the basis for personal development, but also an essential prerequisite for a well-functioning economy and the innovative strength of a region. The programme also focuses on ensuring equal access to healthcare and enhancing the role of culture and sustainable tourism in economic development.

In addition, a rich cultural offer and sustainable tourism are a significant driving force and an important economic factor in the Meuse-Rhine area. Interventions will be complemented by efforts to promote closer cooperation in legal and administrative matters and people-to-people actions to increase trust in order to create a fully integrated border region.

The North Sea region is one of the most innovative regions in Europe. It has an exemplary track record in its transition towards the generation of renewable energy generation. Nonetheless, the region is affected by a strong urban-rural divide, while the coastline will become vulnerable to the projected rise of sea levels. This latter challenge, alongside the geographical predisposition of the region, puts the European renewable energy objectives at risk.
The programme has divided its actions in four complementary objectives, namely:

The JTF programme supports the transition towards climate-neutral economy in six areas with large, emission-intensive industrial clusters. The areas benefiting from the JTF are: Groningen-Emmen, Ijmond, Groot-Rijnmond, West-North-Brabant, Zeeuws-Vlaanderen and South-Limburg.
The programme will help them move away from an economy centred on fossil-fuel extraction or carbon-intensive industries.

The programme supports the diversification of the industry and its integration in new value chains useful for local small and medium-sized enterprises. It will also invest in green technologies for the chemical industry and steel production.
To cut emissions, the use of bio-based raw materials in the chemical industry, as well as the production of renewable energy and green hydrogen will receive support.

Furthermore, the programme invests in network infrastructure for green hydrogen, electrification, and the use of residual heath of non-fossil origin. Finally, the transition on the labour market is addressed through the re/upskilling of employees affected by this transition. To counter labour shortages, the programme will also mobilise job seekers and people outside the labour marke. The training offer is also strengthened through investments in training and educational infrastructure.
Just Transition Fund
The programme supports West-Netherlands in addressing and accelerating the transitions towards a climate-neutral, carbon free and circular economy, as well as towards a healthier and safer society.
The programme focusses on the valorisation of knowledge in the region and on facilitating the implementation of the innovations that will bring about these transitions in West-Netherlands.
By investing in innovation, EU funds will create opportunities for West-Netherlands, notably on

The programme supports also the roll out of innovative solutions for energy efficiency, the production and use of renewable energy, as well as for the deployment of smart energy systems and storage and for the circular economy in the region.

The programme invests in sustainable urban development in the most deprived areas in Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht. The programme supports projects that address the mismatch on the labour market and allow communities to connect and benefit from the societal and economic transitions.

The programme supports South-Netherlands in its ambition to use innovaton to have a positive impact on the economy and on society.

The programme aims to accelerate five important societal transitions (the energy, climate, raw materials, agriculture & food and health transition) by developing and supporting innovative solutions for these transitions.
At the same time, the programme supports companies in the region to seize (inter)national market opportunities in these fields.

The programme invests in innovations within individual small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) as well as cooperation actions between SMEs and knowledge institutions. Actions will include support for demonstrations of innovations in a real environment, where businesses, knowledge institutions and civil society, including end-users, work together on carrying forward innovations.

The programme supports also SMEs investing in innovations that contribute to renewable energy production and to smarter, more efficient, sustainable, stable or safer energy systems and local energy storage.
