The programme addresses the most important cooperation challenges along the German-Dutch border. These encompass the three policy objectives and the Interreg specific objective “A better cooperation governance”. It supports cross-border cooperation in innovation and between small and medium enterprises (SMEs), cooperation between public institutions and within the cross-border civil society, and the green transition. It also contributes to reducing obstacles along the border.
Strategically, the programme aims to strengthen the region’s competitive position in Europe through cooperation in the fields of research and innovation, technological development, and SME support.

Digitalisation, internationalisation, and skills are essential preconditions for future-proof and resilient SMEs. In addition to cross-border economic cooperation, partners in the programme area work together in the fields of energy transition, disaster prevention and management, labour market and public administration. For example, bog and forest fires, floods, cross-border jobs creation, health care and the public sector in general.

Simultaneously, the programme addresses increasing environmental and climate change challenges. Projects are being complemented by efforts to foster closer cooperation in legal and administrative issues and people-to-people actions to increase trust to create a fully integrated border region.
The Interreg Belgium-Netherlands programme covers almost all Flanders and South Netherlands which is a prosperous and densely populated part of Europe.

The area is a logistics hub where ports, rail, water and motorways intersect ensuring strong connectivity towards the interior of the European Union. In the border region, small and medium-sized enterprises are an economic engine, creating jobs and providing a wide range of products/services along the border.

Cooperation is focussed on applied research and innovation in SMEs with a strong societal impact.  The programme invests in the development of innovative products, services or processes addressing energy efficiency, renewable energy, integrated energy systems, climate change adaptation, the circular economy, biodiversity and air pollution. Societal impact is demonstrated through active participation and inclusion of citizens in projects that require behavioural change as part of the solution.

To address societal imbalances, the programme aims at improving cross-border access to information on job opportunities while  supporting vulnerable groups in accessing the labour market. This also includes the promotion of cross-border cooperation between educational institutions aimed at connecting vocational education to the labour market, through for example, dual or hybrid learning environments.

The Belgium-Netherlands programme also supports sustainable cross-border tourism, focussing on both hard and soft infrastructure investments. The latter includes training activities, organisation of traffic flows or sustainable site management.

The programme also focusses on removing border obstacles with the approval of two operations of strategic importance to pursue this objective. The programme will set up a Small Project Fund to address legal and ‘softer’ border bottlenecks and foster cross-border contacts through people-to-people actions.

A project is also being developed to initiate a cross-border knowledge and expertise centre between Flanders and the Netherlands on border obstacles and cross-border data. This centre will serve as a knowledge-building secretariat and a one-stop shop for resolving legal border bottlenecks.
The programme supports North Netherlands in building an open and creative innovation environment.

EU funds will assist the development, testing and implementation of new products, services and processes. Small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) and consortia of SMEs and research institutions receive assistance in seizing innovation opportunities.

The latter are bound to arise from the transition to a circular economy, the transition to sustainable health, the digital transition and the energy transition. Concerning the energy transition, the emphasis will be on harnessing the potential of renewable energy, of smart energy systems and energy storage.

With the goal of strengthening the innovation ecosystem, the programme stimulates networks within the region and supports innovative entrepreneurship, leading to the improvement of SMEs’ competencies for innovation. Human capital for smart specialisation in the region is equally crucial and will entail involving students in innovation projects and by supporting easily accessible initiatives and facilities for interaction between SMEs and research institutions.

programme_description: The programme supports innovation in East-Netherlands in three main areas:
The programme's focus lies on the valorisation of innovative technologies by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to exploit fully the economic potential of these technologies.

The programme assists SMEs and other actors, like large companies and knowledge institutions, in developing new solutions, products and applications contributing to important societal transitions. These are healthy ageing, sustainable and climate-resilient food supply and the transition to a circular economy.
Actions include the development and testing of prototypes and demonstrations of new applications that will accelerate the use of innovations in business and society.
The programme invests also in innovative renewable energy and smart energy systems solutions, products and applications which will contribute to the energy transition in East Netherlands.
Enhancing research and innovation
Renewable energy
Smart energy systems
The national ESF+ programme in the Netherlands will support people at the margins of the labour market in finding sustainable jobs.

The programme will support vulnerable people who have been on long-term assistance such as persons with disabilities, people on long-term assistance, people without basic qualifications and newly arrived migrants. Activities will help them to find a job, pursue education, personal and career development, enabling them to acquire the necessary skills for a changing labour market, while ensuring no one is left behind.  Dedicated support will be provided to people whose employment is precarious – such as people on temporary or flexible employment contracts, self-employed persons or people who risk losing their jobs because of changes in the sector in which they are employed.
Students following special and practical education, as well as ex-detainees, will also benefit from active labour-market policies, lifelong learning pathways and social inclusion activities.

Support measures will focus on improving access to the labour market, including through enhancing up- and reskilling opportunities for people with precarious employment. Projects under the programme will also help to increase the employability for disadvantaged groups, including by taking measures against discrimination.

The ESF+ in the Netherlands will support both workers and jobseekers, keeping in mind the skills needed for the green and digital transitions. Activities include (digital) skills training, career guidance, job placements, language courses, on-the-job training, job coaching, adult learning and facilitating career transitions. Particular attention will be paid to youth in special and practical education and to people in detention centres with the aim of helping them to prepare for the labour market.

The programme will finance innovative solutions to promote equal opportunities and combat anti-discrimination. It will stimulate social innovation to improve and expand childcare and social services to improve work-life balance and advance gender equality.

The Netherlands will use European resources to provide food and material aid to the most deprived – including children. Material support will include school supplies for children, feminine hygiene and other sanitary products. These measures will be accompanied by activities to improve social inclusion, such as offering increased opportunities for leisure and community involvement. Children at risk of social exclusion will be supported through sports and cultural activities.
Nearly 320 000 people are expected to benefit directly from programme activities, including:
Access to employment and activation measures for all
Addressing material deprivation
Gender balanced labour market participation
Lifelong learning and career transitions
Active inclusion and employability

programme_name: (Interreg VI-B) NEXT Mediterranean Sea Basin (NEXT MED)
programme_description: The programme fosters fair and sustainable cooperation between 7 EU Member States and 8 partner countries in the Southern Neighbourhood (i.e. Algeria, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, Tunisia and Türkiye). The participating countries jointly developed the programme based on the principle of equal footing. There is a strong and shared understanding that many of today’s challenges in the Mediterranean Sea Basin are common across the countries in the region and that there is an urgent need to find common solutions.

The largest part of EU funding (42%) will be allocated to projects that address climate change and environmental challenges. these include energy efficiency measures, sustainable water use, climate change adaptation, circular economy as well as risk prevention.

Secondly, the programme aims to create a more competitive and smarter Mediterranean by providing support and improving conditions for SMEs. Such actions should pave the way for greater internationalisation, transnational research-business cooperation as well as reducing disparities and gaps in research and innovation across the Mediterranean.

The third aim is to foster a more social and inclusive Mediterranean by providing better quality and access to education and training. This will concern young people and disadvantaged groups in particular. Health represents a key factor in the reduction of economic and social inequalities. Therefore, project partners will focus on developing innovative digital and services that improve the delivery and efficiency of health services.

Finally, the programme aims to improve the cooperation governance across the Mediterranean through a number of tools, including joint capacity building actions for public authorities as well as transnational cooperation between citizens, civil society actors and public institutions based on bottom-up and participatory approaches.
The programme has a particular focus on young people and it will ensure a strong system of complementarities and synergies with other EU funding streams operating in the Mediterranean.

programme_name: Towards a smarter, well connected and resilient economy, a greener environment and an integrated society
programme_description: The main challenges addressed by the programme are promoting a smarter and more innovative economy, fostering a greener and low carbon transition as well as supporting a more social and inclusive society.

For a smarter and more innovative economy in Malta, the Programme focuses on research and innovation (R&I), digitalisation and business growth. Specifically, the actions envisaged will strengthen R&I capacity, support digitalisation in small and medium enterprises and in public sector services. Thus, the programme will enhance SMEs’ competitiveness, stimulate entrepreneurship and sustain growth.

Support to energy efficiency will pave the way to the green transition in Malta. Efforts to promote investment in renewable energies will benefit enterprises and households while ensuring the security of electricity supply. The programme also identifies wastewater treatment and drinking water supply networks as areas of intervention that will benefit from upgrading and modernisation to reduce losses and leakages.

Waste prevention and separate collection and recycling remain key features of the programme, including through the investment in an Organic Processing Plant. Finally to stem the wave of threats to Malta’s ecosystems are exposed, Malta will benefit from support to green ecological corridors and Natura sites for green infrastructure in urban environments. A focus on sustainable active urban mobility will encourage cleaner forms of transportation and will promote alternative fuels in road transport.

With the support of JTF, the Programme will push for the decarbonisation of the international ports of Malta's mainland (the Grand Harbour and Malta Freeport). This will entail the connection of vessels to onshore electricity power supply whilst berthing, in an effort to reduce the ships' emissions of greenhouse gas emissions and the pollution of the air, and marine environment, air pollution.

For a more social and inclusive society in Malta, the Programme intends to support investments in education and vocational training facilities. In line with the ambition of de-institutionalisation, financial support will target health infrastructures and services with an emphasis on mental health. With refrence to culture and tourism, the valorisation and regeneration of Malta’s cultural heritage represents a priority in view to increase tourists’ visits and improve the social integration of supported areas.

An additional priority addresses the situaton of territorial disparity and disadvantage of Gozo, in compliance with the objectives of the selected territorial strategy, with the aim of promoting Gozo’s socio-economic development.Examples of projects to be supported within the programme include the set-up of a Business Incubation Centre, the development of a Second Electricity Interconnector, “cold ironing” reducing the pollution of ships in ports.

The programme aims to mitigate the consequences of climate change in the Mediterranean sea and its negative effects on all the territories bordering the basin and far beyond. The necessary challenge of the Green deal will also be accompanied by an effort of supervision, coordination, technical and political cooperation that will span the entire the Mediterranean basin.
Moreover, the programme aims to reinforce the potential for innovation that, with the exception of capitals and main cities, remains low across the region.

To reach these objectives, the programme has a strong climate and environment orientation. It contributes to the EU climate targets with 35% of the programme allocation and to environmental objectives - with 66% of its resources. More than 10% of the budget is devoted to tackling biodiversity issues.

The programme also plays an important role in the implementation of the Western Maritime Initiative as it shares parts of its cooperation area with the West Mediterranean area. It will allow involvement of partners beyond the programme area, thus creating links and activating synergies within and across the sea basin regions.

Finally, with the exception of Serbia, the programme area also covers the area of the Adriatic and Ionian Macro regional strategy (EUSAIR). Other Interreg programmes concerning the Adriatic Sea are expected to contribute to the Programme for the priorities related to the EUSAIR. Thus, the programme entails coordination and cooperation mechanisms to interact with other interreg programmes active in the MED area, capitalising on project outputs and results and increasing their territorial impact.

The programme will foster the socioeconomic wellbeing of Malta by reinforcing its human capital, boosting skills and creating opportunities for all. The focus will be on young people, jobseekers, people with disabilities, migrants and other vulnerable groups. It will strengthen the national employment, education, health and social sectors by improving and adapting services in response to new and emerging needs, such as long-term care.

Enhancing the quality and inclusiveness of education, training and lifelong learning are at the core of the programme activities. Strategic priorities include reducing early-school leaving and addressing skills shortages through innovative teaching methods and digital learning tools, inclusive education of vulnerable children – such as those with disabilities – and education and lifelong learning in key areas, including the green and digital transition.

The programme will support jobseekers and create employment opportunities, with a focus on hiring incentives for vulnerable people, integrated pathways for the low-skilled and long-term unemployed, the promotion of gender equality and dedicated youth employment measures. The new Aim, Learn, Master, Achieve (ALMA) initiative for disadvantaged young people not in employment, education or training will also help their integration into the job market and society.

ESF+ investments in Malta will support the social inclusion of the most vulnerable, distribution of material aid for the most deprived and social innovation. Examples include enabling services to reduce the employment gap for persons with disabilities, measures for disadvantaged children, implementing the EU Child Guarantee, and anti-discrimination measures to facilitate the integration of migrants. In addition, Malta will also invest in its health, long-term care and social protection systems by providing training to professionals, rolling out health prevention campaigns and supporting research.

The programme aims to mitigate the consequences of climate change in the Mediterranean sea and its negative effects on all the territories bordering the basin and far beyond. The necessary challenge of the Green deal will also be accompanied by an effort of supervision, coordination, technical and political cooperation that will span the entire the Mediterranean basin.
Moreover, the programme aims to reinforce the potential for innovation that, with the exception of capitals and main cities, remains low across the region.

To reach these objectives, the programme has a strong climate and environment orientation. It contributes to the EU climate targets with 35% of the programme allocation and to environmental objectives - with 66% of its resources. More than 10% of the budget is devoted to tackling biodiversity issues.

The programme also plays an important role in the implementation of the Western Maritime Initiative as it shares parts of its cooperation area with the West Mediterranean area. It will allow involvement of partners beyond the programme area, thus creating links and activating synergies within and across the sea basin regions.

Finally, with the exception of Serbia, the programme area also covers the area of the Adriatic and Ionian Macro regional strategy (EUSAIR). Other Interreg programmes concerning the Adriatic Sea are expected to contribute to the Programme for the priorities related to the EUSAIR. Thus, the programme entails coordination and cooperation mechanisms to interact with other interreg programmes active in the MED area, capitalising on project outputs and results and increasing their territorial impact.

programme_name: ESF+ Social Inclusion, Child Guarantee and Fight Against Poverty
programme_description: The ESF+ national programme on Social Inclusion, Child Guarantee and Fight Against Poverty aims to enhance socio-economic integration for those at risk of poverty and social exclusion, particularly people with disabilities, migrants, and the Roma population.

The programme strives to provide equal access to quality services for children at risk and individuals requiring long-term care. This aligns with the 2030 headline target on poverty reduction, including national sub-targets on child poverty, and supports the implementation of the Child Guarantee national action plan.

Measures are included to foster active inclusion and socio-economic integration. These pathways cater to vulnerable groups such as people with disabilities, inmates, migrants, and refugees, and include hiring incentives for people with disabilities.
The programme also addresses discrimination and gender violence, promotes the socio-economic integration of Roma people, and aims at the eradication of shanty towns.

A key aspect of the programme is the modernisation of the social protection system, which encompasses social services in rural areas. This includes training for professionals in the socio-health field and caregivers.

ESF+ investments will finance actions for deinstitutionalising the child protection system, promoting family-based care, developing quality, universal early care systems, and promoting healthy lifestyles for children.

In the area of social innovation, the programme funds projects to improve employability for vulnerable groups and supports initiatives for enhancing the child protection system, focusing on early intervention and alternatives to institutionalised care.

programme_description: The ESF+ regional programme in Murcia is dedicated to improving the socioeconomic wellbeing of people across the region, increasing access to quality employment, promoting inclusive education and training, and fostering social inclusion. ESF+ measures will focus on increasing the employability of jobseekers as well as marginalised groups such as young people and children, people with disabilities, migrants, Roma, and the homeless.

The programme allocates funds to promote and improve access to employment and reintegrate people into the labour market. Measures include incentives for permanent contracts, training, guidance, and information for self-employment and business creation. Social enterprises will receive support through subsidies to hire full-time working partners with indefinite contracts.

Young people at risk of exclusion will benefit from professional guidance for employment and self-employment, along with training and employment programmes. Subsidies for labour costs will encourage the hiring of beneficiaries of the National Youth Guarantee System.

ESF+ investments will also help to reconcile work and personal life, promoting equal access to the labour market. Additional assistance will be offered to families with dependents in their care, such as children aged 0 to 12 and close family members with disabilities.

The ESF+ regional programme will expand quality and inclusive education and its labour market relevance through measures that prevent and reduce early school leaving and develop lifelong learning. This will include the validation of non-formal learning which supports the acquisition of key competences with a focus on entrepreneurial and digital skills. Specific measures will promote the introduction of dual training and apprenticeships opportunities. The programme will also facilitate mobility for learning for all and accessibility for persons with disabilities.

Funded measures will promote active inclusion and access to quality health and social services. The ESF+ will focus on the socio-economic integration of third country nationals, Roma, and people at risk of poverty.

Specific measures aim to improve accessibility for people with disabilities, including those with severe mental disorders and those suffering from drug addiction. The programme also supports the transition to a person-centred system of care for people with mobility or other issues related to independent living in the community.

programme_name: ESF+ Employment, Education, Training and Social Economy
programme_description: Spain’s ESF+ national programme for education and social inclusion aims to enhance access to employment, ensure gender equality in the workforce, facilitate the adaptation of workers and enterprises to labour market changes, and promote better quality training systems.

The main beneficiaries are the unemployed, vulnerable people, persons with disabilities, female entrepreneurs, self-employed people, small and medium-sized enterprise (SMEs), students and teaching staff in vocational education and training (VET), students with special needs, and migrants.

The programme provides tools to address employment challenges, including increasing access to employment, improving job quality, and promoting skills for the green, digital or blue economy. Actions will also address education challenges to improve quality, reduce early school leaving and adapt training to labour-market needs. Actions under the
will reduce inequalities during childhood.

Addressing these challenges will contribute to Spain’s national targets under the European Pillar of Social Rights, which aim for a 76% employment rate by 2030, 60% adult participation in learning in the past 12 months, and a reduction of the population at risk of poverty or social exclusion by at least 2.8 million.

The programme aims to reduce unemployment through hiring incentives, improve the quality of jobs, and foster the social economy. It will promote women’s participation in the labour market and strengthen the upskilling and reskilling of workers.

ESF+ investments in Spain will improve quality and access to education, reduce early school leaving, and boost vocational education and training (VET) programmes, including dual programmes combining both classroom learning and practical work experience. Funds will also be used to update education curricula and foster collaboration between educational institutions and the business sector. Dedicated actions will support pre-doctoral education staff and researchers and facilitate the accreditation of skills and the upskilling of workers in the green, circular, blue, and digital economy.

The programme devotes resources to financially support vulnerable students, including those with special educational needs, ensuring equal opportunities for success in school. ESF+ funding also guarantees free access to early childhood education (0–3-years old), focusing on increasing access for vulnerable children.

programme_description: The regional ESF+ programme for Asturias is dedicated to advancing professional and social development, enhancing skills, and fostering opportunities for all. The primary focus centres on supporting young people, jobseekers, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.

ESF+ investments in the region will support people to develop their career opportunities through better guidance services and professional support in vocational training centres (VET). The programme also contributes to developing the regional VET system, facilitating the transition to dual VET and the incorporation of online training services.
To address the issue of early school leaving, ESF+ investments in Asturias will increase support for at-risk and vulnerable students during their primary and secondary education.

The ESF+ in Asturias will fund various training initiatives, including job workshops and activities to increase the professional potential of self-employed people. The programme also offers incentives for social economy enterprises, encouraging the creation of permanent employment contracts for people from marginalised backgrounds.

To support youth employment, the programme will provide financial incentives for companies to offer ‘first job’ opportunities. It will also support measures aimed at enhancing employment services, including improved job orientation and higher quality internships.

The ESF+ in Asturias will help to develop integrated pathways for social inclusion and labour market integration. Specialised support will be provided for people with disabilities to find and maintain employment. The programme also aims to increase the autonomy of people living in social housing, with special measures for extremely vulnerable young people who have been separated from their families or have emerged from the child protection system.

programme_description: The ESF+ regional programme in Cantabria will strengthen employment opportunities and reinforce social inclusion for vulnerable groups, including persons with disabilities, older people living in remote areas, and children with special needs.

ESF+ measures include incentives for employers to hire people facing difficulties entering the labour market, including long-term unemployed people, women above 45 years and young people. The programme actively promotes full-time, permanent employment, offering incentives for employers to turn temporary contracts into open-ended contracts. ESF+ funding will also support entrepreneurship among younger people and the social economy in general, by providing start-up funding and guidance for new business projects.

The programme allocates funds to special employment centres providing training and integrated pathways for people at risk of social exclusion. This includes vulnerable groups such as women who have experienced domestic violence, isolated or older people, and the homeless. Specialised support centres will offer dedicated assistance, featuring tailored support, information services, increased access to psychosocial counselling, personal supervision, maintenance, and housing services.

ESF+ funding will also support the establishment of in-home care services, aimed at preventing institutionalisation for those with long-term health issues. Additionally, it will facilitate the hiring of more social care professionals and promote on-site care at the homes of dependent individuals, enhancing their autonomy. Financial support will be extended to projects improving the skills and employability of extremely vulnerable young people who have experienced isolation or recently left the public protection system.

Resources will be directed towards improving mental health services for vulnerable children, along with the expansion of counselling and protection services for victims of abuse or ill-treatment.

With a focus on young people, jobseekers, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups, the programme is designed to strengthen the employment, education, and social sectors, aligning services with new and emerging needs, particularly in anticipation of the digital and green transition.

The programme will focus on enhancing the quality and inclusiveness of education and training. Strategic priorities include reducing early school leaving and addressing skills shortages through innovative teaching methods and digital learning tools.

Thanks to ESF+ funding, Aragon will promote the expansion of inclusive education for children with special education needs, especially children with autism. Funds will also be channelled into developing education and lifelong learning in key areas linked to the green and digital transition, such as vocational education and training for workers in the information and communications-technology sector.

ESF+ investments in Aragon will create employment opportunities, particularly through self-employment and the social economy, supporting jobseekers across the region. The programme focuses on dual education to enhance the employability of young people, in addition to hiring incentives for the employment of vulnerable groups and persons with disabilities. programme_description: The ESF+ regional programme for Andalucía, covering the most populous and the second-largest autonomous community in Spain, is the largest regional ESF+ programme in the country.

With a comprehensive focus on job creation, entrepreneurship, and the social economy, the programme aims to drive positive change across the region. Social inclusion and the fight against poverty are key aspects of all programme activities.

In Andalucía, the ESF+ will provide financial support for strong and sustainable business projects, as well as subsidies to create stable employment in existing or newly established cooperatives. Young people, women, jobseekers, and long-term unemployed people with low qualifications will receive particular attention, with integrated pathways developed to help them find jobs. Dedicated support will also be provided to marginalised groups such as Roma, migrants, and victims of gender-based violence.

The programme invests in enhancing language skills, particularly in rural areas, and fostering the creation of new vocational training opportunities to better match market needs and support emerging economic sectors in the region. An important focus is also placed on improving the quality of dual vocational education.

Dedicated actions will provide support to students with special educational needs, promoting home schooling and the acquisition of key competences. Spanish language promotion among migrant students is also a priority.

Education and care services will be extended to students and their families living in socially vulnerable areas to strengthen the educational and socio-emotional development of children. School equipment and family counselling sessions will be offered to young Roma as part of dedicated socio-educational programmes.

The programme aims to support lifelong learning, namely through the accreditation of competences acquired through work experience and non-formal education, as well as by providing individual learning accounts to support the upskilling of workers.

ESF+ projects in Andalucía will provide tailored career planning and employment guidance for young people. Special measures will focus on re-engaging those who have left traditional education, facilitating their return to education and training.

programme_description: The ESF+ national programme for basic material assistance supports families in severe poverty through vouchers and cards for essential items such as food and hygiene products. The programme focuses on families with dependent minors living below the severe poverty line, specifically those with incomes less than 40% of the national median income.

In addition to material assistance, personalised measures are in place to enhance social inclusion, including a social diagnosis, information on available resources, and referral or reorientation to social, educational, and health support. The programme also funds a series of services, programmes and activities geared towards social and labour market insertion.

By focusing on families with dependent minors, the programme contributes to Spain's 2030 poverty reduction target under the European Pillar of Social Rights, aiming to reduce the number of people in poverty by 2.8 million by 2030, including at least 713 000 children.
More than 1 116 000 people will benefit from vouchers/cards to purchase food and hygienic products.

programme_description: The programme aims to support projects for citizens of rural areas facing demographic challenges like ageing and depopulation. These two phenomena create imbalances along the urban/rural areas divide as well as on the littoral/interior divide, as citizens move away from the countryside and coasts to concentrate in large urban areas.

Rural areas are particularly affected by the struggle to find skilled labour force while providing quality of life and basic services, like internet access, transport and healthcare. The programme aims to experiment with joint solutions to favour social or local innovation. Areas of interventions will likely be social economy, silver economy
development based on local resources or collaborative governance between the countries of the region.

Another of the programme's main objectives is the promotion of cooperation projects attempting to mitigate the consequences of climate change. Among the most alarming consequences of climate change are the increased intensity and frequency of certain natural hazards (drought, fires, rainfalls) affecting both the environment and economic activities.

The programme area of South West Europe has strengths allowing for actions that draw from its own resources and ecosystems: extensive forest mass, connectivity of Natura 2000 network sites, high number of protected natural areas and habitats, good relative groundwater and surface water quality, previous experience in the efficient use of water resources, but also knowledge centres experienced in analyzing and finding solutions tailored to each territory. These strengths need to be combined through the INTERREG projects to respond to territorial needs.

programme_description: The programme fosters fair and sustainable cooperation between 7 EU Member States and 8 partner countries in the Southern Neighbourhood (i.e. Algeria, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, Tunisia and Türkiye). The participating countries jointly developed the programme based on the principle of equal footing. There is a strong and shared understanding that many of today’s challenges in the Mediterranean Sea Basin are common across the countries in the region and that there is an urgent need to find common solutions.

The largest part of EU funding (42%) will be allocated to projects that address climate change and environmental challenges. these include energy efficiency measures, sustainable water use, climate change adaptation, circular economy as well as risk prevention.

Secondly, the programme aims to create a more competitive and smarter Mediterranean by providing support and improving conditions for SMEs. Such actions should pave the way for greater internationalisation, transnational research-business cooperation as well as reducing disparities and gaps in research and innovation across the Mediterranean.

The third aim is to foster a more social and inclusive Mediterranean by providing better quality and access to education and training. This will concern young people and disadvantaged groups in particular. Health represents a key factor in the reduction of economic and social inequalities. Therefore, project partners will focus on developing innovative digital and services that improve the delivery and efficiency of health services.

Finally, the programme aims to improve the cooperation governance across the Mediterranean through a number of tools, including joint capacity building actions for public authorities as well as transnational cooperation between citizens, civil society actors and public institutions based on bottom-up and participatory approaches.
The programme has a particular focus on young people and it will ensure a strong system of complementarities and synergies with other EU funding streams operating in the Mediterranean.

The programme of Cantabria seeks to tackle economic and environmental challenges, as well as specialising on the key economic sectors like tourism, culture and Industry 4.0, all identified in the regional Smart Specialisation Strategy.

The programme will also support development of research and development activities within both businesses and public research centres. Moreover, investment will further digitisation of public administration and small and medium enterprises (SMEs), seeking to improve the mainstreaming of innovative business processes.

The programme will support the green transition, by deploying energy efficiency measures in public buildings and in SMEs and developing an energy efficiency strategy for the region. Other measures include climate risk adaptation, by protecting the territory from floods, water management, resource conservation and reduction of greenhouse emissions.
The region will also invest in green urban mobility by developing cycling infrastructure to connect urban nodes.
The programme will invest in the set-up of the Museum of Prehistory and Archaeology, which will be one of the pillars of the region’s specialisation in archaeology and heritage.
Lastly, Cantabria aims to revive the urban area of Torrelavega, by investing in different areas of economy and society, to avoid the ever increasing depopulation and job losses in the area.

The programme aims to mitigate the consequences of climate change in the Mediterranean sea and its negative effects on all the territories bordering the basin and far beyond. The necessary challenge of the Green deal will also be accompanied by an effort of supervision, coordination, technical and political cooperation that will span the entire the Mediterranean basin.
Moreover, the programme aims to reinforce the potential for innovation that, with the exception of capitals and main cities, remains low across the region.

To reach these objectives, the programme has a strong climate and environment orientation. More than 10% of the budget is devoted to tackling biodiversity issues.

The programme also plays an important role in the implementation of the Western Maritime Initiative as it shares parts of its cooperation area with the West Mediterranean area. It will allow involvement of partners beyond the programme area, thus creating links and activating synergies within and across the sea basin regions.

Finally, with the exception of Serbia, the programme area also covers the area of the Adriatic and Ionian Macro regional strategy (EUSAIR). Other Interreg programmes concerning the Adriatic Sea are expected to contribute to the Programme for the priorities related to the EUSAIR. Thus, the programme entails coordination and cooperation mechanisms to interact with other interreg programmes active in the MED area, capitalising on project outputs and results and increasing their territorial impact.

This objective will be attained by facilitating digital transformation; promoting decarbonisation and the ushering in the green transition. Such improvements will compound actions aimed at mitigating the effects of climate change and at fostering equal access to quality public services. In addition, all the programme’s funding priorities will help address demographic challenges, namely ageing and population decline.

It will support regional specialisation by encouraging knowledge transfer in the most competitive economic sectors and niches of excellence.

It will support small business to internationalise, improving their positioning both at national and international level. The programme will also encourage creation, consolidation, and growth of businesses, granting particular attention to technological investments.

The ERDF will support energy efficiency and the integration of renewable energies in public buildings. It will help set up public networks for the distribution of sustainable normal energy while making schools and other public buildings more energy-efficient and seamlessly integrated with the surrounding natural environment.

In parallel, EU funds will promote a more efficient use of water, achievable through the update of pipelines and regional supply networks. In addition, it will help improve substantially risk protection services, including prevention of forest fires. Likewise, the ERDF will improve accessibility and adaptation of the Natura 2000 areas with a consequent service improvement for tourists.
Finally, the ERDF will co-finance educational infrastructure, as well as renovation and purchase of high-tech equipment in regional hospitals, to improve the quality of the health system.

For that reason, blue and green projects are crucial to this programme. Through it, the EU promotes blue innovation and competitiveness in the Atlantic Area regions. From a greener perspective, the programme aims to encourage resilience to climate change, to reduce pollution and CO2 emissions, to transit towards greener solutions, such as renewable energy and circular economy.

The cooperation area is located within the Atlantic sea-basin strategy, hence, to achieve better results and a significant impact on the blue investments, the Programme should seek synergies with the sea-basin strategy.

Blue Careers, as well as skilling -or reskilling- schemes for people in the blue economy sector will contribute to a more effective and inclusive labour market. Regarding social inclusion, data shows that the access to health care in this cooperation functional area needs to be improved through an Interreg programme, considering the difficulty to finance large investment projects.

The programme pays attention to the importance of cultural heritage and the tourism sector, key economic assets for coastal areas, but also for nearby inland areas, particularly in the French, Spanish and Portuguese regions.

Finally, the programme will focus its attention on governance, a policy objective seeking to ensure a constant flow of information between the Managing authority and Member States. Such close cooperation fits the goal of an optimal implementation of the Atlantic Area Programme.

programme_description: The programme is the largest cross-border cooperation programme in the European Union. It aims at reaching a smarter, greener, more competitive and more inclusive cross-border area. Through the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF), the EU will support border regions between Spain and Portugal in tackling common challenges. Investments are targeted in line with seven priorities.
The programme will provide funding to projects in many cooperation areas, such as:
The programme will contribute respectively to the climate objectives with 30% of allocated budget and to biodiversity with 13,4% of its total budget.

The programme will develop five territorial strategies linked to the specific necessities of five programme sub-areas, promoting an approach adapted to the territory. The strategies will be developed under different themes.
The programme area falls within the geographical scope of the Atlantic Strategy and contributes to its implementation mainly by focusing on cooperation for the green and blue economy.

From the programme area analysis emerge a high diversity of needs. These comprise three countries, two coastal areas, several biogeographical areas, a great diversity of climate, coastal and inland areas, valley and mountain areas, urban and rural, populated and depopulated areas. All of these face significant economic, social and territorial disparities.

This territorial diversity is compounded by common problems and challenges, like generating and maintaining employment and economic activities; attracting people and addressing progressive ageing and depopulation, supporting public services notably in rural areas; ensuring sustainable mobility; combating poverty and exclusion; protect and sustainably use natural and cultural resources; mitigate the consequences of climate change and prevent risks.
On that basis, and thanks to an increased allocation for the new period (boosted by a financing rate at 65%), the following seven priorities for investments were set:

The programme aims to diversify the regional economy. To this end, it will support scientific and technical knowledge as well as competitiveness for small and medium enterprises. Under the specific allocation for EU outermost regions, the programme will provide a compensation to the transport sector for the additional costs linked to remoteness.

Under the social strand, projects will focus on improving the quality and inclusiveness of education, investing in infrastructure, digitisation, and health facilities. The programme will also support citizens to exercise their rights. The specific allocation for outermost regions will support cost overruns in health services and in the provision of quality care.

To ensure the green transition of the region, the programme will support the renovation of buildings and infrastructures, the conservation of its rich biodiversity, and the digitisation of the maritime transport sector.

In addition, the programme aims to boost sustainable tourism. Under the specific allocation, the programme will support investments in airport infrastructures, and the installation of a hydroelectric pump storage plant. Finally, following the eruption of the volcano in La Palma in 2022, the programme also support specific projects such as a monitoring and alert systems.

programme_description: The programme aims at boosting investments in key sectors across Spain, for the benefit of the people and businesses. Less developed regions and those facing more acute challenges stand to benefit the most from a shift towards a smarter, greener more competitive Europe, one that is closer to citizens’ needs.

Through the European Regional Development Fund, the EU helps the Spanish regions achieving the digital and smart transformation of their economies. It does so by fostering collaborative research, supporting technology transfer and innovative start-ups. Moreover, it guidesthe mainstreaming of emerging technologies in public services and enhances sustainable growth, competitiveness, and job creation in small businesses.

In addition, the programme aims to reduce energy emissions and facilitate the transition towards greener solutions, such as clean energies, railways and sustainable urban mobility. In that respect, the programme will enable important investments in renewable hydrogen and thorough renovations of public buildings to save energy. Citizens will also benefit from measures aimed at climate change adaptation, preparedness against natural disasters, sustainable water management and protection of nature.

Finally, the programme contributes to tackling territorial disparities, by investing in sustainable development in urban and rural areas. These actions are based on a participative mechanism at local level.This method ensures a more effective financial support and an impact that match more closely the citizens’ needs.

programme_description: The programme aims to contribute to the region’s economic development by investing in business competitiveness, sustainability, and social inclusion.

Through the European Regional Development Fund, the EU supports Asturias in the digital and smart transformation of its economy. It fosters collaborative research, supports entrepreneurship and innovative start-ups. It will further encourage the use of emerging technologies in public services as means to enhance the sustainable growth, competitiveness and job creation in small and medium-sized enterprises. The programme will invest in new digital public services, with a  focus to the needs of rural and depopulated areas.

The green transition is a central priority in the programme. Thus, it will devote resources towards energy efficiency measures, like the deep renovation of public buildings and increasing energy generation from renewable sources. Additionally, the programme will support the upgrading of water management, to prevent the waste of water. Coherently, the programme will support climate change adaptation projects, which ultimately contribute to protecting nature and biodiversity, one of the region’s main assets.
Finally, the programme aims to reinforce the region’s social accessibility and quality of services, by investing in education centres and in health infrastructure, both in primary care and hospitals.

The programme will contribute to the economic development and growth of Andalusia, by investing in business competitiveness, sustainability, and social inclusion.

EU support will focus on the development of research and innovation capacities and the uptake of advanced technologies. It will cover research and innovation activities, market-oriented transfer of knowledge and will promote cooperation between the various actors of Andalusia’s research and innovation environment. Digital transformation seeks to achieve more efficient public services, more extensive use of open data, advanced telecommunications and work-based infrastructures for increased public and private capacity.

The programme will contribute to improving SMEs competitiveness, by promoting entrepreneurship, cooperation within the Andalusian business sector, as well as internationalisation of the economy to attract foreign investments.

The programme will also support improving the energy efficiency of public and private buildings, along with the deployment of smart distribution grids and storage solutions. of. It will boost the deployment of renewable energy in the region, including by increasing the availability of technologies that are rarely obtainable on the market.

Due to its geographical location, Andalusia is characterised by its high vulnerability to climate change. The ERDF will support mitigation, adaptation, and prevention actions, to improve the region’s resilience against natural disasters. Moreover, the programme will support the sustainable management of water from an integrated perspective. This entails fostering the transition to a circular economy, as well as enhancing the protection and preservation of nature, including Natura 2000 sites. On sustainable mobility, investments will support the improvement of sustainable urban mobility. Actions will promote active mobility as well as supporting different means of public transport.

The programme also helps to improve road safety  and to make TEN-T nodes more accessible by train. These interventions accompany the optimisation of interurban mobility services and the development of the Andalusian Logistics Network.

The ERDF will contribute to social inclusion by improving the quality of education at all levels, including vocational education . The programme also supports the rehabilitation and regeneration of deprived urban areas. Specific actions are aimed at to improving accessibility of public infrastructure for vulnerable groups. Consistently wit these areas of interventions, the programme will finance the upgrade of hospitals and primary care centres. The promotion of sustainable tourism, the protection and rehabilitation of cultural and natural heritage will also benefit from ERDF financing.
Lastly, the programme seeks to support urban areas establishing the Sustainable Urban Development Fund which will combine public-private resources.

The ESF+ National Programme for Youth Employment is designed to address the challenges faced by Spanish youth in accessing quality, permanent employment. This programme aims to improve working conditions for young people and facilitate their integration in the labour market by promoting permanent contracts, reinforcing training opportunities, and encouraging self-employment.

The overarching goal of the programme is to contribute to achieving the national 2030 target under the European Pillar of Social Rights of a 76% employment rate, with a specific focus on reducing the share of young people not in employment, education, or training to 10%.

The programme directs investments towards actions that assist young people in adapting to a changing labour market, emphasising improved working conditions through incentives for employers to provide permanent contracts. ESF+ measures will concentrate on upskilling youth, with projects focusing on training in digital and green skills, interregional and intra-EU mobility programmes, school workshops and first professional experiences in the R&D sector. There are also measures to promote and encourage self-employment among young people through training and targeted incentives.

ESF+ investments will fund individual counselling, career guidance, job information and job search assistance. Dedicated actions will promote the active inclusion of young people in the labour market and help to improve their employability. This includes participation in the
for disadvantaged young people and the establishment of active inclusion pathways for persons with disabilities and young people at risk of social exclusion.

programme_description: The programme sets out to address the main challenges that hamper regional competitiveness. Namely, the small and medium enterprises’ (SMEs) low level of productivity, the lack of innovation, the reduced access to external markets and the strong dependence on tourism. In addition, the programme addresses environmental and climate vulnerability linked to insularity, such as pressure on natural resources and dependency on external energy.

The ERDF will support new scientific and technologic infrastructure for the benefit of SMEs, applied research projects and technology transfer between research centres, businesses, and the University. It will also support the digitalisation of public services and businesses thus increasing SME competitiveness in sectors with high added value.

The programme will also support energy-efficient renovation of public and private buildings, along with the production of renewable energies, including through local renewable energy communities. Efficient use of water resources also plays a key role and will benefit from several water treatment plants.

The programme will also promote the transition to a circular economy by investing in separate waste collection systems and waste treatment at local level. In addition, investments will support sustainable urban mobility, mainly in the functional urban area of Palma de Mallorca.
Finally, the programme will support educational infrastructure, the rehabilitation and construction of social housing for disadvantaged groups and the new symphonic orchestra of the Balearic Islands.

programme_description: The Just Transition Fund (JTF) addresses the regions most affected by the ongoing phase-out of coal in Spain. It supports growth, economic diversification and job creation. The programme will benefit the region of Asturias, the province of A Coruña in Galicia, the provinces of Teruel in Aragón, León, and Palencia in Castilla y León, Almería, Cádiz, and Córdoba in Andalusia; and a group of municipalities around Alcúdia on the island of Mallorca.

The funding will help the country's fair transition to a climate neutral economy The programme will invest primarily in energy efficiency, circular economy and renewable energy sources (e.g. solar, offshore wind, renewable hydrogen). Such investments, in line with climate objectives  will help transform these economies and meet the  energy needs of the future.

The programme will also finance innovation and research projects in areas related to the green transition, helping develop solutions and technologies that stimulate new economic activities. In addition, looking to support long-term economic transformations and generateing opportunities, the JTF will support SMEs and projects in sectors that have been identified as strategic.

Several regions will develop projects fostering sustainable and cultural tourism as well as the conservation of the ethnographic heritage. Rural municipalities affected by closures of mining sites or power plants affecting rural areas, will benefit from JTF  investments to continue thriving. their endogenous strengths.

Finally, the JTF will pay special attention to training and reskilling unemployed people, and workers in carbon-intensive industries. With the JTF, training will be made available for workers who seek qualifications in sustainable development and aspire to well-paid jobs.

The mission of ESPON is to deliver evidence, data and advice.  Given the main territorial challenges at stake and the EU policy framework, ESPON intends to support policy makers at all levels by providing territorial evidence and knowledge to inform policy responses to strengthen EU territories’ resilience and recovery of from crises by achieving a green transition to climate-neutral economies while ensuring just living conditions in all places.
With a total budget of EUR 60 Million , (EUR 48 Million EU funding) , the Programme will cover all 27 EU Member States in partnership with Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

ESPON research and activities are highly relevant for cohesion policy programming and implementation, and as part of the interregional programmes family it particularly contributes to cohesion policy effectiveness. In addition, key areas supported through research and evidence include  the European Green Deal, Just Transition and Recovery, the Territorial Agenda 2030 (TA2030) process and implementation.

ESPON supports these processes through policy briefs, territorial evidence reports, territorial monitoring tools and other dedicated studies and outreach events, both arranged on demand of respective ESPON member countries, European cooperation partners, and the relevant intergovernmental networks. ESPON also supports macro-regional strategies, sea-basin strategies, as done in the past, with data and monitoring tools and responding to ad-hoc support requests.

Since 2004, the EU strategy for the Outermost regions (OR) identified the intensification of cooperation with neighbouring countries as one of its key pillars.

For this reason, in recent decades, the Programme emerged as the main instrument for promoting the regional integration of the ORs into their geographical areas of reference. This highlights the importance of regional cooperation and good neighbourly relations, namely through cooperation with seven African countries in the Macaronesia and Guinea Gulf.

The programme promotes the ecological transition, supporting the development of a green and blue economy, fighting climate change through risk prevention and disaster management in its cooperation projects with neighboring African countries.
The improvement of competitiveness through innovative and smart economic transformation represents another priority of the programme.
Improving migration management at origin and destination is the last priority of the programme.

Finally, the MAC Programme is complementary to the new EU's "Global Europe" - Neighborhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument (NDICI). As stated in the Interreg regulation, it is possible to include a specific financial allocation to help partner countries and regions in strengthening their cooperation with the outermost regions in their neighborhood.

The programme area connects Western and Eastern Europe, and stretches along a main corridor between the Baltic and Adriatic seas. This geographic location has contributed to above-average economic growth. However, the area still experiences regional disparities: north-south, east-west, and between urban agglomerations and structurally weaker rural areas.

In addition, all regions are undergoing demographic changes. These trends are expected to continue. In this context, the long tradition of cross-border coordination and cooperation will continue. Focus will be placed on addressing common challenges to bring added value to the programme area.

The main aim of the programme is to address climate change – including sustainable water management – and to protect nature and biodiversity. As such, operations with an environmental focus are strategically important. The programme endeavors to protect and promote cultural heritage and tourism and increase investment in cross-border education and training.

These priorities are supplemented by efforts to foster closer cooperation in legal and administrative questions and people-to people activities, to increase trust and create an integrated border region.

programme_description: The programme addresses the technological and climate challenges and their impact on competitiveness, as well as economic, social and environmental sustainability in South Tyrol. The actions supported are divided into three priorities: driving technological change (smart), tackling climate change (green) and making mobility sustainable (mobility).

Specifically for research, innovation and development, support will be provided to projects in the fields of smart specialisation (RIS3), high quality research infrastructures, innovation clusters and community spaces for innovation.
Digitalisation focuses on integrated and interoperable infrastructures and e-government services for citizens and businesses.
In the energy sector, the energy efficiency of public buildings and the construction of district heating and cooling networks will be promoted.

Risk prevention is done by securing and strengthening the resilience of the areas most vulnerable to hydraulic, hydrogeological and avalanche risks, and by modernising the region’s warning and alarm system.
In the area of mobility, the programme will fund digital solutions, cycling infrastructure and low-emission public transport.

The programme sets out to address the technological and environmental challenges in Abruzzo. More specifically, the programme focuses on their impact on competitiveness, and on the economic, social and environmental sustainability of the region. The actions supported are divided into five priorities:

In accordance with the first priority, interventions will emphasise research and innovation to the benefit of production systems. This will compound the support to the digitalisation of businesses’ production processes, coherently with the revised Smart Specialisation Strategy.

The priority “Digital Connectivity” will devote resources to the strengthening of the Regional Area Network (RAN), so that advanced digital services benefit citizens, businesses, research organisations and public bodies.

Under the third priority, the focus is on a clean and fair energy transition. This will include green and blue investments, circular economy solutions, and climate change mitigation and adaptation measures. Concretely, actions entail the installation of renewable energy production plants (photovoltaic and biomass), adaptation to climate change and disaster risk prevention and the transition to a resource-efficient and circular economy. To that end, the programme will support the establishment of facilities for the treatment and recycling of municipal waste, and the modernisation of the waste collection system. Moreover, businesses implementing circular economy processes in their production will receive support. Finally, EU funds will support the protection of biodiversity.

In the area of urban mobility, interventions aim at promoting multimodal mobility as part of the transition to a net-zero carbon economy. For instance, this will be achieved through the purchase of zero-emission electric city buses and the creation of digital services in local public transport.
The fifth priority focuses on the implementation of the territorial strategies for the eight main urban areas of the region and the municipalities functionally linked to them.

The programme includes priorities for each of the two funds: the ESF+ will finance actions for improving the education systems, training of teachers and initiatives for students’ skills, while the ERDF will invest in physical infrastructures, such as gyms, canteens, pedagogical rooms and labs, and digital equipment.
Supported projects will modernise the curricula of education institutions. Activities will include self-assessment tools for schools, as well as training for teachers and administrative personnel.

Actions funded by ESF+ will focus on strengthening students’ basic written and numerical skills, as well as on helping young people to develop skills for the green and digital transitions. programme_description: The National Programme Metro+ and southern medium cities supports the territories of 14 metropolitan cities in Italy. Funding is allocated to measures in the sectors of digital services for citizens, social inclusion of disadvantaged groups, energy efficiency, green infrastructure, public buildings and support for sustainable mobility. Moreover, new measures addresses issues such as the enhancement of cultural and natural heritage and the development of sustainable tourism. Other measure will intervene in the field of security with actions aimed at upgrading the peripheral areas of metropolitan cities, including those in the south.

On the other hand, the National Programme Metro+ will intervene also in medium-sized cities in the south of Italy (located outside the perimeter of metropolitan cities) by funding inclusion measures to reduce poverty and exclusion. This will be achieved through coordinated actions for social inclusion and innovation aimed at improving the quality of life of citizens living in suburbs and marginal areas.

The Programme contributes also to the implementation of those macro-regional and basin strategies covering the urban areas concerned: EUSALP (Northern Metropolitan Cities), EUSAIR (Metropolitan Cities and Medium-South Cities located on the Adriatic-Ionian side) and WESTMED (Metropolitan Cities and Medium-South Cities).

Moreover, by sharing and encouraging urban initiatives supported by the European Urban Initiative (EUI), the National Programme will promote synergies with innovative urban actions, capitalising on the experience of the thematic partnerships of the European Urban Agenda. It will also support the promotion of new project partnerships between European cities, capitalising on the experiences and results of the URBACT programme and other Interreg programmes.
Finally, the National Programme will promote the New European Bauhaus methodological approach.

programme_description: The National Programme Security for Legality 2021-2027 continues part of the interventions of the National Programme Security for Legality 2014-2020. It invests in digital systems for the national ministry of interior affairs and for local authorities.

Interventions that improve the digital collection and exchange of information allow to identify and counter corruption and crime in the less developed regions of Italy (Molise, Campania, Puglia, Basilicata, Calabria, Sicilia and Sardegna). By contributing to the overall security of, the programme enables citizens, businesses and other local actors to thrive and grow.
The programme focuses on the less developed regions of Italy, where the occurrence of crime and corruption is above average, negatively affecting the welfare of citizens and their livelihoods.

Drawing on the lessons learnt during the previous programming period, the programme also includes interventions to improve the administrative capacity of the involved local authorities for an efficient implementation of the interventions.

The Just Transition Fund National Programme aims at supporting a just transition towards low-emissions economic sectors in the Province of Taranto (Apulia) and in Sulcis Iglesiente (Sardinia). It will foster economic diversification and job creation in green sectors, including renewable energy.

The main challenges addressed by the programme are countering the effect of the transition by mitigating the social and employment effects increasing, increasing the share of renewable energy and promoting the diversification of local production systems.

To counter the effect of the transition in Sulcis Iglesiente, the programme supports the creation of renewable energy communities to reduce energy poverty. It encourages the use of clean technologies in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to improve efficiency of production processes and of businesses.

In the province of Taranto, the programme focuses on ensuring the availability of affordable energy from renewable sources in public buildings, and supports the implementation of projects related to green hydrogen.

To promote the diversification of the local production system in Sulcis Iglesiente the programme supports projects that help SMEs introduce new technological and innovative solutions in the field of circular economy, energy conversion of production processes, remediation, and reuse of contaminated areas.

In the province of Taranto, the programme will reduce the reliance of the local economy on carbon intensive activities by promoting economic diversification, mitigating job and economic losses due to the transition, developing excellence sectors of the local economy (cultural and creative enterprises and aerospace).

To mitigate the social and employment effects of the transition in the area of Sulcis Iglesiente, the programme focuses on up-skilling and re-skilling workers affected by the transition improving the offer of courses and trainings.

Furthermore, the programme will strengthen services to support jobseekers and the creation of new enterprises. In the Province of Taranto, the programme supports the training of workers at risk of unemployment/inactivity to facilitate their transfer to technological sectors linked to the energy transition and circular economy.

Examples of projects to be supported by the programme include the construction of a facility for the chemical storage of renewable energy through the production of green fuels in Sulcis Iglesiente, and the restoration of polluted land by planting different species covering approximately 996 hectares in the Province of Taranto.

programme_name: NP Research, innovation and competitiveness for green and digital transition 2021-2027
programme_description: The National Programme Research, Innovation and Competitiveness supports the smart and sustainable growth of the productive system in the less developed regions of Italy. These areas presents a difficult socio-economic framework characterized by a range of weaknesses. Such weaknesses include generally low investment levels in research or sectors like digital and green technologies. In these regions enterprises have reduced size, little access to credit, skilled labour or international markets, adding to an already limited presence of enterprises in the high tech sector.

The programme aims to redress these conditions as well as promoting the production of clean renewable energy, and its efficient use through the development of smart transmission systems and distribution networks.
The interventions are oriented by two priority axes (plus a Technical Assistance axis) and divided in six specific objectives: A more competitive, greener, smarter and resilient Europe.

Specifically for research, innovation and development, support will go to projects in the fields of competitive and strategic research, smart specialisation (RIS3), innovation clusters and community spaces for innovation, technology transfer processes and services. Interventions on digitalisation focus on the promotion and strengthening of the digital transition of the entrepreneurial system.

The programme will foster competitiveness and a sustainable transition for the SMEs in the involved regions. Increased competitiveness will be supported through the support to productive investments, creation of new enterprises, internationalisation of SMEs and access to credit for entreprises. The programme will also support the development of the necessary competences for the introduction of new technologies in the productive system.

In the energy sector, the programme will promote the production and utilisation of renewable energy sources, as well as the development and the modernisation of smart grids for energy transmission and distribution.

The programme allows a wide use of revolving financial instruments, reaching 32 % of the global budget, and covering almost all the Specific Objectives selected. Loans represent about 75% of the instruments, which contribute to the mainstreaming of the European Bauhaus principles.

The programme contributes to the climate targets with 33 % of the budget dedicated to activities with an impact on climate; in this regard, beside the activities, the programme has a strong focus on investments on green transition.

programme_description: The Polish European Funds for Social Development programme is the second biggest ESF+ programme in the EU. It will improve the quality of social services, inclusiveness of education systems and conditions for life-long learning. It will provide people in the region with opportunities to gain digital and green skills, boosting both employability and career prospects. The programme will expand childcare and improve work-life balance for carers, helping to increase the participation of women in the labour market.

The programme places strategic priority on supporting persons with disabilities and their families to become socially and professionally active. It will develop the social economy and dedicated investments will be allocated to make social and healthcare services more accessible and affordable. It will also strengthen the capacity of social partners and civil society organisations.

Programme activities will be aligned with the Recovery and Resilience Plan for Poland, which aims to increase the effectiveness of public employment services, childcare, the social economy, long-term care and healthcare.

The programme will invest in measures for upskilling and reskilling of people working across sectors such as labour market institutions, enterprises, vocational and higher education, social assistance and healthcare. It will also finance improvement of upskilling systems, with a focus on helping workers develop necessary skills for the green and digital transitions. Digital Development Clubs will be established to help people with very limited digital skills, such as older citizens, to thrive in an increasingly digital society. The programme will also fund Individual Learning Accounts to promote adult life-long learning. Transnational cooperation measures will expand upskilling opportunities, enabling the exchange of experiences and mutual learning.

A strategic priority will be the creation and functioning of more childcare places during the first two years of investment, as well as upskilling of child carers. Projects will also support the development and testing of models of support for women and carers, fostering the collection of robust data on gender equality and equal representation in the labour market.

Supported employment solutions will be further developed, enabling persons with disabilities to integrate into the labour market. These solutions will include training for administration on the organisation of workplace solutions and support for the creation of a network of supported employment agencies providing services to persons with disabilities. ESF+ investments will enable their social integration, expand higher education offers and increase access to public institutions, information, products and services.

The programme will strengthen social integration services and improve their quality. These investments will promote the development of the social economy and foster the social and professional integration of migrants.

The European Funds for Social Development also offer financial instruments to business start-ups and social enterprises. Thanks to the programme, health services will be improved through coordination of disease-prevention programmes, deinstitutionalisation of medical care and through the provision of psychiatric care for children and long-term care for people with dementia.

Special attention will be directed to building the capacity of social partners. The programme will support training and networking activities, strengthen social dialogue on the European Green Deal and the involvement of social partners in the policy and law-making process. Support will be provided for activities undertaken by the social partners related to gender balance and equality at work, health and safety at work, healthy ageing of workers and accessibility.

The programme will also support civil society organisations to increase their participation in the law-making process, including through the co-creation, monitoring and evaluation of public policies to improve accessibility and inclusion for people with special needs.
