programme_description: The programme’s ambition for Silesia is to facilitate its just transition, making the region’s economy modern and competitive. This objective will allow citizens to enjoy better quality of life in a clean environment rich with development opportunities. With resources allocated from both the European Regional Development fund and the Just Transition Fund, the programme constitutes the largest allocation among all EU regional programmes and defines 13 key areas of intervention to deliver on its ambition.

Interventions will increase business activity in research, development, and innovation. The programme plans to support investments in research infrastructure and research implementation. The public sector will benefit from the process of digitisation, which, along with internationalisation will assist small businesses and entrepreneurship.

In line with environmental goals, the programme will support actions protecting biodiversity, furthering buildings energy efficiency and investments in renewable energy sources. EU funds will support multimodal transport infrastructure that contribute to the decarbonisation of urban mobility. Investments will contribute to improving safety on local and regional roads while boosting the accessibility and attractiveness of sustainable public transport. Outside urban centres, support will go to the development of zero-emission public rail transport of regional range.

The programme will invest also in inclusive education, vocational education and higher education, social and health services, as well as sustainable tourism and culture. Measures will seek to stabilise the regional labor market, reducing the effects of the economic slowdown that followed the COVID-19 pandemic and the effects of the Russian aggression on Ukraine. The focus will be on bespoke measures to strengthen skills and competences matching the demand of a labour market increasingly driven transformed by the transition to greener and more digital ways of production. To match such a demand, the programme will encourage smart specialisations in the regions while workers will receive assistance adapting to market transformations.

Moreover, the programme encapsulates a dedicated support for the LGBT community. Funding will prioritise initiatives supporting housing for homeless LGBT people as well as teacher training. Silesia increased their social spending in JTF from 7% to 16%, mainstreaming its gender component and devoting a large allocation for skills development. Gender equality increased from EUR 1 million to EUR 15 million.

Under just transition measures, the programme’s support will be allocated to the development of centres supporting the creation and transfer of knowledge and technology for a green, smart, digital economy.

With the goal of preventing energy poverty, funding will go to the installation of ecological and affordable energy sources, increasing energy savings in public buildings and in the housing sector. To mitigate the effects of industrial activity on the environment, EU funds will support recultivation, regeneration, and restoration of post-industrial areas, with an eye to the removal of the risk of improperly stored waste. EU support will also play a role in the repurposing disaffected industrial areas. Funding will support the decontamination of water polluted by mining, along with support to improve water management.
Sustainable urban development is programmed using i.e., Integrated Territorial Instruments and will consume approx. 25,75% of the ERDF and 16,07% JTF.

The region took an ambitious approach towards the wider use of financial instruments. This concerns specially entrepreneurship, revitalisation, energy efficiency and renewable energy sources. 12,34% of the ERDF allocation of the programme is dedicated to financial instruments.

programme_description: The main objectives of the programme are:

The programme will increase business activity in research and development. This will entail implementation and innovation through support for R&D infrastructure as well as the creation of regional and supra-regional research agendas. Coherently with the regional smart specialisation strategy, skills development and digitalisation will contribute to the process for public sector and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

In the area of environment and climate the programme will continue actions in the field of water and wastewater management and biodiversity protection. A key feature of for cliamte change adaptation projects will be the development of environmental forecasting and warning systems. In the same line, urban areas will benefit from advisory systems to achieve climate neutrality. The programme also includes measures to encourage the uptake of renewable energy sources, with interventions to advise public entities, enterprises and citizens.

Regarding mobility, the programme aims to ease access to urban public transport and better the standards of the road and rail network. Such measures will match efforts to to improve road safety, including for pedestrians and bikers, while investments will support building insfrastructure for charging/refuelling zero-emission vehicles.

A part of investments will promote inclusive education - kindergartens and vocational education and training, deinsitutionalised ocial and primary healthcare -, as well as sustainable tourism and culture.

The socio-professional activation for members of marginalised communities such as refugees and migrants benefits from financing, namely for tools such as bespoke language courses, internships, vocational trainings, etc. Other measures targeting marginalised communities include actions supporting the LGBT+ community. Youth employment represents a key priority: Wielkopolska is to receive one of the most significant allocations for the Youth Guarantee and the ALMA initiative in Poland. A substantial allocation for gender equality and women's economic activation aims at mitigating the gender employment gap and increasing women's chances in the labour market.
The programme will target areas facing adaptation and restructuring difficulties at regional and supra-local level.

The Territorial Just Transition Plan will cover the Konin subregion. The JTF will assist companies withdrawing from traditional industries by means of a comprehensive support for businesses, adressing infrastructure and complementary training. Projects are planned to create new businesses, support self-employment and create new jobs in industries that emphasise the endogenous potential of transition areas.

JTF supports workers employed in the mining and energy sectors and related industries, workers who are at risk of being made redundant. Support materialises in the means to retrain or endeavour on entrepreneurial pathways to stay in employment (e.g. career counselling, legal and psychological assistance, gosp. start-up grants). Investments will drive the development of vocational training, to better match the provision of education to the needs of the local labour market, strengthening cooperation with employers and adapting to the challenges posed by the digital and green transition.

To support the transition to the circular economy, the programme fosters resources and material-efficient production and logistics processes, increases in product repurposing, upcycling, material recycling and resource efficiency. Investments also aim to reduce energy consumption in production processes as well as water, heat and cold. In order to preserve and restore former functions of natural and landscape assets of brownfield sites, including post-mining areas, the scope of the intervention will include their rehabilitation, remediation, restoration and decontamination. Important aspects of the intervention are the growth of water resources in the sub-region and climate change resilience through the development of micro and small water retention, including the development of aquatic ecosystems, investments in water facilities and hydro-technological infrastructure.

Investments related to ensuring access to stable, green and affordable energy sources will be supported as well as to investments that raise energy standards in public buildings and housing. Electro-mobility measures will be promoted by purchase of zero-emission rolling stock, charging infrastructure, integration of collective transport and cycling routes.

The programme presents an ambitious approach towards the wider use of financial instruments. In particular, in the area of enterpreurship, revitalisation, energy efficiency and renewable energy sources. 11% of the programme allocation is dedicated to financial instruments.

programme_description: The European Funds for Łódzkie 2021-2027 programme (FEŁ2027) pursues five Cohesion Policy Objectives financed by the ERDF, the ESF+ and the JTF. The programme encompasses 9 priorities, and 3 technical assistance priorities. The main aim of the programme is strengthening and making effective use of the region's economic and social potentials. In fact, it will support the region's energy transformation and foster entrepreneurial attitudes, namely towards the sustainable and smart development of Łódzkie that brings about higher quality of life and better professional development for its citizens.
On this basis, the programme FEŁ2027 will focus on the priorities of the European Green Deal, like the digital transition, strengthening the EU economy, securing jobs and reducing inequalities.

According to the 2021 Regional Innovation Scoreboard, Łódzkie remains in the group of the “emerging innovators +”. Therefore, actions are planned to strengthen research and innovation activities and the uptake of advanced technologies. Actions will also encourage the mainstreaming of research and development projects and investments in innovation for SMEs. The funds will also target the digitalization of the activities of public institutions with the development of public e-services together with the overall digital transformation of the regional economy.

In the area of environment and climate, investments will go to improving air quality and energy efficiency in the Łódzkie region. Infrastructure will equally be fitted to increasily use renewable energy sources, while the region will benefit from measures aimed at adapting to climate change. The percentage of expenditure devoted to the protection of biodiversity amounts to 5,3% of the Programme allocation

Concerning mobility, investments will improve road safety and transport accessibility in the Łódzkie Voivodeship, with a major focus on rail infrastructure, and support to public transport between cities and in rural areas.

The programme FEŁ2027 will invest also in inclusive education, vocational education and training, de-institutionalized social and health services (mainly aimed at primary health care and outpatient care) as well as in sustainable tourism and culture.

The measures financed by the ESF + will focus on adapting the workforce to the rapidly changing regional labour market and on including people who are currently unemployed or inactive. Actions will also help providing young people with relevant their qualifications and professional experience.

The programme also envisages the use of the Just Transition Fund for activities related to the restructuring of the Bełchatów Power Plant and the affiliated lignite mine. Such actions lead to ambitious goals of climate neutrality of the whole region while providing options to mitigate the socio-economic impact of the transition on its citizens.

One of the priorities for support in this regard will be the development of entrepreneurship, in particular SMEs. Another will be to provide a modern education and training offer that responds to the needs of the economy in transition. Measures are also planned to improve access to public services, to increase the use of renewable energy sources and to reduce environmental pollution while developing green infrastructure in degraded areas and ensuring accessible local transport.

programme_description: The Pomorskie voivodeship has an attractive, coastal location at the crossroads of international transport routes. This provides the basis for the development of many activities related to maritime transport, logistics and wind energy, notwithstanding the many activities based on advanced technologies, ICT or systems of increased autonomy based on 4.0 industry.

In terms of size and strength, Pomorskie is an average economy in Poland. It has a relatively stable position in relation to other Polish regions, maintaining the 7th place in terms of share in national GDP and 6th place in terms of GDP per capita. The Pomeranian economy is service-oriented with tourism playing an important role. At the same time the maritime, petrochemical, wood and furniture, construction, electromechanical and hotel industries maintain a preminent role.

The programme aims at strengthening the region's economy while supporting the aspirations of the Pomeranian Voivodeship to achieve the leading position among Polish regions. Those ambitions require more effective use of its competitive advantages: geographical location at the crossroads of transport routes, diversified structure of the economy and a relatively favorable demographic situation to foster integrated, sustainable and intelligent development. To obtain such development objectives, the programme entails interventions in line with 7 priorities and two technical assistance priority axes (ERDF and ESF+).

The programme encompasses measures to strengthen productivity, innovation (including the implementation of R&D results) and the adaptability of enterprises. This will entail increasing their expansion and international visibility, encouraging their cooperation with research institutions and the public sector. Such synergies would place the region on the way towards technological leadership and the implementation of modern solutions. Support will also cover the digitalisation and cybersecurity in public sector.

In the area of environment and climate the region plans to enhance energy security, transforming the region into a national leader in green energy production and eco-efficient technologies, while preserving landscape assets. To enhance environmental security, measures include enhancing preparedness for extreme events through adaptation to climate change. With the objective of achieving climate neutreality, the region committed to reducing emissions and to supporting committing to climate neutrality through emission reduction and through support to circular economy.
On mobility, the programme will fund measures increasing the cohesion of regional internal transportation according to the following areas of intervention.

Furthermore, the programme plans to increase access to high-quality pre-school education while supporting vocational training for the key sectors of the region’s economy. The support will be also dedicated to deinsitutionalised social and health services (mainly targeted at primary healthcare and ambulatory care), as well as sustainable tourism and culture.

Measures financed from the ESF+ will support education at every level, taking into account not only the improvement of students’ knowledge but also the development of their competences. An important aspect of support will be inclusive education aimed at supporting children with disabilities, behavioural and emotional disorders, learning difficulties and students with a migran background (including repatriates). Pomorze has chosen to activate young people in the labour market through the ALMA initiative, helping not only to find better employment but also to enrich the workforce with new competences. To ensure equal opportunities for women, measures will focus on tackling discrimination in the labour market and overcoming gender stereotypes, not only through direct support for the labour market activation of parents, but also through dedicated support for workers and employers. An amount of EUR 75 million from ESF+ has been earmarked for the implementation of the European Child Guarantee and EUR 18 million for the European Youth Guarantee. For skills, the programme dedicates around EUR 91 mln.
Finally, interventions for the regeneration of deprived areas in cities will be comprehensive and place-based for the benefit of local communities and linked to existing local social policies.
The programme contributes to the key EU priorities in the area of green growth, digitalisation, innovation, economic transformation and to the mainstreaming of New European Bauhaus principles.

programme_description: The Podkarpackie Voivodeship is situated in South-Eastern Poland at the border with Ukraine. The region's economy made grat progress in the last 20 years. However, the voivodeship has still the third lowest GDP per capita in Poland and is affected by negative demographic trends. The programme's goal is to strengthen the region's economic potential, by fostering the integrated and sustainable development of the Podkarpackie region. To deliver security and high quality life to the region's citizens, EU funded interventions will answer to the eight priorities of the European Funds for Podkaprackie programme.

Measures will stimulate innovation in the region by further tightening cooperation between business and science. Moreover, small businesses will receive support to create new products and technologies and, along with the public sector, will benefit from digitalisation and the development of skills that align with regional smart specialisations.

Under the priority relating to environment the, region plans to continue actions in the field of water and wastewater management as well as biodiversity protection (6,38% of the total EU funds allocation). Podkapracie plans to develop climate change adaptation projects, supporting advisory systems to foster climate neutrality. To increase energy efficiency, measures will include the refurbishment and isolation of buildings and investing in renewable energy sources.

To improve sustainable mobility, the region needs to make urban public transport more accessible and improve the standard of the road and rail network. The region equally plans investments to improve road safety and the transport system's resilience to climate change.

To improve services to the public the programme will support kindergartens, deinstitutionalised social and health services (mainly targeted at primary healthcare and ambulatory care). To increase opportunities for the workforce, the programme will invest in vocational education to increase and diversify the schools’ offer to match the market's demand. The programme will also promote sustainable tourism and culture.

Measures financed from the ESF+ will focus on activating people currently excluded from the labour market. By investing in skills development, improving employees' health and championing work flexibility, the programme commits to adapting the workforce to a rapidly changing labour market.

Preschools, especially in rural areas, will open more places to accomodate a greater number of pupils. Programmed activities will aim at increasing access to education for students with disabilities in mainstream schools by providing relevant trainings to teachers and hiring students’ assistants. Measures in the field of social policy will focus on providing tailored support to marginalised people and communities, people without homes, struggling families and youth leaving foster care.

From the ESF+, approximately EUR  98 millions will go to the implementation of the European Child Guarantee, with EUR 88 million more earmarked for the European Youth Guarantee. The ESF+ also contributes EUR 10 million to the programme for the promotion of gender equality. The ESF+ amount for skills development will amount to around EUR 38 million.

Finally, the support is also planned for areas facing adaptation and restructuring difficulties at local and regional level through the Integrated Territorial Instruments and Community-Led Local Development.

The programme will also contribute to the implementation of the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region. It will focus in particular on the area of innovation, cooperation between enterprises and research organisations as well as on energy, climate change adaptation andr transport. As Podkarpackie is a border region with Ukraine and Slovakia, activities will be implemented in synergy with the planned Interreg programme Poland-Ukraine 2021-2027, Poland-Slovakia 2021-2027 and Interreg Central Europe 2021-2027.

programme_description: The Opolskie regional Programme will provide support to several areas:

In the area of innovation, investments will aim at increasing the competitiveness and innovativeness of enterprises. Specifically, the programme will continue investments in digitization, along with support for commercialisation processes and support to increase the level of internationalisation of economic and scientific activity.

The European Regional Development Fund will invest in low-carbon economy, air protection and energy efficiency. To prevent environmental threats, EU funds will cover adaptation to climate change. Other investments will aim at reducing the waste of water and the development of blue and green infrastructure.
With the goal of transitioning smoothly to a circular economy, support will go to making the municipal waste systems more effective,  combined to campaigns to raise environmental awareness.

Consistently with the goal of preserving the natural environment, the purchase of low/zero-emission rolling stock, along with the development of the necessary infrastructure, will contribute to the development of more sustainable means of transport.

To address social challenges, both the European Regional Development Fund and the European Social Fund+ will invest in education. The goal will be to increase access to pre-school education, equalise educational opportunities for students from disadvantaged families and increase participation in lifelong learning.

Projects will increase access to employment, reduce social exclusion and poverty, improve access to social services and reduce the number of children placed in institutional forms of care. An important element of support will be improving access to healthcare services, mainly by investments in primary and ambulatory care, deinstitutionalisation of long-term care and increasing the numbers of medical staff.

Finally, the Programme will contribute to revitalisation of urban centers, enabling them to create sustainable development, growth and employment (for instance by revitalisation of the degraded areas and by counteracting the negative phenomena of suburbanisation) and by creating conditions for partnership management of development.

programme_description: The mission of ESPON is to deliver evidence, data and advice.  Given the main territorial challenges at stake and the EU policy framework, ESPON intends to support policy makers at all levels by providing territorial evidence and knowledge to inform policy responses to strengthen EU territories’ resilience and recovery of from crises by achieving a green transition to climate-neutral economies while ensuring just living conditions in all places.
With a total budget of EUR 60 Million , (EUR 48 Million EU funding) , the Programme will cover all 27 EU Member States in partnership with Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

ESPON research and activities are highly relevant for cohesion policy programming and implementation, and as part of the interregional programmes family it particularly contributes to cohesion policy effectiveness. In addition, key areas supported through research and evidence include  the European Green Deal, Just Transition and Recovery, the Territorial Agenda 2030 (TA2030) process and implementation.

ESPON supports these processes through policy briefs, territorial evidence reports, territorial monitoring tools and other dedicated studies and outreach events, both arranged on demand of respective ESPON member countries, European cooperation partners, and the relevant intergovernmental networks. ESPON also supports macro-regional strategies, sea-basin strategies, as done in the past, with data and monitoring tools and responding to ad-hoc support requests.

The Urbact IV programme focuses on supporting cities in implementing solutions to tackle the green, just and digital transitions in particular, through collaboration, capacity building and expertise. The purpose is to promote integrated sustainable development in cities, improve city’s policies and improve the effectiveness of Cohesion policy in cities.

Its supports the delivery of key principles of sustainable urban development on the ground, such as good governance, integrated and place-based approaches, all making the link to the urban and territorial dimension of Cohesion policy and to its minimum requirements as per the 2021-2027 regulatory provisions.

The Programme will cover the EU 27 Member States, Norway, Switzerland as well as some countries benefitting from the Instrument for Pre-Accession (IPA) such as Albania, Montenegro, Serbia, Republic of North Macedonia, and Bosnia-Herzegovina.The URBACT programme covers the entire territory of the participating countries and is open to cities of all sizes. It will pay particular attention to cities benefitting from Cohesion policy in order to support them by increasing cooperation with other cities to find solutions, by supporting them with dedicated tools and expertise to improve their capacity to develop and implement integrated strategies and plans, to transfer innovative solutions and practices, to share and build knowledge and to find funding for planned investments and projects.

Since 2004, the EU strategy for the Outermost regions (OR) identified the intensification of cooperation with neighbouring countries as one of its key pillars.

For this reason, in recent decades, the Programme emerged as the main instrument for promoting the regional integration of the ORs into their geographical areas of reference. This highlights the importance of regional cooperation and good neighbourly relations, namely through cooperation with seven African countries in the Macaronesia and Guinea Gulf.

The programme promotes the ecological transition, supporting the development of a green and blue economy, fighting climate change through risk prevention and disaster management in its cooperation projects with neighboring African countries.
The improvement of competitiveness through innovative and smart economic transformation represents another priority of the programme.
Improving migration management at origin and destination is the last priority of the programme.

Finally, the MAC Programme is complementary to the new EU's "Global Europe" - Neighborhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument (NDICI). As stated in the Interreg regulation, it is possible to include a specific financial allocation to help partner countries and regions in strengthening their cooperation with the outermost regions in their neighborhood.

The programme aims to support projects for citizens of rural areas facing demographic challenges like ageing and depopulation. These two phenomena create imbalances along the urban/rural areas divide as well as on the littoral/interior divide, as citizens move away from the countryside and coasts to concentrate in large urban areas.

Rural areas are particularly affected by the struggle to find skilled labour force while providing quality of life and basic services, like internet access, transport and healthcare. The programme aims to experiment with joint solutions to favour social or local innovation. Areas of interventions will likely be social economy, silver economy
development based on local resources or collaborative governance between the countries of the region.

Another of the programme's main objectives is the promotion of cooperation projects attempting to mitigate the consequences of climate change. Among the most alarming consequences of climate change are the increased intensity and frequency of certain natural hazards (drought, fires, rainfalls) affecting both the environment and economic activities.

The programme area of South West Europe has strengths allowing for actions that draw from its own resources and ecosystems: extensive forest mass, connectivity of Natura 2000 network sites, high number of protected natural areas and habitats, good relative groundwater and surface water quality, previous experience in the efficient use of water resources, but also knowledge centres experienced in analyzing and finding solutions tailored to each territory. These strengths need to be combined through the INTERREG projects to respond to territorial needs.
The Atlantic Area programme cooperation space is eminently a maritime territory. This characteristic, jointly with the coast-hinterland relationships, heavily influences the Programme's conception.

For that reason, blue and green projects are crucial to this programme. Through it, the EU promotes blue innovation and competitiveness in the Atlantic Area regions. Ultimately, this approach will foster the protection and preservation of maritime and costal ecosystems. From a greener perspective, the programme aims to encourage resilience to climate change, to reduce pollution and CO2 emissions, to transit towards greener solutions, such as renewable energy and circular economy.

The cooperation area is located within the Atlantic sea-basin strategy, hence, to achieve better results and a significant impact on the blue investments, the Programme should seek synergies with the sea-basin strategy.

Blue Careers, as well as skilling -or reskilling- schemes for people in the blue economy sector will contribute to a more effective and inclusive labour market. Regarding social inclusion, data shows that the access to health care in this cooperation functional area needs to be improved through an Interreg programme, considering the difficulty to finance large investment projects.

The programme pays attention to the importance of cultural heritage and the tourism sector, key economic assets for coastal areas, but also for nearby inland areas, particularly in the French, Spanish and Portuguese regions.

Finally, the programme will focus its attention on governance, a policy objective seeking to ensure a constant flow of information between the Managing authority and Member States. Such close cooperation fits the goal of an optimal implementation of the Atlantic Area Programme.

programme_name: (Interreg VI-B) NEXT Mediterranean Sea Basin (NEXT MED)
programme_description: The programme fosters fair and sustainable cooperation between 7 EU Member States and 8 partner countries in the Southern Neighbourhood (i.e. Algeria, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, Tunisia and Türkiye). The participating countries jointly developed the programme based on the principle of equal footing. There is a strong and shared understanding that many of today’s challenges in the Mediterranean Sea Basin are common across the countries in the region and that there is an urgent need to find common solutions.

The largest part of EU funding (42%) will be allocated to projects that address climate change and environmental challenges. these include energy efficiency measures, sustainable water use, climate change adaptation, circular economy as well as risk prevention.

Secondly, the programme aims to create a more competitive and smarter Mediterranean by providing support and improving conditions for SMEs. Such actions should pave the way for greater internationalisation, transnational research-business cooperation as well as reducing disparities and gaps in research and innovation across the Mediterranean.

The third aim is to foster a more social and inclusive Mediterranean by providing better quality and access to education and training. This will concern young people and disadvantaged groups in particular. Health represents a key factor in the reduction of economic and social inequalities. Therefore, project partners will focus on developing innovative digital and services that improve the delivery and efficiency of health services.

Finally, the programme aims to improve the cooperation governance across the Mediterranean through a number of tools, including joint capacity building actions for public authorities as well as transnational cooperation between citizens, civil society actors and public institutions based on bottom-up and participatory approaches.
The programme has a particular focus on young people and it will ensure a strong system of complementarities and synergies with other EU funding streams operating in the Mediterranean.

The programme aims to mitigate the consequences of climate change in the Mediterranean sea and its negative effects on all the territories bordering the basin and far beyond. The necessary challenge of the Green deal will also be accompanied by an effort of supervision, coordination, technical and political cooperation that will span the entire the Mediterranean basin.
Moreover, the programme aims to reinforce the potential for innovation that, with the exception of capitals and main cities, remains low across the region.

To reach these objectives, the programme has a strong climate and environment orientation. It contributes to the EU climate targets with 35% of the programme allocation and to environmental objectives - with 66% of its resources. More than 10% of the budget is devoted to tackling biodiversity issues.

The programme also plays an important role in the implementation of the Western Maritime Initiative as it shares parts of its cooperation area with the West Mediterranean area. It will allow involvement of partners beyond the programme area, thus creating links and activating synergies within and across the sea basin regions.

Finally, with the exception of Serbia, the programme area also covers the area of the Adriatic and Ionian Macro regional strategy (EUSAIR). Other Interreg programmes concerning the Adriatic Sea are expected to contribute to the Programme for the priorities related to the EUSAIR. Thus, the programme entails coordination and cooperation mechanisms to interact with other interreg programmes active in the MED area, capitalising on project outputs and results and increasing their territorial impact.

The programme is the largest cross-border cooperation programme in the European Union. It aims at reaching a smarter, greener, more competitive and more inclusive cross-border area. Through the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF), the EU will support border regions between Spain and Portugal in tackling common challenges. Investments are targeted in line with seven priorities.
The programme will provide funding to projects in many cooperation areas, such as:
The programme will contribute respectively to the climate objectives with 30% of allocated budget and to biodiversity with 13,4% of its total budget.

The programme will develop five territorial strategies linked to the specific necessities of five programme sub-areas, promoting an approach adapted to the territory. The strategies will be developed under different themes.
The programme area falls within the geographical scope of the Atlantic Strategy and contributes to its implementation mainly by focusing on cooperation for the green and blue economy.

Since joining the European Union, Małopolska has experienced significant economic growth, with its GDP per capita rising from 46% of the EU average in 2004 to 69% in 2020. The region boasts a high employment rate and lower-than-average rates of youth not in employment, education, or training (NEET), as well as at risk of poverty and social exclusion (AROPE). However, one pressing issue is the high gender employment gap in the region, necessitating measures to ensure equal opportunities for women in the labor market. Małopolska faces demographic challenges, with a growing population of post-working age individuals, highlighting the importance of adaptability and active aging programs.

The primary aim of the program is to strengthen and leverage the region's economic and social potential for integrated, sustainable, and intelligent development. This includes ensuring a high quality of life and security for its residents and addressing the just transition in the Western Małopolska subregion. The program outlines 11 priorities across 5 Policy Objectives, aligning with the EU legislative package and the Just Transition Fund.

Under Policy Objective 1 (PO1), efforts are directed toward boosting research and development, innovation, and digitalization in the public sector and SMEs, along with skills development. Policy Objective 2 (PO2) focuses on environmental and climate initiatives, including water management, biodiversity protection, and renewable energy adoption. Policy Objective 3 (PO3) aims to enhance mobility by improving public transport, road safety, and infrastructure for zero-emission vehicles.

Policy Objective 4 (PO4) targets inclusive education, childcare, vocational training, and social and health services. It also emphasizes support for women in the labor market, gender equality, and work-life balance. The program is committed to promoting inclusive education for individuals with disabilities, enhancing language competences, and leveraging cultural and training infrastructure. Additionally, support will be provided to migrants and the Roma minority.

The program allocates significant funds to various initiatives, including the European Youth Guarantee, gender equality, and skills development. It also addresses adaptation and restructuring difficulties in certain areas and supports the transition to a green, smart, and digital economy, with a focus on energy efficiency, renewable energy, and environmental remediation. Sustainable urban development and financial instruments are key components, contributing to EU priorities like green growth, digitalization, and innovation.

The program identifies eight projects of strategic importance, including the expansion of a regional cycling network, knowledge transfer centers for innovation, and a Telecare Centre for dependent residents. However, Poland acknowledges shortcomings in fulfilling certain enabling conditions related to fundamental rights, transport planning, social inclusion, and healthcare policy frameworks.

programme_name: Thematic Programme for Climate Action and Sustainability
programme_description: Portugal is particularly exposed to climate change, therefore the country committed to transitioning to a carbon-neutral economy by 2050. Portugal’s transport system can make a significant contribution to achieving this goal. The national Thematic Programme for Climate Action and Sustainability (PACS) will invest 87% of its allocation in this sector.

PACS will invest in major cities’ environmentally friendly urban public transport, namely in infrastructure and in clean rolling stock. Outside major cities, PACS will support the modernisation and electrification of the national rail network and increase rail capacity in the areas where demand is greatest. It will also expand the maritime and port capacity, enhancing the resilience of the infrastructure, supporting the energy transition of the port sector and inter-modality for passengers and freight. In the Azores, it will focus on both port and airport infrastructure.

Moreover, PACS will contribute to tackling energy challenges, by strengthening and modernising infrastructure, promoting storage and supporting a better management and increased digitalisation of energy networks.

Additionally, PACS envisages to invest in the protection of the shoreline, including by rebalancing sand and sediment dynamics, constructing and rehabilitating shoreline defence structures or stabilising cliffs.

Lastly, it will support investments to help change collective behaviour leading to a higher circularity of resources (circular economy), through national communication campaigns, raising awareness and informing the general population. It will also support studies and the development of a monitoring system for the municipal waste sector.

The main objectives of the Mazowieckie regional programme are:

With the goal of increasing research and development activities for business, while incentivising innovation implementation, the programme supports the uptake of research results for commercial use. Moreover, the programme also aims at driving the digitalization of both the public sector and SMEs, alongside the development of skills, in accordance with smart specialisations.

The programme also fosters climate change adaptation measures, and it will continue its previous initiatives in the field of energy efficiency. To this end, the programme invests in actions to reduce energy poverty and greenhouse gas emissions. Such actions include the installation of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) equipment and related infrastructure; the replacement and modernisation of heat sources or the connection to heating/cooling networks.

To ensure water security, the programme will invest in the development of all forms of retention, construction and modernisation of water and sewage networks. Such actions will accompany an overall transition to models of circular economy.

Regarding mobility, Mazowieckie plans investments to improve road safety (including the construction of bypasses of cities and municipalities). Furthermore, investments will cover initiatives to increase road safety, especially for cyclists and pedestrians, while the purchase of new low- and zero-emission rolling stock will make public transportation more efficient and attractive. The programme will also sustain the construction of charging points and refuelling stations for electric and hydrogen vehicles.
The programme will invest in improving the efficiency and resilience of the healthcare system, in the field of prevention, as well as long-term and hospice care.

It will be possible to obtain support for the development of social services for people in need of support, assistance services for people with disabilities, creation of protected and assisted housing, support for the process of deinstitutionalization of foster care and support for the elderly.

programme_description: The support under the Lubuskie regional Programme will focus around such priorities as: innovation, entrepreneurship, digitalization, low-emission and environmentally friendly transport, protection of environment and energy efficiency.
The social key areas for investments are labour market, employment, lifelong learning, health care, social integration and the territorial dimension.

Investments will strengthen innovation and R&D and increase the commercialisation of research. They will lead to further digitalisaton, both in the area of public services and in entrepreneurship. EU funds will also help increasing the uptake of modern technologies in the healthcare system.

It is planned to modernize public buildings in terms of better energy efficiency and increase the additional renewable energy generation capacity. Investments will lead to transition towards a circular and resource-efficient economy.

The development of public transport infrastructure, including with the purchase of low- and zero-emission rolling stock, will increase the availability of sustainable public transport. The promotion of its use will contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution.

The European Regional Development Fund together with the European Social Fund+ will invest in pre-school education and in education and training of adults. Investments will help increasing the number of people using care services in their local community, rather than institutions. Social housing solutions will continue to receive support while in healthcare, investments will focus on primary and ambulatory care and will include mental healthcare. Sustainable tourism and culture will benefit from the develpment of new infrastrucure, while the development of thematic tourist routes and other products is ongoing, with the goal of preserving and cultural heritage and modernising sites to bring about greater  social inclusion.
Finally, it is planned to support projects targeting specific urban and rural territories resulting from the integrated territorial development strategies.

programme_description: The programme aims to make effective use of the region’s economic and social potential, and foster integrated, sustainable, and intelligent development of the Lubelskie voivodeship to ensure a high quality of life and security for its inhabitants.

Measures included in the European Funds for Lubelskie 2021-2027 programme are intended to increase research and development (R&D) by businesses, support R&D infrastructure, create and implement regional and supra-regional research agendas, promote digitalisation in the public sector and SMEs, and skills development.

In the area of environment and climate, the region plans to continue projects that improve water and wastewater management and protect biodiversity. Other projects will focus on environmental forecasting and warning systems, urban climate change adaptation, and advisory systems to foster climate neutrality. Conventional energy sources will be replaced with renewable solutions, mainly solar, and public entities, enterprises, and citizens will get access to advice on this topic.
The region plans investments to improve road safety and increase the safety of cyclists and pedestrians, in addition to building charging/refuelling infrastructure for zero-emission vehicles.

The programme foresees infrastructural investments in inclusive education, kindergartens and vocational education and training, de-institutionalised social and health services (mainly primary healthcare and ambulatory care), as well as sustainable tourism and culture.  Measures to help the unemployed and the workforce adapt to a rapidly changing labour market will include investments in skills development, in more flexible forms of work, and in improving employee health.

New preschool places will be created, particularly in rural areas. Greater access to mainstream schools for children with disabilities will be achieved by training teachers, hiring classroom assistants and improving the quality of vocational education and training. Social policy measures will focus on providing tailored support to marginalised people and communities, homeless people, low-income families, and young people leaving foster care.

As part of an ambitious approach to the use of financial instruments, the region plans to launch a pilot for two instruments that support culture and revitalisation. Financial instruments dedicated solely to not-for-profit activities in health, transport and the labour market are intended to ensure that public funds have greater impact.
The programme contributes to the EU priorities of green growth, digitalisation, innovation, economic transformation, and mainstreaming of the New European Bauhaus principles.

programme_description: The programme is the biggest national infrastructural programme supported by the ERDF and the Cohesion Fund in the EU. It focuses on the challenges of the European Green Deal by co-financing investments that contribute to transition of Poland to a green economy. This transition encompasses sectors like energy, transport, environment, health and culture sectors.
The programme will play a crucial role for Poland on its way towards decarbonisation of the energy sector through investments in energy efficiency. Investments will cover:

The programme will also aim to make clean public transport more accessible and more convenient to use for all citizens. Additionally, it will continue to finance the road modernisation in order to complete the Polish network of high-speed roads.

The programme will also help the Polish cities to adapt to extreme weather events caused by climate change and to protect urban areas from risk of flooding and drought. Also, the funds will remain available for addressing challenges such as pollution by urban wastewater and access to clean drinking water. Furthermore, it will support the protection of the natural environment and contribute to the decontamination of abandoned lots that pose environmental and health risks. The programme will also boost transition of Polish enterprises into circular economy and lighten the environmental footprint of products and technological processes.

The programme will take up the challenge of transforming the Polish health sector through investments in primary and ambulatory care, as well as through the implementation of the mental healthcare reform. Both are necessary to improve the functioning of the Polish healthcare system.

Cultural infrastructure and protection of cultural heritage will also be strengthened to make the sector more sustainable, inclusive, environmentally-friendly, digitalized and overall more resilient to crisis such as COVID.

programme_description: The European Funds for Digital Growth 2021-2027, shortned in its polish acronym FERC, is a successor of the Operational Programme for Digital Poland 2014-2020. It is the biggest European programme dedicated exclusively to the development of information and communication technology supported by ERDF.

The programme contributes to the implementation of the objectives set by the European Gigabit Society, as well as Europe’s Digital Decade targets. Its main goal is to support Poland in reaching the average EU level of digitalisation and it will implement its action in line with the three following priorities.

Priority 1 is dedicated to the rollout of the ultra-fast broadband in the non-viable areas. To promote equal access to the Internet a connection wiht a 100Mbps theshold will be provided to households and enterprises situated in sparsely populated areas. At the same time, EU funds will contribute to providing gigabit internet access in places constituting the main driving force of socio-economic development.

Priority 2 focuses on delivering high quality, user-centric digital public services for citizens and businesses. Digitalisation projects will expand the scope of matters that can be done entirely online and will increase the resilience of IT systems by reinforcing cybersecurity standards. The re-use of existing documents held by public sector bodies will promote the use of open data and stimulate innovation in products and services.

Priority 3 represents the provision of technical assistance and support to the programme’s management and control system. Beneficiaries, potential beneficiaries and partners will benefit from assitance, information and help with the promotion of the programme.

This programme is the main tool to implement the Administrative Capacity roadmap in Portugal. It will finance key actions to develop the institutional capacity that is necessary to define, monitor and evaluate public policies. The programme includes one priority covering coordination, management, monitoring and audit of all Portuguese funding programmes for 2021-2027.

The biggest part of the investments (88% of the total allocation) will support preparation, implementation, monitoring and control. Therefore, reinforcing the capacity of the Member State’s authorities, beneficiaries and relevant partners.

The programme aims to boost investments in key sectors for the benefit of the people and businesses in the region. It will be integral to root the region in the effort to make all of Europe more competitive, greener, more inclusive, and closer to its citizens’ needs.

Through the programme, the EU will support measures to strengthen the research and innovation capacity of the region, such as the uptake of advanced technologies in companies. Small and medium-size enterprises will receive assistance in their efforts to become more innovative create quality jobs, while strengthening their competitiveness on global markets.
In addition, the region’s green transition will receive support for the decarbonisation of local administration and the promotion of climate-neutral buildings.

Consistently with climate change preparedness, the programme promotes circular economy models along with sustainable and responsible consumption patterns. Such measures include waste prevention and the preservation of biodiversity by favouring nature-based solutions.

The programme also seeks to enhance social cohesion and employment in the region. To this end, modernising health care and increasing access to services will be instrumental, as will be supporting all levels of education. Additionally, EU support to lifelong learning, employment and entrepreneurship will help enterprises rise to the challenges of the green transition and provide workers with the skills that match labour market demands.

Finally, the programme supports models of sustainable urban development that is closer to the citizens’ needs. Integrated strategies developed by local authorities, focused on increasing competitiveness of cities by urban regeneration, decarbonisation and reducing climate vulnerability, reducing early school leaving, and promoting social inclusion.

programme_description: The mission of ESPON is to deliver evidence, data and advice.  Given the main territorial challenges at stake and the EU policy framework, ESPON intends to support policy makers at all levels by providing territorial evidence and knowledge to inform policy responses to strengthen EU territories’ resilience and recovery of from crises by achieving a green transition to climate-neutral economies while ensuring just living conditions in all places.
With a total budget of EUR 60 Million , (EUR 48 Million EU funding) , the Programme will cover all 27 EU Member States in partnership with Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

ESPON research and activities are highly relevant for cohesion policy programming and implementation, and as part of the interregional programmes family it particularly contributes to cohesion policy effectiveness. In addition, key areas supported through research and evidence include  the European Green Deal, Just Transition and Recovery, the Territorial Agenda 2030 (TA2030) process and implementation.

ESPON supports these processes through policy briefs, territorial evidence reports, territorial monitoring tools and other dedicated studies and outreach events, both arranged on demand of respective ESPON member countries, European cooperation partners, and the relevant intergovernmental networks. ESPON also supports macro-regional strategies, sea-basin strategies, as done in the past, with data and monitoring tools and responding to ad-hoc support requests.
The research activities that the ESPON will carry out in the 2021 – 2030 period will be aligned within integrated
, which are closely linked to the overall strategic goals of the EU Cohesion Policy 2021-2027 objectives and to the Territorial Agenda 2030 priorities:

The programme Azores will prioritise socio-economic convergence and demographic sustainability. It will do so by addressing the most important regional challenges in a broad range of areas. It will intervene principally in the fields of competitiveness and innovation by promoting digitalisation and energy efficiency accelerating the use of renewable energy sources. To face the challenges of climate change, the programme will foster prevention and adaptation and invest in sustainable transport. The programme will invest also in education, health and employment, social inclusion and territorial development.

The biggest part of the investments will support growth and competitiveness of micro enterprises and small and medium businesses, fostering job creation, development of local markets and internationalisation. A top priority will be to address youth unemployment, in order to reduce the rate of people not in education, employment or training (NEET). For the first time, the regional programme will also fight the very high poverty levels and address material deprivation.

In addition, the programme will invest in education and qualifications, notably through the reinforcement of vocational and educational training (VET) courses. Additionally, the programme will devote resources to the access to higher education and its support, including through the recruitment, training and retention of teachers in the islands.

Finally, Azores benefit from a European Regional Development Fund specific allocation for being a EU Outermost Region, which will support the costs of public service obligation in transport, strengthening the links between rural and urban areas and between the islands.

programme_description: Since the industrial revolution, North-West Europe has been at the vanguard of industrialisation and economic development in Europe. However, this century of growth came at a great cost: for the environment, for people, for territorial inequalities. The programme is looking for ways to contribute to compensate for such costs.

The overall aim of the programme and of its actions is to contribute to a balanced development across the North-West Europe programme area, regardless of the type of territory, helping to make it greener, more innovative, and more inclusive.

Through the programme, the EU supports the North-West Europe regions to be more resilient to climate change, to strengthen ecological connectivity, to reduce pollution and CO2 emissions, to transit towards greener solutions, such as renewable energy and circular economy. At the same time the EU will accompany both public and private players in the region while they develop their capacity for innovation capacity.

The programme contributes also to a more effective, inclusive, and quality labour market. In fact, it helps vulnerable groups, and it supports the emergence of available, accessible, inclusive, and resilient healthcare systems for all citizens.
Finally, it contributes to strengthen economic development, social inclusion and social innovation enhancing the role of culture and sustainable tourism.
The Atlantic Area programme cooperation space is eminently a maritime territory. This characteristic, jointly with the coast-hinterland relationships, heavily influences the Programme's conception.

For that reason, blue and green projects are crucial to this programme. Through it, the EU promotes blue innovation and competitiveness in the Atlantic Area regions. Ultimately, this approach will foster the protection and preservation of maritime and costal ecosystems. From a greener perspective, the programme aims to encourage resilience to climate change, to reduce pollution and CO2 emissions, to transit towards greener solutions, such as renewable energy and circular economy.

The cooperation area is located within the Atlantic sea-basin strategy, hence, to achieve better results and a significant impact on the blue investments, the Programme should seek synergies with the sea-basin strategy.

Blue Careers, as well as skilling -or reskilling- schemes for people in the blue economy sector will contribute to a more effective and inclusive labour market. Regarding social inclusion, data shows that the access to health care in this cooperation functional area needs to be improved through an Interreg programme, considering the difficulty to finance large investment projects.

The programme pays attention to the importance of cultural heritage and the tourism sector, key economic assets for coastal areas, but also for nearby inland areas, particularly in the French, Spanish and Portuguese regions.

Finally, the programme will focus its attention on governance, a policy objective seeking to ensure a constant flow of information between the Managing authority and Member States. Such close cooperation fits the goal of an optimal implementation of the Atlantic Area Programme.
The Programme focuses on three areas to be supported by the ERDF.

The programme will contribute to a smarter Europe by improving conditions for research and innovation. This will be achieved by strengthening the capacity of the public research institutions in the region (including the newly established Atlantic Technological University (ATU). The aim is also to  strengthen the links between domestic SMEs and these institutions in order to ensure that the region’s enterprises remain competitive and productive.

Efforts towards a greener, low-carbon Europe will be made by improving energy efficiency of residential homes. This will reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the programme area. The support will target households in or at risk of energy poverty.

Measures to increase the use of existing under-used buildings will be taken to create new homes to address problems of dereliction and vacancy in towns and to support regeneration of those areas to make them viable. This approach is in line with the New European Bauhaus initiative and creates the potential to realise beautiful, sustainable, and inclusive projects.

The programme area covers approximately 3 million km² of the northernmost parts of Europe and North Atlantic. Territories encompass Finland, Ireland, Sweden, Faroe Islands, Greenland, Iceland and Norway, which are defined by harsh climate, sparse population and extreme peripherality. Such characteristics makes many traditional forms of cooperation difficult.

The programme supports the twin green and digital transition as well as recovery from the pandemic in this vast region. This way, the northern and arctic communities can cooperate and work together in a way that recognises their specificities.

Through the ERDF, the EU supports the generation of attractive, competitive, and sustainable communities by harnessing innovation and digital solutions. Through these interventions, EU funds support the expansion the capacity for climate change adaptation and resource sufficiency, seizing the unique growth opportunities in the region - including supporting indigenous Sámi and Inuit cultures, livelihoods and entrepreneurship - while taking into account ecosystem-based approaches.

The programme aims also to strengthen the organisational capacity among the communities to make best use of cooperation opportunities, and to boost the programme’s role in developing transnational territorial cooperation in the Arctic.

programme_name: EIST (Employment, Inclusion, Skills and Training) Programme
programme_description: Ireland’s national ESF+ Employment, Inclusion, Skills and Training programme is opening doors to new qualifications and skills, getting people into jobs and a more inclusive society, with equal opportunities for young people, women and disadvantaged groups.

The programme will increase employment opportunities with activation programmes for young people, persons with disabilities, long-term unemployed and women. The aim is to create equal opportunities and help both those who have jobs and the unemployed to progress in their careers and have better employment prospects.

Activities will focus on expanding skills and lifelong learning. Workers may take part in employer-led upskilling or reskilling courses, while those lacking basic skills will have improved access to literacy, numeracy and digital literacy courses. Training will support early childhood education professionals and carers with a view to enhancing their skills and competences thus helping to deliver quality social services. Higher education institutions and schools will receive funding for programmes and projects to create more inclusive learning environments. Further financial support will be provided to disadvantaged students in higher education.

Dedicated projects will foster the social inclusion of vulnerable groups – including Roma, Irish Travellers, migrants and single-parent families. Migrants – including people fleeing the Russian aggression in Ukraine – will benefit from a comprehensive employment programme that includes language and social skills training, as well as individual mentoring. Special programmes will address the training and personal/social development needs of early school leavers and at-risk youth. Trainings and services will also be adapted to reach out to more people that can benefit from the programme
The provision of quality social support services and their accessibility, will improve the wellbeing of vulnerable children and families, including young parents and refugees.
Food and material aid will be provided to the most deprived, such as children and families living in poverty, homeless people and victims of domestic violence.

The ESF+ in Ireland will fund social innovation measures, including the testing of new ideas and policies to promote better social inclusion and support disadvantaged groups such as long-term unemployed individuals or young people living in deprived areas.

The National Programme Culture 2021-2027 seeks to address development challenges relating to the cultural sector in less developed regions in Italy (Molise, Campania, Puglia, Basilicata, Calabria, Sicily and Sardinia).

The main challenges addressed by the programme are harnessing the potential of culture for building creative and sustainable economies, unlocking the potential of the cultural sector for the green transition and the European Green Deal, maximising the contribution of the cultural sector to reducing growing social inequalities and territorial divides.

For harnessing the potential of culture for building creative and sustainable economies, the programme focuses on supporting digitalisation with a particular focus on public sector services and enhancing SMEs sustainable growth, competitiveness and job creation and sustain third sector entities carrying out economic activities in the cultural sector.

For unlocking the potential of the cultural sector for the green transition and the European Green Deal, the Programme intends to support energy efficiency interventions in archives, libraries and monumental complexes with high energy consumption, and investments for upgrading safety and resilience from risks of cultural sites owned by the State and by Sicily Region. The programme will also combine interventions for energy efficiency and prevention and risk resilience, specifically targeting 10 monumental complexes with a particular historical and artistic importance.

For maximising the contribution of the cultural sector to reducing social inequalities and territorial divides, priority is given to investments aimed at enhancing the role of culture for social inclusion and social innovation. Specifically, the Programme intends to support interventions for regenerating and activating state-owned cultural sites with the aim of widening cultural participation in relation to cultural welfare, to cultural and artistic education for nursery and primary schools, to tackle marginalisation and social exclusion of vulnerable people or at risk of deviations. Support is also envisaged for projects proposed by local communities aimed at increasing cultural participation through the development of cultural laboratories for the construction of creative communities.

Examples of projects to be supported within the programme include the creation of a common digital infrastructure and pilot worksite where exemplary interventions using integrated intervention methods for energy upgrading and preventing and securing the sites against natural risks will be carried out in monumental complexes of historical and artistic significance.

The region will also continue its work to close the digital skills gap to improve the resilience of the regional economic system. Such interventions will enable a shift from traditional production structures to more innovative ones, in line with the National Transition Plan 4.0 and the Regional Sustainable Development Strategy 2030.

Veneto will target the most energy-intensive sectors with a high potential for improvement through measures to reduce consumption and increase the use of renewable energy sources. Actions in Research and Innovation will be crucial in identifying solutions to make energy generation more efficient and reduce consumption.

For climate risk-prevention, the region will focus on the erosion of the coastal area and damage caused by frequent storms, landslides, floods and on the monitoring of seismic risk. With an eye on circular economy, the region plans to review production and consumption patterns to increase efficiency in the waste re-use cycle.

In complementarity with the ESF+ programme, the programme will enable the region to develop accessible technological infrastructure for distance learning and improve school infrastructure. Furthermore, EU funding will allow the purchase of school laboratory equipment and contribute to reducing school dropout, fostering the integration of people at risk of social exclusion. In urban areas, actions will be implemented for social integration of vulnerable people and households through inclusive housing and measures to improve access to quality services. The involvement of local communities in the promotion and regeneration of cultural heritage will be strengthened with the goal of fostering social inclusion and sustainable tourism.

Veneto will promote the residential and economic attractiveness of a number of inland and urban areas in conjunction with other urban initiatives in the other policy areas. Under this objective, the region foresees measures to regenerate these areas, improve access to digital services and improve the quality of the urban environment through a sustainable and integrated mobility system, green infrastructure and actions to promote social inclusion in more fragile contexts.
The programme’s contribution to climate is 36.7% and to sustainable urban development 16.2%.

programme_description: The ESF+ programme for addressing material deprivation in Lithuania will provide food and basic material assistance to people across the country who are most in need, addressing income inequality, poverty and social exclusion. The programme will support individuals and families with low income, including large families, single parents, older persons and long-term unemployed people.

People who can benefit from the programme will be referred from municipalities’ social services, ensuring those most in need will be the first to receive food and material assistance.  The support will be provided to individuals with a monthly income lower than the value of minimum consumption needs as approved by the Minister of Social Security and Labour. This support will cover children at-risk of poverty or social exclusion, older persons and persons with disabilities, as well as long-term unemployed individuals who live under the bare minimum. Ukrainian refugees are entitled to receive an identical support.

Partner organisations distributing the e-vouchers for the purchase of food and material goods will complement them with accompanying measures, such as consultations, training, information on availability of social or other relevant services.

programme_description: The Sicily regional programme is the second largest in Europe. It will contribute to the promotion of innovative, smart and sustainable economic transformation in line with the objectives defined by the EU Green Deal.
Regarding digitalisation, the programme will support the wider uptake of digital transition services by businesses, public authorities and citizens.

Moreover, the programme foresees actions aimed at the decarbonisation of the economy and the mitigation of the effects of climate change. It will support the renewable energy and energy efficiency sectors, together with the development of clean energy infrastructure and energy carriers/technologies.
On adaptation to climate change, the programme will promote actions to strengthen prevention measures to increase hydrogeological resilience in line with the sector plans.

Converning sustainable water management, the programme will contribute to the implementation of regional sector planning. In particular this will be achieved through measures aimed at restoring the efficiency of water supply networks and resolving infringements of EU wastewater legislation.
Regarding the circular economy, the programme will support the prevention of waste generation, transforming it into high-quality secondary resources.

On sustainable mobility, the programme supports less impactful urban transport modes. To this end, the programme will finance the upgrading and strengthening of public transport and the renewal of the rolling stock, including by capitalising on technological innovation.

The programme will also promote the attractiveness, sustainability and competitiveness of functional urban areas and inland Sicilian areas, helping to reduce gaps by strengthening the integrated territorial dimension of sectoral policies.

programme_description: The Trento ESF+ regional programme will improve employment opportunities and services, increase access to quality education and training, and promote social inclusion and gender equality in the region.

ESF+ investments in Trento focus on improving employability and access to the labour market for unemployed people, with a focus on opportunities for the long-term unemployed and those with precarious or short-term contracts. Actions include personalised guidance and upskilling/reskilling in support of labour mobility and/or self-employment.

The programme also allocates resources to strengthen the employability of young people through hiring incentives, complementing national schemes. The ESF+ in the region will support women’s participation in the labour market, such as vouchers for educational services and hiring incentives for employers.

Measures will increase labour market inclusion of unemployed and inactive people while strengthening the employability of workers most at risk of losing their jobs. Funded projects will improve the quality and safety of work environments, promote respect for labour rights and increase the possibilities of finding a job. The programme will also invest in strengthening the capacity of employment centres and the quality of public and private employment services for job seekers and inactive people.
The ESF+ in Trento will also invest in training courses for unemployed people and in measures to promote employment mobility.

The ESF+ in Trento will improve educational and vocational training opportunities, as well as the quality, innovation and resilience of the regional education system. The programme invests in students' key competences, with particular attention paid to digital and linguistic skills.

Dedicated actions promote lifelong learning and continuous-learning opportunities for adult and young people to support the acquisition of the skills needed to enhance employability and labour mobility. Actions include learning opportunities for digital skills, transversal and basic skills as well as technical and professional skills such as managerial, entrepreneurial and organisational skills.

ESF+ investments will foster the socio-economic integration of disadvantaged people and support social enterprises. The focus will be on low-income families and other vulnerable groups including persons with disabilities and people with a migrant background. The programme will finance the consolidation and expansion of integrated social and healthcare services such as housing, early education and care for dependent people, or persons with limited autonomy.
Over 70 000 participants will benefit from the programme, including:

programme_description: The ESF+ regional programme for Marche will invest in strengthening social and employment support services, improving the links between educational institutions and enterprises with the aim of boosting employment and promoting social inclusion. Dedicated support will be provided to young people and women to find jobs and mitigate high unemployment rates among these groups in the region.
ESF+ investments in Marche will also enhance the attractiveness of historical towns, promoting labour-market opportunities through tourism.

Projects funded under the ESF+ will promote skills acquisition in the region – particularly in the field of digital competencies and tourism. The link between university education and technical secondary schools with enterprises will be improved.

The programme will place strategic importance on public employment centres, taking an active role through training of their employees and improving their monitoring and data gathering capacity. Actions will also be undertaken to guarantee digital inter-operability and information sharing between labour-market services, local authorities and other entities which provide support for employment.

Actions under this programme will allow adults who did not complete compulsory education to obtain primary and secondary education diplomas. The ESF+ will also finance technical secondary schools and provide opportunities for workers to participate in trainings on digital skills.

Young people will benefit from increased research and study grants, as well as from measures to prevent early school leaving. The ESF+ regional programme will provide dedicated opportunities to enhance their skills for the green and digital transitions.

ESF+ investments will also promote young people's involvement in the labour market, particularly through the financing of traineeships, apprenticeships and academic or non-academic post-secondary education and higher education.

Projects promoting social inclusion will involve non-governmental organisations in active inclusion activities for the region’s most vulnerable groups, including persons with disabilities, long-term unemployed, and homeless people. Dedicated funding will be provided for the strengthening of local social services.
Working women will be able to benefit from specific incentives, such as vouchers for nurseries and incentives for firms to adopt family-friendly working models.
