programme_description: The region has chosen four areas in which it will concentrate investments. These encompass the following areas of intervention:

Concretely, there will be calls for proposals for research and development projects, industrial research projects, technology transfer activities and investments to strengthen the ecosystem of innovative start-ups.

The programme will also provide funding for the digital transition of businesses, including through administrative simplification and the provision of innovative digital services. For small and medium sized enterprises, the Marche Region is focusing on the modernisation of its production system, while also promoting export and supporting local enterprises. Under these priorities, actions will give new life to the entrepreneurial fabric of the region, making it better equipped for current and forthcoming challenges while creating new jobs.

Marche’s second priority focuses on reducing energy expenditure both for businesses and public authorities. Initiatives aimed at producing more energy from renewable sources will receive support from EU funds. This will contribute to energy self-sufficiency as well as to the reduction of pollution.

Climate change is another central issue driving the region’s priorities. In fact, Marche was hit hard by a combination of droughts and floods. For this reason, investments devoted to mitigating hydrogeological risk are paramount. Equally important are interventions improving the water network, managing river basins and reducing the erosion of the coast lines.

The third priority puts the spotlight on urban mobility with the clear objective of promoting sustainable multimodal urban mobility as part of the transition to a net-zero carbon economy. Several interventions are planned: from the renewal of public transport networks to the creation of infrastructure and hubs that facilitate the use of public transport.

Finally, there are funds dedicated to support integrated local strategies, both in urban areas and in the inner, mountainous part of the region. In these areas, local authorities and organisations define together which interventions will make life in the cities and remote communities more attractive and inclusive. The management authority of the programme will provide the necessary technical support to the local authorities to make these local strategies a success.

programme_description: The Urbact IV programme focuses on supporting cities in implementing solutions to tackle the green, just and digital transitions in particular, through collaboration, capacity building and expertise. The purpose is to promote integrated sustainable development in cities, improve city’s policies and improve the effectiveness of Cohesion policy in cities.

Its supports the delivery of key principles of sustainable urban development on the ground, such as good governance, integrated and place-based approaches, all making the link to the urban and territorial dimension of Cohesion policy and to its minimum requirements as per the 2021-2027 regulatory provisions.

The Programme will cover the EU 27 Member States, Norway, Switzerland as well as some countries benefitting from the Instrument for Pre-Accession (IPA) such as Albania, Montenegro, Serbia, Republic of North Macedonia, and Bosnia-Herzegovina.The URBACT programme covers the entire territory of the participating countries and is open to cities of all sizes. It will pay particular attention to cities benefitting from Cohesion policy in order to support them by increasing cooperation with other cities to find solutions, by supporting them with dedicated tools and expertise to improve their capacity to develop and implement integrated strategies and plans, to transfer innovative solutions and practices, to share and build knowledge and to find funding for planned investments and projects.

The programme area covers the western and southern part of Latvia and northern part of Lithuania with a total population of 1.8 million.
The largest share of the programme budget is dedicated to prevent risks related to climate change, combat the loss of bio-diversity and avert the degradation of the environment.

The funds will also support the integration of disadvantaged social groups into the labour market. It will develop more efficient and proactive social services, while improving their accessibility. The programme equally aims at strengthening the capacity and know-how of organisations that provide these services.

The funds will also strengthen the role of cultural heritage and tourism in creating jobs, promoting local economic activity and diversifying the use of heritage and heritage sites, including the development of revenue-generating activities.
Actions in these main priorities are complemented by efforts to foster better governed co-operation and trust building measures between cross-border communities.
Operations of strategic importance (OSI) will support climate and sustainable tourism, like creating a joint tourism brand.

The mission of ESPON is to deliver evidence, data and advice.  Given the main territorial challenges at stake and the EU policy framework, ESPON intends to support policy makers at all levels by providing territorial evidence and knowledge to inform policy responses to strengthen EU territories’ resilience and recovery of from crises by achieving a green transition to climate-neutral economies while ensuring just living conditions in all places.
With a total budget of EUR 60 Million , (EUR 48 Million EU funding) , the Programme will cover all 27 EU Member States in partnership with Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

ESPON research and activities are highly relevant for cohesion policy programming and implementation, and as part of the interregional programmes family it particularly contributes to cohesion policy effectiveness. In addition, key areas supported through research and evidence include  the European Green Deal, Just Transition and Recovery, the Territorial Agenda 2030 (TA2030) process and implementation.

ESPON supports these processes through policy briefs, territorial evidence reports, territorial monitoring tools and other dedicated studies and outreach events, both arranged on demand of respective ESPON member countries, European cooperation partners, and the relevant intergovernmental networks. ESPON also supports macro-regional strategies, sea-basin strategies, as done in the past, with data and monitoring tools and responding to ad-hoc support requests.

The Urbact IV programme focuses on supporting cities in implementing solutions to tackle the green, just and digital transitions in particular, through collaboration, capacity building and expertise. The purpose is to promote integrated sustainable development in cities, improve city’s policies and improve the effectiveness of Cohesion policy in cities.

Its supports the delivery of key principles of sustainable urban development on the ground, such as good governance, integrated and place-based approaches, all making the link to the urban and territorial dimension of Cohesion policy and to its minimum requirements as per the 2021-2027 regulatory provisions.

The Programme will cover the EU 27 Member States, Norway, Switzerland as well as some countries benefitting from the Instrument for Pre-Accession (IPA) such as Albania, Montenegro, Serbia, Republic of North Macedonia, and Bosnia-Herzegovina.The URBACT programme covers the entire territory of the participating countries and is open to cities of all sizes. It will pay particular attention to cities benefitting from Cohesion policy in order to support them by increasing cooperation with other cities to find solutions, by supporting them with dedicated tools and expertise to improve their capacity to develop and implement integrated strategies and plans, to transfer innovative solutions and practices, to share and build knowledge and to find funding for planned investments and projects.

The programme aims at strengthening the Latvian-Estonian cooperation that is necessary to tackle the major challenges the cross-border territories face. Moreover, cooperation will develop the potential of an area rich in natural and cultural assets. It will also improve the quality of life for approximately two million people living in the area.
To boost the small-scale economy of the cross-border region, small businesses will receive support to innovate and find joint solutions for smart and green transformation.

programme_description: The ESF+ regional programme for Emilia-Romagna in Italy will improve employment opportunities and the efficiency of active labour-market services. ESF+ investments in the region will support education and training, including lifelong learning, and promote social inclusion and equal opportunities. This will help prepare people for fair, green and digital transitions.

The ESF+ in the region will support young people, particularly those not in employment, education or training by creating and enhancing training opportunities, apprenticeships and support services for their employment.

Programme activities will focus on supporting the innovation and development of academic and non-academic, post-secondary education and of higher education, with particular attention given to women and young people. Funded measures will prepare people in the region for the green and digital transition and for careers in strategic sectors of the regional economy, investing in lifelong learning and skills-development opportunities for adults and young people to support their employability and labour mobility.

ESF+ investments will promote projects designed to prevent social exclusion and foster active inclusion and equal opportunities. Measures will include expanded access to university education and access to childcare services for disadvantaged children.

programme_description: The Lazio ESF+ regional programme will improve employment opportunities and services, increase access to quality education and training and promote social inclusion and gender equality. It will address social challenges, foster upskilling and ensure that active labour market policies reach out to young people and vulnerable groups.

The focus will be on measures that ensure people from a disadvantaged background, including long-term unemployed and persons with disabilities, have better access to jobs – thanks to integrated and personalised support and upskilling and reskilling. Active labour market services will be strengthened. To boost women’s participation in the labour market, the programme will also support conciliation services, innovative flexible work organisation in companies and extended access (e.g. opening hours) to childcare facilities that can improve work-life balance.

Young people not in employment, education or training (NEETs) will be offered quality and inclusive education and training, enabling them to successfully integrate into the labour market. They will also have access to subsidised loans with a reduced interest rate, which can support them for starting self-employed professional activities and/or set up new micro- or small enterprises.

ESF+ Lazio will support the development of non-academic, post-secondary education, higher education and greater opportunities for advanced university degree programmes (such as PhD and master’s degrees). In order to prepare people and enterprises for the green and digital transitions, the programme will increase research grants and other funding, reinforceskills identification, validation and certification services and expand opportunities for non-academic, post-secondary education and lifelong learning. The “Torno subito” (“I will be right back”) programme will be replicated, with a dedicated budget to provide young people with specialised training outside the region and Italy – followed by work experience upon their return to the region to apply the newly-acquired skills.

The programme will be dedicated to promoting active inclusion and equal opportunities for vulnerable people – including migrants and persons with disabilities – focusing on personalised support. Social and care services in the region will be enhanced – including access to housing and childcare. Strategic importance is assigned to care services for children and dependent people, who will benefit from a voucher programme.
More than 325,000 participants will benefit from programme activities, including:

programme_description: Latvia's ESF+ programme for Addressing Material Deprivation will provide food and basic material assistance to the most deprived people across the country. It will support the households most in need of food and basic material assistance and help improve both the social safety net and overall social inclusion for some of Latvia's most vulnerable people.

People will be able to benefit from the programme once they have been referred from the municipalities’ social service agencies, stating that they belong to a needy household, a low-income household or a household in a crisis situation. This will ensure that those who are most in need will be able to receive necessary food and material assistance. Certification of eligibility from the municipality will not be required for persons receiving ready-made meals in soup kitchens.

The support will focus on helping the most vulnerable households, including children, elderly persons and persons with disabilities, as well as long-term unemployed people. Ukrainian refugees are also entitled to receive an identical support package.

Partner organisations involved in the distribution of food and basic material assistance will complement this support with accompanying measures, such as consultations, training, information on availability of social or other services based on individual needs assessment.
Thanks to this ESF+ programme, it is estimated that approximately 59 000 people per year will receive the food and material assistance they need. This includes:

programme_description: The European Commission adopted the single multi-fund cohesion policy programme for the period 2021-2027 in Latvia on 25 November 2022. The programme paves the way for investments from the European Regional Development Fund, the Cohesion Fund, the European Social Fund+ and the Just Transition Fund. The cohesion policy funds will boost the development of the country towards a more competitive, greener and fairer economy.

The funds will be invested to increase Latvia’s level of research and innovation, in particular via investments in innovative Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs) and trainings to increase the general level of basic digital skills.

In line with the European Green Deal, the funds will be invested in energy-efficiency measures reducing greenhouse gas emissions and at the same time reducing energy poverty. The CF and ERDF will invest in sustainable modes of transport including railways and better tram and cycling infrastructure in cities. The JTF will mainly invest in the restoration of peatlands, which as a natural carbon sink are reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

The investments will also allow more people to acquire labour market relevant skills at all education levels necessary for a digital and green transition, including life-long-learning. They will improve access to early childhood care, education and social housing.

The Campania regional programme refers to one of the most important Region in Southern Italy. The region faces challenges in expressing its potential for innovation and in facing the green transition with its climate change adaptation aspects.

To address these challenges, the programme aims to ease the small and medium enterprises (SMEs) access to innovative techniques and processes. To this end the programme will facilitate the upgrade of research infrastructures, as well as the creation and upscaling of innovative firms. A balanced use of grants and financial instruments will support the industrial transition while creating better access to ICT services and the capital market.

Coherently with environmental goals, the programme enhances energy efficiency for public buildings and enterprises. In addition, investments in renewables energies for self-consumption will receive assistance. Such investments will help climate change adaptation, risk prevention and disaster resilience, including for environmental infrastructures for wastewater treatment and waste management. The programme also encourages a shift towards cleaner forms of mobility, especially in urban areas.

The promotion of social constitutes an additional priority in Campania. Through support to the social economy, the programme aims to favour the access to quality education services, and inclusion of marginalised people, including third countries nationals. A push to strengthen primary health care and digital health services on the territory is key for social inclusion, whereas culture can be a key driver of both inclusion and innovation.

A cross cutting issue is represented by the need to improve the effective delivery of the EU interventions and to this effect a new plan for administrative reinforcement will frame capacity building interventions.

Examples of projects to be supported within the programme include the digitalisation of businesses and the Public Administration, the improvement of water infrastructures, the purchase of “zero emission” rolling stock, “cold ironing” reducing the pollution of ships in ports and tertiary education infrastructures.
Finally, within the framework of integrated territorial strategies and with backing to 26 urban areas and 7 inner areas, the programme fosters a Region closer to its citizen.

The ESF+ regional programme for Abruzzo in Italy aims to reduce unemployment through incentives for hiring, education and training, as well as support for self-employment. Active labour-market policies will address the needs of people furthest away from the labour market, such as long-term unemployed, persons with disabilities and people from a migrant background. Activities under the programme will advance the employment of women and help young people integrate into the labour market.

University education and higher technical education and training are also an investment priority for the region, including in skills for advancing the green and digital transitions. Lifelong learning mechanisms will be put in place. The programme will encourage links between high school and university and higher, technical education with the labour market.

To support social inclusion, planned projects will address extreme poverty and social exclusion with complex policies capable of considering different types of issues and needs, targeted at vulnerable groups, families as well as caregivers. Actions will range from creating places to combat social exclusion, to creating pathways for independent living and supporting families, young people and children in situations of fragility. The ESF+ will also support centres for victims of domestic violence.

Funding will provide incentives for firms to hire long-term unemployed and inactive people. Micro-credit will also be granted to develop new businesses in remote areas. In order to improve work-life balance and promote women’s employment, working mothers will receive vouchers to acquire care services.

Projects under the programme will target both young people and adults already in work. Innovative projects in high schools and in technical post-secondary education will focus on strategic areas of industry and the regional economy. The programme will help enhance the capacity of job centres and other entities to provide tailored counselling and training. This priority also includes actions for advanced education such as doctoral programmes and second-level masters.

The programme will fund workshops supporting labour-market integration for people with disabilities and will fund measures to help people in prison to find a job after leaving the criminal justice system. This programme will also enhance the ability of local social services to provide support to people at risk of poverty and social exclusion.

Young people will benefit from micro-credit to create new businesses, hiring incentives awarded to firms, and opportunities such as a three-year programme including both formal education and on-the-job training focused on the most in-demand skills in the labour market.

programme_description: The Programme area is extremely diversified in terms of territory and population density. It features densely populated areas on the Italian side and more rural areas on the Slovenian side. Ongoing depopulation trends affect the area, especially on the Italian side. The area’s economic performance does not fare much differently than EU standards with the Italian side being slightly above the EU average of GDP per capita and the Slovenian side being slightly below.

Interventions will focus on introducing digitization, making natural and cultural heritage more accessible for a wider public.  Moreover, enhancing Green Infrastructure Networks and fostering shared approaches, improve the management and promotion of protected areas. There is a need to promote linguistic minorities and cultural heritage at large by supporting creative industries and sustainable, accessible tourism. In the latter sector, interventions will support the shaping of an integrated approach encompassing transport, culture, education, innovation, and sustainable development. Such actions will create the conditions to increase tourism flows to peri-urban and rural areas towards sustainable approach to tourism. The programme will provide direct support to the European Capital of Culture 2025 (Nova Gorica - Gorizia), namely via a small projects fund.

The programme seeks to finance people-to-people actions to strengthen mutual trust and to overcome existing obstacles. Furthermore, it will favour collaboration in the area through the implementation of joint pilot actions, joint tools and monitoring systems, coordinated protocols, innovative joint solutions and the exchange of best practices. Additionally, joint cross-border strategies will seek to capitalise on good practices stemming from the previous Interreg Italy-Slovenia Programme(s).
Finally, Programme will promote synergies with EU EUSAIR and EUSALP Strategies.

Analysis of the local context shows both opportunities and challenges. The region needs support for innovation capacity. Moreover it needs to ensure the sustainable use of natural and and cultural resources through the promotion of the green and digital transitions; including through the development of sustainable mobility.help tomitigating the consequences of climate change and prevent risks related to it. In addition, the area needs to address progressive ageing and attract the youth in depopulating areas; while also addressing diversity with specific and bottom up territorial approaches.
On that basis, five priorities for investments were set:

In order to better involve the local communities in the cooperation strategy implementation and in its governance, the programme will support the creation of a Small Projects Fund in the German speaking area. This experience will serve as a guide to similar actions that could be further developed in the rest of the programme area.

The programme aims to mitigate the consequences of climate change in the Mediterranean sea and its negative effects on all the territories bordering the basin and far beyond. The necessary challenge of the Green deal will also be accompanied by an effort of supervision, coordination, technical and political cooperation that will span the entire the Mediterranean basin.
Moreover, the programme aims to reinforce the potential for innovation that, with the exception of capitals and main cities, remains low across the region.

To reach these objectives, the programme has a strong climate and environment orientation. It contributes to the EU climate targets with 35% of the programme allocation and to environmental objectives - with 66% of its resources. More than 10% of the budget is devoted to tackling biodiversity issues.

The programme also plays an important role in the implementation of the Western Maritime Initiative as it shares parts of its cooperation area with the West Mediterranean area. It will allow involvement of partners beyond the programme area, thus creating links and activating synergies within and across the sea basin regions.

Finally, with the exception of Serbia, the programme area also covers the area of the Adriatic and Ionian Macro regional strategy (EUSAIR). Other Interreg programmes concerning the Adriatic Sea are expected to contribute to the Programme for the priorities related to the EUSAIR. Thus, the programme entails coordination and cooperation mechanisms to interact with other interreg programmes active in the MED area, capitalising on project outputs and results and increasing their territorial impact.

programme_name: (Interreg VI-B) NEXT Mediterranean Sea Basin (NEXT MED)
programme_description: The programme fosters fair and sustainable cooperation between 7 EU Member States and 8 partner countries in the Southern Neighbourhood (i.e. Algeria, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, Tunisia and Türkiye). The participating countries jointly developed the programme based on the principle of equal footing. There is a strong and shared understanding that many of today’s challenges in the Mediterranean Sea Basin are common across the countries in the region and that there is an urgent need to find common solutions.

The largest part of EU funding (42%) will be allocated to projects that address climate change and environmental challenges. these include energy efficiency measures, sustainable water use, climate change adaptation, circular economy as well as risk prevention.

Secondly, the programme aims to create a more competitive and smarter Mediterranean by providing support and improving conditions for SMEs. Such actions should pave the way for greater internationalisation, transnational research-business cooperation as well as reducing disparities and gaps in research and innovation across the Mediterranean.

The third aim is to foster a more social and inclusive Mediterranean by providing better quality and access to education and training. This will concern young people and disadvantaged groups in particular. Health represents a key factor in the reduction of economic and social inequalities. Therefore, project partners will focus on developing innovative digital and services that improve the delivery and efficiency of health services.

Finally, the programme aims to improve the cooperation governance across the Mediterranean through a number of tools, including joint capacity building actions for public authorities as well as transnational cooperation between citizens, civil society actors and public institutions based on bottom-up and participatory approaches.
The programme has a particular focus on young people and it will ensure a strong system of complementarities and synergies with other EU funding streams operating in the Mediterranean.

The Alpine region is disproportionally affected by climate change, loss of biodiversity and natural hazards. The transnational Interreg programme aims to address these challenges, making the region greener and more resilient through the implementation of the EU Green Deal in one of the most innovative regions in Europe.
The programme has divided its actions in four complementary objectives, namely:

This sea-crossing programme aims to foster fair and sustainable development for the people living in the Mediterranean Sea Basin. The programme builds on 15 years of cooperation experience between Italy and Tunisia and it aspires to make the Mediterranean a greener, cleaner, more competitive and more inclusive space to live.

The programme is particularly ambitious in terms of contributing to the Green Deal with 45% of the programme funding allocated to green transition measures and to joint solutions that address climate change and environmental challenges.

Joint actions will focus on increasing renewable energy sources, improving sustainable water management, strengthening the protection and preservation of nature and biodiversity and developing risk management tools.

Secondly, the programme will boost the business system by supporting sustainable growth and competitiveness in SMEs in order to generate higher income and better jobs, particularly for women and young people. This includes start-up initiatives and services, living labs and cross-border business networks.

Tourism is a potential accelerator of economic growth, which is not yet used in a sufficiently sustainable manner. Therefore, the aim is to develop joint models and solutions to promote sustainable, natural and cultural tourism geared towards new market segments as well as responsible and alternative forms of tourism involving local communities.

In addition, the programme seeks to address the fragility in the health systems by ensuring more equal and better access to health in terms coverage and quality of the services in the programme area. The programme will include joint actions to promote access to health care for marginalised and vulnerable populations.

Finally, with the aim to improve the overall cooperation governance, the programme will finance capacity building in public administration, models of participatory governance and small-scale projects that engage civil society and promote a true people-to-people approach.
The programme pays particular attention to ensuring complementarities and synergies with other EU funding streams operating in the Mediterranean Sea Basin.

The new programme aims for a central Europe with less social and economic disparities, one which cooperates to become smarter, greener, and better connected. Its mission is to bring regions and cities together beyond borders to find fitting solutions for their citizens in a fair and equal way.

The chosen priorities include economic transition processes, climate change, and the long-term socio-economic consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic. The programme supports businesses to become more innovative; and communities - climate-neutral and resilient to climate change risks. It also fosters ideas on how to improve transport connections of rural and peripheral regions in central Europe.

In practice, the programme brings together public organisations, the private sector and civil society and finances transnational projects, which develop, test and implement solutions that are urgently needed to make central Europe more resilient and attractive. The programme supports these partnerships also with guidance and knowledge.
The Adriatic-Ionian area aligns with the perimeter of the EU strategy of the Adriatic-Ionian Region (EUSAIR), embracing a unique mix of EU partner countries, Western Balkans and third countries.

The programme will facilitate the conditions for strong effective cooperation and good relations among partner countries. It will provide a constructive contribution to the EU enlargement process, reduce disparities and improve social cohesion with non-EU countries, as well as supporting the implementation of EUSAIR as such.

The programme aims at addressing the challenges that the countries of the Adriatic-Ionian region share. These range from the safeguard of biodiversity and climate change to sustainable transport. By way of innovative methods the programme will act as a pivotal instrument for the identification of common solutions and it will contribute to making the region smarter, greener and stronger in the face of economic shocks.

The socio-economic analysis of the programme area shows both opportunities and the common challenges. The area needs  support in promoting the competitiveness of micro, small, and mdium-sized enterprises (MSMEs).

Investment will go to fostering technology transfer in the sectors of green and blue economy and in mitigating the effects of climate change or anthropogenic impacts (notably waste management and tourism) on the land-sea system. Funds will help safeguard areas with high biodiversity value while promoting the sustainable and inclusive models of tourism that capitalise on cultural and natural heritage assets. In addition, EU funds will support the youth, in particular promoting the employability of youth not in education, employment nor training (NEETs).

EDIOP Plus is Hungary’s largest national programme aiming to improve Hungary’s competitiveness.

The EU funds can help SMEs buy the state-of-the-art technology they need to become greener, more digital, and more productive. A network of enterprise agencies will provide comprehensive and coordinated assistance to all SMEs, specifically to female entrepreneurs, start-ups and enterprises in the least developed regions.
The European Social Fund (ESF+) will help SMEs and citizens adapt to labour market changes by supporting trainings, wage subsidies, healthy and safe workplaces, and flexible working arrangements.

The vision of this cross-border programme is a border region that makes full use of its environmental, natural and cultural values. This will be achieved by promoting the preservation and sustainable utilisation of the region’s resources for tourism, and by establishing it as an attractive green tourism destination.

The main aim of the programme is to address environmental challenges linked to climate change, and to protect nature and biodiversity. Support will be given to joint cross-border projects that protect biodiversity, foster joint water and disaster management and reduce pollution.

The programme will protect and promote cultural heritage and sustainable and harmonised cross-border tourism. This will lead to a more integrated cross-border economy, one that will contribute to increased local tourism income and employment.

Actions in these priorities are supplemented by small-scale, people-to-people, trust-building projects, which are of high importance in the cross-border area as they foster closer cooperation and contribute to creating an integrated border region.

The programme supports the implementation of the EU Strategy for the Danube Region (EUSDR), fostering transnational actions across fourteen countries, including nine EU member states and five partner countries.
The programme region is characterized by its cultural diversity and territorial and socio-economic disparities. Therefore the Interreg programme aims at creating a shared ‘Danubian’ space.

The first objective of the programme is to make the Danube region smarter, with projects devoted to enhancing innovation and technology transfer. This will require efforts to develop new skills for industrial transition and smart specialisation. In addition the programme contributes to increase the use of renewable energies, preserve the biodiversity with ecological corridors and support joint actions on management of risks related to climate change.

Moreover, the programme allows EU Member States to work together with candidates and potential candidate countries, to reach common goals and to improve standards for an efficient public administration.

The programme acts as one-stop-shop for the almost 100 Interreg programmesInteract’s focus is on improving the process of cooperation in Interreg and beyond, limiting the diversity of solutions through harmonisation and eventually simplifying it.

Interact will continue to focus on strengthening the management capacity of Interreg programmes and other cooperation actors, like the Investment for Jobs and Growth programmes, and the EU Macro-regional Strategies.

The overall programme objective is defined as follows:

The incidence of floods, land-slides and fires deriving from draughts and land abandonment drive the need for climate change adaptation strategies. This, along with the management of natural and anthropic hazards, emerged as priorities for the upcoming programme, as well as key areas of investment.

Co-operation in the field of protection and valorisation of natural resources, including green infrastructure, represents a common investment need for the programme.Territorial analysis showed how, excluding major urban centres, uneven distribution of public services (especially in the health, cultural and tourism sectors) represents a significant obstacle on the path to a balanced development and internal regional cohesion of the border region.
Cultural heritage in the area has the potential to contribute to the development of a long-term preservation instrument, including under a common approach for tourism destination management .
In accordance with the Interreg Specific Objectives, the focus will be on promoting people-to-people interventions as a foundation for more structured cooperation.

Such cooperation should seek to build sustainable and inclusive communities and an open business environment. This will represent a solid base for designing tailor-made solutions for future community-led initiatives and integrated socio-economic strategies at cross-border level. Thus people-to-people actions will function as “laboratories” for the engagement of local communities.
Finally, the Programme will promote synergies with the EU Strategy for Danube Region.

Building upon hundreds of existing local partnerships between Ukraine and the three bordering Member States, the programme aims to address the vital needs of the border region. Such partnerships acquire greater relevance now, after the Russian military aggression of Ukraine, which greatly impacted the border area.

The programme will provide financing for investment in the health sector. It will particularly focus its support to the mainstreaming of digital technologies in healthcare, implementing both health screening and health promotion programmes, while also addressing rescue services. In addition to that, the programme will help to identify barriers, build partnerships, develop prevention activities, and develop health-related social initiatives.

The programme partners agreed on providing financing to projects supporting green transition. This will cover actions aimed at increasing preparedness for natural and human-made threats, but also address the protection of natural habitats and mapping pollution sources from air, soil and water. Another important element will be investing in information campaigns concerning the sustainable use of natural resources.
The programme will also help to identify and test cooperative approaches to cultural activities and tourism-related services. This will be done by involving youth and educating it on cultural values.
Finally, the programme is designed to enhance the cooperation of public authorities when it concerns legal and administrative burdens that make cooperation across borders difficult.

The Swedish ESF+ Programme will enhance access to employment for jobseekers, promote lifelong learning and support socio-economic inclusion. ESF+ investments will help Sweden’s most vulnerable – including young and older persons, long-term unemployed and persons with disabilities – to find work or enrol in training and education.

Thanks to the programme, employed people will be able to develop the skills they need to adapt to the changing world of work and benefit from the green and digital transition. Projects financed from ESF+ will promote inclusion and labour equality between men and women. The programme funds actions for testing, developing and reinforcing long-term socio-economic solutions.
The ESF+ in Sweden will also contribute to transnational cooperation, in particular with Member States involved in
People fleeing the war in Ukraine and registered in Sweden under the
will be able to receive support from the ESF+ programme.

Measures under the ESF+ will help to integrate unemployed people into the labour market, as well as promote lifelong learning for those already employed. Peoples’ skills will be matched with employers’ needs, allowing workers to adapt to the changing labour market. The programme will focus on helping those at risk of poverty and those furthest away from the labour market – including long-term unemployed, older people, newly-arrived migrants, persons with disabilities and people on sick leave needing support to return to their role at work. At-risk students as young as 13 years of age will also be helped to avoid early school leaving.

The programme will promote economic self-sufficiency, focusing on children and adults at risk of poverty or social exclusion. Measures will include training, education, validation, help with homework and meaningful leisure and extracurricular activities for children and young people, helping to promote social inclusion.

This priority supports the northern regions Upper Norrland and Middle Norrland, which are characterised by few opportunities for public transport, a low population density and an ageing population, with economies based largely on natural resources. ESF+ support will strengthen the capacity of local and regional structures to cope with these challenges.

ESF+ funds will enable innovative, effective solutions to address complex societal challenges, and support the creation of new networks and methods of collaboration. Interventions will address needs related to social inclusion, labour market integration, education and capacity building - from an individual, organisational and structural level.

programme_description: This programme will give support to enterprises and innovation environments with the ambition of strengthening competitiveness and contributing to their sustainable development. By supporting business transformation, SMEs will become enablers for the energy and environment transition, thus contributing overall to the climate transition targets.

The ambition is to contribute to a smarter Europe by supporting small businesses in innovation, digitalisation and economic transformation measures. Among other things, the programme seeks to address the shortage of certain skills linked to new technologies and also the need to increase cooperation between academia and SMEs in order to improve their capacity to innovate.

Moreover, the programme will undertake strategic measures that will lead to a greener, low-carbon Europe.  This will be done by investing in new innovative renewable energy solutions as well as by promoting energy efficiency and the transition towards a circular economy. The investments will encourage more companies to develop viable innovative goods and services with the potential to reduce energy use. The support will also contribute to the systemic transition to circular business models in the region’s economy. This will be done by actions that develop, influence and demonstrate the potential of reducing the use of raw materials and the climate impact while generating profit.

programme_name: European Regional Development Fund programme for Upper Norrland 2021-2027
programme_description: The EU funds will contribute to making the Upper Norrland region and Europe smarter, more competitive, greener, and more connected.

The ambition is to contribute to a smarter Europe by supporting and strengthening the development of research environments and the ability of companies to increase their own research and development. Businesses and the public sector in the region will be encouraged to better exploit the potential of digital technologies.

New business and organisational models will receive support to harness the potential of digitalisation, and the establishment of the European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIH) will be targeted to offer regional businesses and the public sector greater capacity to seize the opportunities of digitization.

Access to high-capacity broadband is lacking in some parts of the region, in areas with sparse population and very long distances. To close this gap, investments will support actions to increase the availability of broadband with high transmission capacity.

Interventions will also enable the emergence of new business models and concepts, especially the ones that combine entrepreneurship and engagement to help solve major societal challenges and actions that strengthen entrepreneurship. This focus includes models of entrepreneurship based on the Sami culture. The programme will promote lifelong learning, skills development and career transitions through synergies and initiatives between actors and organisations, also among the Sami population.

Through cohesion funds, the EU supports Upper Norrland in reducing its carbon emissions and in its transition to greener solutions, such as renewable energy, and local, flexible, and agile energy storage solutions.
Development of climate-smart transport will be supported by stimulating the transfer of transport from road to rail and shipping.

The programme aims to contribute to the effective and coordinated implementation of cohesion policy in Bulgaria, focusing on strengthening the administrative capacity of national authorities, beneficiaries and programme partners.

) initiative, which offers short-term work placements abroad and individual coaching.

The programme addresses the most important cross-border cooperation challenges along the borders of four Member States, in line with the three policy objectives and Interreg- specific objective outlined in cohesion policy 2021-2027.

Strategically, the programme will support new business development in many sectors in the region. Start-ups have the potential to create numerous jobs, and cross-border mobility and networks are considered vital to their success.

At the same time, the programme will address environmental issues, in particular biodiversity and climate change. Environmental challenges require all countries to accelerate the introduction of circular economy policies and to reduce demand for natural resources. Digitalisation can help extend product lifespans and increase waste recycling. The region’s environment suffers from eutrophication of the sea and the effects of harmful substances, including greenhouse gases.

The Central Baltic is a highly educated region, and the number of people completing tertiary education exceeds the EU-27 average. Employment rates are above average in all countries, but youth unemployment is generally higher than the overall rates. The programme will support the access of vulnerable groups to the labour market.

Public administrations in the Central Baltic countries face administrative, regulatory, language and cultural barriers. These stem from different national legislation, incompatible administrative processes, or the lack of common territorial planning. The programme identifies an urgent need for improving public sector capacity.

The programme aims at strengthening the Latvian-Estonian cooperation that is necessary to tackle the major challenges the cross-border territories face. Moreover, cooperation will develop the potential of an area rich in natural and cultural assets. It will also improve the quality of life for approximately two million people living in the area.
To boost the small-scale economy of the cross-border region, small businesses will receive support to innovate and find joint solutions for smart and green transformation.

The programme will enhance nature protection and biodiversity as well as green infrastructure, in particular in the urban environment. It will implement joint actions to reduce pollution and will develop innovative and sustainable strategies aimed at waste prevention and management in border areas.

EU support will also go to the development of sustainable and accessible tourism products and services. These will not only help the cross-border economy, they will also aim to improve social inclusion and encourage social innovation.

Furthermore, the programme will support local authorities and organisations to work on cross-border strategies and develop joint services to the benefit of citizens living in border areas. It will also bring together people in joint community events and initiatives to increase trust for future cooperation.

The programme aims to mitigate the consequences of climate change in the Mediterranean sea and its negative effects on all the territories bordering the basin and far beyond. The necessary challenge of the Green deal will also be accompanied by an effort of supervision, coordination, technical and political cooperation that will span the entire the Mediterranean basin.
Moreover, the programme aims to reinforce the potential for innovation that, with the exception of capitals and main cities, remains low across the region.

To reach these objectives, the programme has a strong climate and environment orientation. It contributes to the EU climate targets with 35% of the programme allocation and to environmental objectives - with 66% of its resources. More than 10% of the budget is devoted to tackling biodiversity issues.

The programme also plays an important role in the implementation of the Western Maritime Initiative as it shares parts of its cooperation area with the West Mediterranean area. It will allow involvement of partners beyond the programme area, thus creating links and activating synergies within and across the sea basin regions.

Finally, with the exception of Serbia, the programme area also covers the area of the Adriatic and Ionian Macro regional strategy (EUSAIR). Other Interreg programmes concerning the Adriatic Sea are expected to contribute to the Programme for the priorities related to the EUSAIR. Thus, the programme entails coordination and cooperation mechanisms to interact with other interreg programmes active in the MED area, capitalising on project outputs and results and increasing their territorial impact.

Such a cooperation, which allows neighbours like Turkey and Greece to sit around the same table and join forces on the implemention of common projects is rare and highly appreciated by all stakeholders.

Although geographically eligible, Russia was suspended from all cooperation and from this programme after its unprecedented and unjustified aggression against Ukraine. This geographic location has contributed to above-average economic growth. However, the area still experiences regional disparities: north-south, east-west, and between urban agglomerations and structurally weaker rural areas.

In addition, all regions are undergoing demographic changes. These trends are expected to continue. In this context, the long tradition of cross-border coordination and cooperation will continue. Focus will be placed on addressing common challenges to bring added value to the programme area.

The Italy-Austria cross-border cooperation programme is the only one within the Interreg family that follows the bottom-up approach of the Community Led Local Development. In the 2021-2027 programming period, the long tradition of cross-border cooperation in the programme area will be continued and thematically focused on the main challenges identified for the region.

The great cultural proximity between the two programme partners, the Austrian and the Bavarian regions, forms an important common basis. This proximity facilitates cross-border cooperation and contributes to a fundamental understanding of each other, which can mitigate many potential border-related obstacles to development.

Strategically, the programme promotes the positive positioning of the programme area in terms of economic growth and innovation and their strengthening through cooperation, while contributing to the twin transitions of green and digital transformation.
At the same time, it addresses environmental issues and challenges related to climate change.

Furthermore, the programme focuses on the important role of tourism in the programme area for economic development as a driver of employment. With its own tourism strategy, the programme focuses on sustainable and resilient tourism development to ensure the quality of life in the programme area.

Actions under these main priorities will be complemented by efforts to further reduce existing border obstacles. This should improve everyday life and cooperation in the border regions and facilitate the use of existing common potential.

programme_name: Programme ESF Plus 2021-2027 German Speaking Community of Belgium
programme_description: The ESF+ programme for the Belgian German-speaking community, also referred to as East Belgium (Ostbelgien), aims to make sure that jobseekers find work by developing skills employers need. In doing so, the programme contributes to reaching the national target of 80% employment and a participation rate of almost 61% of all adults in training by 2030.

ESF+ investments will tackle major labour-market challenges, such as demographic change and the green and digital transitions, which have resulted in a heightened risk of a shortage of skilled workers. The programme offers significant flexibility, supporting workers and jobseekers in their preferred language by enabling them to attend a bigger choice of training opportunities, including in neighboring Germany or in the Belgian regions of Wallonia and Flanders.

Measures funded by the ESF+ will also support the implementation of key social rights priorities by focusing on training and lifelong learning, gender equality, equal opportunities, active support for safe and adaptable employment and inclusion of vulnerable groups, such as persons with disabilities.

The programme will support career guidance or training courses for both employed persons and job seekers. ESF+ funding will also ease the transition between education and training and employment, and will promote entrepreneurship. Activities will develop qualifications and further training measures, facilitating (re)entry into the labour market for unemployed and long-term unemployed job seekers.

The ESF+ in East Belgium will support persons who face barriers to finding a job by providing specialised education and training – such as by increasing opportunities to engage in language and social-skills courses, or counselling and support for systematic (re)integration into the world of work.

Flexible education and training opportunities funded through the ESF+ in East Belgium will address skills shortages to meet the demands of the digital and green transitions. This could include training in IT or language development, as well as in new areas that boost the economy through green technologies, create sustainable industry or transport, or reduce pollution. Where there is an identified need as part of this transformation, ESF+ funding will also support further training for employees or process designers to secure and create new jobs in the region. Cross-border or cross-regional partnerships will be developed as projects of strategic importance, offering workers access to a wider range of skills.
Approximately 1 500 participants will be supported into work or training; Around 1 000 qualifications will be obtained thanks to the programme activities.

programme_description: The ESF+ Flanders programme will increase employment opportunities in the region – including for low-qualified people, newly-arrived migrants, persons with disabilities or other vulnerable groups that may face barriers to participating in both the labour market and wider society.

ESF+ activities in the region will also support vulnerable young people, promote skills development and increase engagement in lifelong learning.  The aim is to also increase inclusiveness and well-being at the workplace.

The programme will fund with priority measures that increase job opportunities and lead to employment for vulnerable people, such as young people, long-term unemployed, persons from a migrant background or persons with disabilities. The focus is on the provision of personalised support.
Actions under the priority for social inclusion will aim to help people with weak links to society to overcome obstacles for full participation and integration into the labour market when possible.

Under this priority the programme will address inequalities in the education and training system, preventing early school leaving and facilitating the transition between learning and working for at-risk young people. Furthermore, dedicated actions aim to increase participation in lifelong learning for employees as well as for those that are not in employment, focusing on green and digital skills.

The ESF+ investments in Flanders will also support ‘Workable work’, including through actions that aim to improve the inclusion and well-being of employees at the workplace. Measures as part of this priority will target at-risk employees who are experiencing high levels of stress or low motivation and will include training opportunities that ensure a better work-life balance.
The programme will also fund activities devoted to social innovation, strengthening the capacity of the Flemish labour-market institutions and services such as the public employment service.

programme_description: The Interreg Belgium-Netherlands programme covers almost all Flanders and South Netherlands which is a prosperous and densely populated part of Europe.

The area is a logistics hub where ports, rail, water and motorways intersect ensuring strong connectivity towards the interior of the European Union. In the border region, small and medium-sized enterprises are an economic engine, creating jobs and providing a wide range of products/services along the border.

Cooperation is focussed on applied research and innovation in SMEs with a strong societal impact.  The programme invests in the development of innovative products, services or processes addressing energy efficiency, renewable energy, integrated energy systems, climate change adaptation, the circular economy, biodiversity and air pollution. Societal impact is demonstrated through active participation and inclusion of citizens in projects that require behavioural change as part of the solution.

To address societal imbalances, the programme aims at improving cross-border access to information on job opportunities while  supporting vulnerable groups in accessing the labour market. This also includes the promotion of cross-border cooperation between educational institutions aimed at connecting vocational education to the labour market, through for example, dual or hybrid learning environments.

The Belgium-Netherlands programme also supports sustainable cross-border tourism, focussing on both hard and soft infrastructure investments. The latter includes training activities, organisation of traffic flows or sustainable site management.

The programme also focusses on removing border obstacles with the approval of two operations of strategic importance to pursue this objective. The programme will set up a Small Project Fund to address legal and ‘softer’ border bottlenecks and foster cross-border contacts through people-to-people actions.

A project is also being developed to initiate a cross-border knowledge and expertise centre between Flanders and the Netherlands on border obstacles and cross-border data. This centre will serve as a knowledge-building secretariat and a one-stop shop for resolving legal border bottlenecks.
The aim of the programme is to make a clear contribution to the green and digital transitions.

The programme will strengthen research and development activities, economic growth, and even better exploitation of research results through targeted innovation involving enterprises (in particular small businesses).
At the same time, it will address environmental issues and challenges related to climate change and the protection and preservation of nature and biodiversity.
It will also protect cultural heritage and promote tourism, intensifying investment in cross-border education and training.

Actions under these main priorities will be complemented by efforts to promote closer cooperation in legal and administrative matters and people-to-people actions to build trust to create a fully integrated border region.

The ESF+ Federal Food Aid Programme for Belgium aims at reducing poverty by supplying food to the country’s most vulnerable people, as well as through offering social support alongside the distribution of food. The programme will focus exclusively on these activities and build on experience gathered through the previous food aid programme for Belgium under the Fund for European Aid to the Most Deprived (FEAD).

Food will be made available free of charge to municipal social services and other accredited partner organisations for distribution to people at risk of poverty. To complement material assistance with social support, each organisation distributing food aid is required to direct people receiving food aid towards the municipal social services that offer a wider range of support, including social assistance, financial assistance and debt mediation.

Partner organisations will put in place additional accompanying measures, such as support in budget management, debt mediation and healthy nutrition advice. This extra support represents an important first step for the  most vulnerable people, prior to involving them in more active measures – often supported under other ESF+ programmes.
Addressing material deprivation

The ESF+ programme Wallonia - Brussels will support jobseekers of all ages into employment or self-employment, with a focus on creating opportunities for young people and those who are long-term unemployed. Dedicated measures will combat poverty and help people with disabilities to live independently, outside of specialised institutions.

The programme has been designed to address the socioeconomic challenges of Wallonia and Brussels. Both regions have a relatively high number of people who are in long-term unemployment, face barriers to labour-market integration or are at risk of poverty and social exclusion.

Projects funded under this programme priority will focus on getting unemployed or inactive persons of all ages into employment or self-employment, including people with low skills or from a migrant background. To achieve this, ESF+ funding will increase opportunities to gain or improve skills and competences, with particular attention paid to skills for the green economy.

A specific programme priority is dedicated to testing new ways of helping people out of long-term unemployment. The ‘Territoires Zéro Chômeurs de Longue Durée’ pilot project, for instance, advances local partnerships that identify services not currently offered by the labour market, giving long-term-unemployed individuals expanded opportunities to find a job.
The programme will assist vulnerable young people to successfully complete their education or training and will implement the
with increased employment opportunities for young people with little or no work experience.

The ESF+ will allocate significant resources to social inclusion under two dedicated priorities. People at risk of poverty will receive help, including to find housing, with debt management support to develop basic competences, to overcome obstacles that may prevent them from fully participating in society. When possible, this will also include assistance to get a job. Children living in poverty will be given access to activities and leisure activities they might be otherwise excluded from. Dedicated measures will support deinstitutionalisation of persons with disabilities and assist them to expand their autonomy and inclusion in the community, including through providing improved training and information for outreach workers and support staff.

Investments for competitiveness will concentrate on encouraging research, development, innovation. The region chose to dedicate its funds on digitalisation, especially for small and medium enterprises (SMEs). The impacts of both brexit and the recent sanitary crisis stand as a lesson learnt for the Flemish economy, which will benefit from EU support to build resilience to external shocks.
Concerning energy and climate change adaptation, funds will improve energy efficiency, renewable energy, and sustainable urban mobility.
Flanders invests a significant part of its programme in sustainable urban development. Local stakeholders, including provinces and cities will enjoy much autonomy in submitting eligible projects.

programme_description: The mission of ESPON is to deliver evidence, data and advice.  Given the main territorial challenges at stake and the EU policy framework, ESPON intends to support policy makers at all levels by providing territorial evidence and knowledge to inform policy responses to strengthen EU territories’ resilience and recovery of from crises by achieving a green transition to climate-neutral economies while ensuring just living conditions in all places.
With a total budget of EUR 60 Million , (EUR 48 Million EU funding) , the Programme will cover all 27 EU Member States in partnership with Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

ESPON research and activities are highly relevant for cohesion policy programming and implementation, and as part of the interregional programmes family it particularly contributes to cohesion policy effectiveness. In addition, key areas supported through research and evidence include  the European Green Deal, Just Transition and Recovery, the Territorial Agenda 2030 (TA2030) process and implementation.

ESPON supports these processes through policy briefs, territorial evidence reports, territorial monitoring tools and other dedicated studies and outreach events, both arranged on demand of respective ESPON member countries, European cooperation partners, and the relevant intergovernmental networks. ESPON also supports macro-regional strategies, sea-basin strategies, as done in the past, with data and monitoring tools and responding to ad-hoc support requests.

programme_name: ERDF Programme 2021-2027 of the Brussels Capital Region
programme_description: The programme aims to support sectors with a high social, environmental and economic impact for the region. To this end, funds will be devoted to promoting inclusive economic models, namely those that encourage the participation of more vulnerable people.

Among other interventions, like boosting Small and Medium Enterprises’ economic potential, the programme aims at filling existing gaps in innovation chains and developing the financial offer for innovation processes.

The funds encourage environmentally friendly approaches and the development of digital solutions. Such approach is set to make professional opportunities available, while facilitating citizens’ and businesses’ interactions with the administrations. Such actions are set to stimulate the region’s economic dynamism.

Through the ERDF, the EU also supports the region in its efforts to reduce energy emissions and to transit towards greener solutions. To this end, improving the energy performance of public buildings and of social housing will be crucial. In addition, the ERDF will help amplifying existing waste- and resource-recovery chains, along with supporting the development of high-quality green spaces for all citizens, notably in underprivileged neighbourhoods.

In line with the social profile of the region, the programme also helps to increase the offer of housing and accommodations for vulnerable categories. This action will accompany the improvement of the urban environment and the livability of low-income areas.

The ESF+ programme for the Brussels Capital Region will fund projects that aim to improve people’s access to quality employment and offer activation opportunities to all types of jobseekers. The measures supported through the programme will help people integrate into today’s labour market. Dedicated support will be offered to longer-term unemployed jobseekers, people with disabilities, young people, newly-arrived immigrants and persons dependent on social welfare.

The programme will support people who are furthest away from the job market, such as long-term unemployed people, young people not in employment, education or training, as well as groups at risk of social exclusion, including migrants, helping them find and maintain employment. A specific emphasis will be placed on improving access to the labour market for persons with disabilities.
In order to ensure better work-life balance and equal access to employment, access to childcare will be improved for (single-parent) families with young children.

The programme will support specifically young people through projects that facilitate the transition from education to the labour market, including by supporting additional training, internships and student placements. Projects funded by the programme will support persons at risk of social exclusion – such as newly-arrived immigrants and persons on social welfare – to help them better integrate into the labour market and society. Activities will include language training to strengthen reading, numeracy skills and evaluation and recognition of competencies and qualifications. Measures also include help with successfully approaching  potential employers – such as drafting a CV or motivation letters or preparing for job interviews.

Since the industrial revolution, North-West Europe has been at the vanguard of industrialisation and economic development in Europe. However, this century of growth came at a great cost: for the environment, for people, for territorial inequalities. The programme is looking for ways to contribute to compensate for such costs.

The overall aim of the programme and of its actions is to contribute to a balanced development across the North-West Europe programme area, regardless of the type of territory, helping to make it greener, more innovative, and more inclusive.

Through the programme, the EU supports the North-West Europe regions to be more resilient to climate change, to strengthen ecological connectivity, to reduce pollution and CO2 emissions, to transit towards greener solutions, such as renewable energy and circular economy. At the same time the EU will accompany both public and private players in the region while they develop their capacity for innovation capacity.

The programme contributes also to a more effective, inclusive, and quality labour market. In fact, it helps vulnerable groups, and it supports the emergence of available, accessible, inclusive, and resilient healthcare systems for all citizens.
Finally, it contributes to strengthen economic development, social inclusion and social innovation enhancing the role of culture and sustainable tourism.

The programme addresses the most important cooperation challenges along the South Baltic border, in line with the four policy objectives and the Interreg-specific objective defined in cohesion policy 2021-2027. The programme will focus on four priorities.
These are divided into a further seven specific objectives. Within this framework, the programme supports cross-border cooperation between public institutions, the private sector and civil society.

Strategically, the programme will promote digitisation and cooperation between SMEs and research institutions, and technology transfer to exploit the region’s economic potential. At the same time, it will address environmental issues and climate change. Particular attention will be paid to promoting renewable energy, sustainable water management and the transition to a circular and resource-efficient economy.
The programme will protect and promote cultural heritage and tourism. Actions will be complemented by closer cooperation between public authorities and stakeholders.
The programme will make a significant contribution to the implementation of the EU strategy for the Baltic Sea region.

programme_name: National programme for the ERDF in Denmark: Strong enterprises through innovation, digitalization and green transition
programme_description: Denmark wants to be a frontrunner regarding climate. Consequently, the programme’s main focus is on green transition and digitalisation of SMEs, while also addressing the socio-economic impacts of this transition on tourism related areas and small and medium sized towns.

The majority of the funding supports Danish SMEs by activities which include counselling and advice; networking and cooperation; improving their innovation capacity and competitiveness; green transition and internationalisation.
Furthermore the support will lead to increased co-operation between SMEs, public and semi-public bodies and allow them to develop and use new welfare technologies.
In Denmark the green transition goes hand-in-hand with innovation. The programme supports transition to circular economy with actions that help transform waste to raw materials.

Funding in the tourism sector aims to attract new enterprises and encourage existing SMEs to invest in the further development of the tourist destinations. Support to living town centres intends to boost investments and make them more viable and attractive. This would also include possible infrastructure investment that serve to address climate related challenges in these town centres.

programme_name: Green Technologies and Skills for a Just Transition
programme_description: Denmark’s Just Transition Fund covers two regions which have specific transition needs and challenges. These are North and South Jutland. The main focus is on Research and Development activities which will allow SMEs in these regions to adapt to the green transition. At the same time an available and qualified workforce is also necessary for the new skills required for the transition. This will entail intiative to provide the current workforce with new skills. To achieve this, Denmark has developed a network of local business “lighthouses” which support the need for R&D and activities related to the workforce.

The two regions have different focusses. North Jutland’s ambition is to capture, recycle and/or store C02 and to produce future green fuels and other products with captured C02 and hydrogen. South Jutland aims at expanding the country’s existing green energy strengths to develop, test and demonstrate the green technologies of the future such as integrated energy systems.

Enterprises will be supported with a view to broaden their green technology markets. They will be supported in their efforts to reduce their emissions and hire the workforce thar fits their goals. Business advice will also be available for these enterprises so they can make better use of materials and circular business models. At the same time businesses will receive support to invest in technologies that will allow them to become more carbon neutral.

The circular and green economies will benefit from Denmark undertaking activities such as developing brown biorefining (eg pyrolysis). Discovering or using synergies between technologies, demonstration and skills development in this field are clearly needed for the future. The CO2 hubs planned in North and South Jutland will aid in identifying barriers and ridding Denmark of bottlenecks may they be technological, knowledge or training-related. Moreover, aid will be key in developing Carbon Capture and Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) infrastrucutre.
Just Transition Fund

programme_name: A stronger Denmark through education and skills
programme_description: Denmark’s national ESF+ programme will promote a more inclusive and skilled labour force that meets the needs of a changing labour market. The ESF+ will invest in raising skills and expand vocational training and higher education to prepare the workforce for the jobs of tomorrow.

The programme will also develop the skills and competences needed for a fair and social labour market that is ready for the green and digital transitions. The programme will also aim to increase employment for people furthest away from the labour market, such as long-term unemployed people, young people and people from a migrant background, and promote social integration for citizens at risk of homelessness.

One of the priorities of the programme is to provide the Danish labour market with the right skills, with a strong focus on the green and digital transitions. Enhancing the quality of education, including vocational education and training and higher education, upskilling and reskilling, training and lifelong learning are therefore at the core of the programme activities. The ESF+ will support projects that can equip beneficiaries, especially small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs), with the competences, knowledge and skills needed to succeed during the green transition.

The ESF+ in Denmark will help to increase the start-up rates, growth and survival rates of companies. Strategic priorities supported by ESF+ investments will promote women entrepreneurs, who are currently underrepresented.
