programme_description: The programme area covers approximately 3 million km² of the northernmost parts of Europe and North Atlantic. Territories encompass Finland, Ireland, Sweden, Faroe Islands, Greenland, Iceland and Norway, which are defined by harsh climate, sparse population and extreme peripherality. Such characteristics makes many traditional forms of cooperation difficult.

The programme supports the twin green and digital transition as well as recovery from the pandemic in this vast region. This way, the northern and arctic communities can cooperate and work together in a way that recognises their specificities.

Through the ERDF, the EU supports the generation of attractive, competitive, and sustainable communities by harnessing innovation and digital solutions. Through these interventions, EU funds support the expansion the capacity for climate change adaptation and resource sufficiency, seizing the unique growth opportunities in the region - including supporting indigenous Sámi and Inuit cultures, livelihoods and entrepreneurship - while taking into account ecosystem-based approaches.

The programme aims also to strengthen the organisational capacity among the communities to make best use of cooperation opportunities, and to boost the programme’s role in developing transnational territorial cooperation in the Arctic.

The new Interreg VI-A Sweden-Finland-Norway (Aurora) programme merges the previous Interreg Nord and Interreg Botnia-Atlantica programmes. Its objective is to strengthen the area’s competitiveness, sustainability and attractiveness through social inclusion, digitalisation and the green transition.

The programme area is vast, being sparsely populated in the north, and more populated in the south. Although this poses certain challenges, the vast distances and cold climate provide opportunities for testing know-how and technology in Arctic conditions. Areas with potential include space technology, energy technology, hydropower, bioeconomy, the circular economy, and smart food. There is also enormous potential for innovative health services, in particular e-health.
The programme will support the green transition, with a focus on climate change adaptation, protection of nature and biodiversity, and sustainable urban mobility.

A specific feature of this programme is the Sápmi sub-area. The Sámi are the indigenous people of Finland, Norway, Sweden and north-western Russia. They have a common cultural and linguistic bond and a common identity that is, by definition, without (national) borders.
Interreg has been very important for Sámi cooperation to preserve cultural heritage, including
Sámi traditional handicraft, and Sámi languages. Interreg Aurora will continue to support these important topics, along with Sámi entrepreneurship and innovation based on traditional knowledge.

The overall objective of the Programme is to improve the living conditions and the economic development of cross-border communities. EU funds will foster cross-border cooperation supporting small businesses. This objective will be carried out while focusing on environmental issues, such as restoring biodiversity and the sustainable use of the area’s cultural and natural heritage. Significant support has also been devoted to improving local mobility through modernizing road and rail connections.

by supporting cross-border initiatives to valorise cultural, historical, and non-tangible heritage of the region. This will equally benefit community-building and cultural activities with positive effects for the local community’s quality of life and social inclusion.

As regards the rail investments, a significant part of the projects will focus on modernization or reconstruction of railway stations and stops. The roads investments will have a strong focus on closing gaps on the important transport (TEN-T) connections to allow people and goods to quickly get to other places in the European Union.

Urban transport projects such as transferring the busiest bus lines to electric traction, constructing new and upgrading existing tram and trolleybus lines will help to increase the attractiveness of these more environmentally friendly ways of travelling.

The programme will also support measures that will improve the intermodal freight transport. In line with smart specialisation strategies, the funds will support Finland's innovation systems and master its green and digital transition. The programme will improve research, development and innovation. Investments will also foster digitalisation, accelerate small and medium-sized businesses’ growth and increase productivity. The main objectives of the programme are to promote the growth and competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Thus, the programme sets out to improve access to employment for all jobseekers, concomitantly promoting lifelong learning, especially in the case of reskilling and upskilling opportunities.

As regards the SMEs the Åland programme supports stimulating business creation while strengthening the opportunities for innovation and development of established enterprises. Furthermore, the programme strengthens competitiveness, increases productivity and supports internationalisation.

A key challenge for the programme is to guarantee access to employment for all jobseekers, in particular for young people or long-term unemployed. Moreover, some of its key features include social economy and the promotion of self employment.
Lifelong learning, in particular when it exploits flexible upskilling and reskilling opportunities for all, are the main focus of the programme's ambition to revitalise the region's workforce.

Such increase in productivity will allow to improve their position in global value chains and reap benefits from emerging business opportunities, thus stimulating the creation and development of new innovative firms.

At the same time, the programme contributes to the development of key skills.  Other complementary support instruments (in particular the Recovery and Resilience Facility, the Modernisation Fund, the Fair Transition OP or the Union’s Horizon Europe and Digital Europe programmes) will ensure the transition to a sustainable and digital economy.

Under the policy objectives entitled “A more competitive and smarter Europe” and “A greener, low-carbon transition to a carbon-neutral economy and a resilient Europe” a range of sub-actions will compound the above-mentioned instruments.
Awarding funds as financial instruments, the programme is a pioneer in Czechia and holds the second highest percentage of climate related expenses among the programmes.

The programme addresses the most important cross-border cooperation challenges along the borders of four Member States, in line with the three policy objectives and Interreg- specific objective outlined in cohesion policy 2021-2027.

Strategically, the programme will support new business development in many sectors in the region. Start-ups have the potential to create numerous jobs, and cross-border mobility and networks are considered vital to their success.

At the same time, the programme will address environmental issues, in particular biodiversity and climate change. Environmental challenges require all countries to accelerate the introduction of circular economy policies and to reduce demand for natural resources. Digitalisation can help extend product lifespans and increase waste recycling. The region’s environment suffers from eutrophication of the sea and the effects of harmful substances, including greenhouse gases.

The Central Baltic is a highly educated region, and the number of people completing tertiary education exceeds the EU-27 average. Employment rates are above average in all countries, but youth unemployment is generally higher than the overall rates. The programme will support the access of vulnerable groups to the labour market.

Public administrations in the Central Baltic countries face administrative, regulatory, language and cultural barriers. These stem from different national legislation, incompatible administrative processes, or the lack of common territorial planning. The programme identifies an urgent need for improving public sector capacity.
The aim of the programme is to make a clear contribution to the green and digital transitions.

The programme will strengthen research and development activities, economic growth, and even better exploitation of research results through targeted innovation involving enterprises (in particular small businesses).
At the same time, it will address environmental issues and challenges related to climate change and the protection and preservation of nature and biodiversity.
It will also protect cultural heritage and promote tourism, intensifying investment in cross-border education and training.

Actions under these main priorities will be complemented by efforts to promote closer cooperation in legal and administrative matters and people-to-people actions to build trust to create a fully integrated border region.

The Comenius multi-fund programme aims to enhance skills and knowledge acquisition and prepare people from all generations for the green and digital transformation of the European economy and society. It supports the modernisation of the educational system to make it more fair and accessible.

Specific attention is given to children with special educational needs who will receive help from pedagogical assistants, psychologists and other support staff. Equality and inclusion in education would enable all children to reach their full potential.

The Comenius programme invests in fostering research and in developing excellence, in the fields of infrastructure and of human resources. The programme places special emphasis helping qualified women make the best use of their skills. It gives strategic importance to connecting the Czech research and innovation community to the ‘European Open Science Cloud’ – an initiative to promote open science. This and other projects under Comenius programme will support better exploitation of research results in the economy and society – for the benefit of all.

The programme will create and develop an open education system that will build the skills and qualifications needed for the smart, multidisciplinary and interconnected environments of the fourth industrial revolution Measures under Comenius programme will provide relevant educational content for lifelong learning. This will ensure that when leaving school young people are able to adapt to the challenges of a dynamic and constantly changing labour market.

Aligned with the ambition of Comenius programme, the Recovery and Resilience Facility will supply digital equipment and education courses to address the digital gap in schools that are lagging behind.

The

programme partners identified the transition to a greener and more social Europe as their main common challenge and opportunity. Thus, common climate risks, and the common biodiversity features are specifically addressed in the programme: 43% of the financial resources are allocated to climate objectives, while 23% of the financial resources are dedicated to biodiversity.

The programme, will support the Joint Action Plans for the prevention of risks and protection against disasters (e.g. floods, fires, desertification, coastal erosion, drought). The Plans include investments in research and innovation networks, exchange of good practices, know-how, etc.. Building on previous experiences of cross-border cooperation will be key in developing solutions and achieve results in the area of intervention. These joint action plans will mitigate the vulnerability of disaster prevention/management systems, thus improving resilience to climate change.

To contribute to the protection of the maritime environment, the programme will support actions to collect maritime data through a WEBGIS platform and provide it to a wide range of user groups (citizens, public institutions, researchers).

Tourism and culture are two important sectors for the programme area and cooperation brings added value to a number of fields that the programme will support. Actions will promote alternative forms of tourism, building on common cultural heritage and identity.
Furthermore, bulding on previous results, the programme will enure that cultural and tourist sites are accessible to vulnerable groups, including persons with disabilities.

The programme area is confronted with large flows of migrants, therefore the programme capitalises on previous experience to support an integrated system of maritime border surveillance, improving the maritime and aerial surveillance of the cross border area.

The Programme will significantly support job creation, business competitiveness, economic growth and sustainable development, and will improve citizens’ overall quality of life through investments from the ERDF, the Cohesion Fund , the Just Transition Fund and the European Social Fund.

The Thalia Programme will support research, innovation and development and SMEs’ growth, based on an improved smart specialisation strategy, building on the current priority areas on energy, tourism, agriculture and food, structured environment-construction, transport-shipping, health, the environment and information and communication technologies. Furthermore, it will put emphasis on actions that will interconnect the national R&I system with the economy, the business world and society as a whole. Cyprus’ low ranking on all indicators of DESI (Digital Economy and Society Index) will be addressed through investments in measures related to digitalisation of companies and public services.

The green conversion of Cyprus will be achieved through significant investments in energy efficiency, the reduction of carbon emissions and the penetration of RES, combined with renewed efforts to reach the applicable targets for waste and water management. Furthermore, the programme deals with actions on adaptation to climate change and actions in habitat protection and restoration within the Natura 2000 Networks. Regarding investments in circular economy, a key priority is to promote actions for source sorting, separate collection, reuse and recycling to reduce landfill waste.

The development of sustainable public transport will be pursued through the deployment of an electric bus network and active mobility such as walking and cycling. The Programme marks a shift away from the concentration on road investments in favour of multi-modal and more sustainable modes of transport. Integrated Territorial Investments will further improve the quality of life in urban and non-urban areas in Cyprus, ensuring maximum utilization of the growth potential of cities and non-urban areas, successfully tackling social challenges, stimulating growth, liveability and innovation.

Moreover, the Cypriot Territorial Just Transition Programme constitutes a commitment to accelerate Cyprus’ energy transition process towards the 2030 and 2050 targets. The envisaged actions of the plan will strengthen the energy transmission and distribution system and increase storage capacity that will subsequently facilitate RES penetration. Furthermore, it will support measures for SMEs to apply new technologies and will also empower Human Capital through education and training actions, including through the creation of a new Green Technical School in Nicosia.

Promotion of social cohesion is supported through investments to support the labour market, foster skills and strengthen social cohesion. Programmed actions include outreach, consulting and guidance actions for young people, the modernisation of Public Employment Services, and the promotion of flexible working arrangements. The European Social Fund + will also invest in the development of technical Vocational Education and Training and in new initiatives such as Individual Learning Accounts and the ALMA initiative, in line with the European Skills Agenda and the reinforced Youth Guarantee. Additionally it will provide significant support for the restructuring of social welfare services and actions in line with the European Child Guarantee, such as affordable early childhood education and care and access to free school lunches for deprived pupils. Lastly, Social innovation actions include the provision of Home care services for persons with disabilities.

The purpose is to promote integrated sustainable development in cities, improve city’s policies and improve the effectiveness of Cohesion policy in cities.

Its supports the delivery of key principles of sustainable urban development on the ground, such as good governance, integrated and place-based approaches, all making the link to the urban and territorial dimension of Cohesion policy and to its minimum requirements as per the 2021-2027 regulatory provisions.

The Programme will cover the EU 27 Member States, Norway, Switzerland as well as some countries benefitting from the Instrument for Pre-Accession (IPA) such as Albania, Montenegro, Serbia, Republic of North Macedonia, and Bosnia-Herzegovina.The URBACT programme covers the entire territory of the participating countries and is open to cities of all sizes. programme_name: (Interreg VI-B) NEXT Mediterranean Sea Basin (NEXT MED)
programme_description: The programme fosters fair and sustainable cooperation between 7 EU Member States and 8 partner countries in the Southern Neighbourhood (i.e. Algeria, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, Tunisia and Türkiye). The participating countries jointly developed the programme based on the principle of equal footing. There is a strong and shared understanding that many of today’s challenges in the Mediterranean Sea Basin are common across the countries in the region and that there is an urgent need to find common solutions.

The largest part of EU funding (42%) will be allocated to projects that address climate change and environmental challenges. these include energy efficiency measures, sustainable water use, climate change adaptation, circular economy as well as risk prevention.

Secondly, the programme aims to create a more competitive and smarter Mediterranean by providing support and improving conditions for SMEs. Such actions should pave the way for greater internationalisation, transnational research-business cooperation as well as reducing disparities and gaps in research and innovation across the Mediterranean.

The third aim is to foster a more social and inclusive Mediterranean by providing better quality and access to education and training. This will concern young people and disadvantaged groups in particular. Health represents a key factor in the reduction of economic and social inequalities. Therefore, project partners will focus on developing innovative digital and services that improve the delivery and efficiency of health services.

Finally, the programme aims to improve the cooperation governance across the Mediterranean through a number of tools, including joint capacity building actions for public authorities as well as transnational cooperation between citizens, civil society actors and public institutions based on bottom-up and participatory approaches.
The programme has a particular focus on young people and it will ensure a strong system of complementarities and synergies with other EU funding streams operating in the Mediterranean.

The programme aims to mitigate the consequences of climate change in the Mediterranean sea and its negative effects on all the territories bordering the basin and far beyond. The necessary challenge of the Green deal will also be accompanied by an effort of supervision, coordination, technical and political cooperation that will span the entire the Mediterranean basin.
Moreover, the programme aims to reinforce the potential for innovation that, with the exception of capitals and main cities, remains low across the region.

To reach these objectives, the programme has a strong climate and environment orientation. It contributes to the EU climate targets with 35% of the programme allocation and to environmental objectives - with 66% of its resources. More than 10% of the budget is devoted to tackling biodiversity issues.

The programme also plays an important role in the implementation of the Western Maritime Initiative as it shares parts of its cooperation area with the West Mediterranean area. It will allow involvement of partners beyond the programme area, thus creating links and activating synergies within and across the sea basin regions.

Finally, with the exception of Serbia, the programme area also covers the area of the Adriatic and Ionian Macro regional strategy (EUSAIR). Other Interreg programmes concerning the Adriatic Sea are expected to contribute to the Programme for the priorities related to the EUSAIR. Thus, the programme entails coordination and cooperation mechanisms to interact with other interreg programmes active in the MED area, capitalising on project outputs and results and increasing their territorial impact.

The programme supports the implementation of the EU Strategy for the Danube Region (EUSDR), fostering transnational actions across fourteen countries, including nine EU member states and five partner countries.
The programme region is characterized by its cultural diversity and territorial and socio-economic disparities. Therefore the Interreg programme aims at creating a shared ‘Danubian’ space.

The first objective of the programme is to make the Danube region smarter, with projects devoted to enhancing innovation and technology transfer. This will require efforts to develop new skills for industrial transition and smart specialisation. In addition the programme contributes to increase the use of renewable energies, preserve the biodiversity with ecological corridors and support joint actions on management of risks related to climate change.

Moreover, the programme allows EU Member States to work together with candidates and potential candidate countries, to reach common goals and to improve standards for an efficient public administration.

The Employment + programme supports fair, green and digital transitions by upskilling and reskilling people already in employment, as well as those who are currently not working. The programme focuses on improving the gender balance so as to develop an inclusive and resilient labour market. It supports better living conditions for people at risk of poverty, integration of Roma and third-country nationals, expanded availability of social services and improved access to health services across the country.

The programme creates employment opportunities for jobseekers who have difficulties finding or keeping a job – including older people, people with disabilities, or individuals with low skills. The new
(ALMA) initiative will help disadvantaged young people to integrate into the labour market with short work placements abroad and individual coaching.

Support for children is a strategic priority. Childcare availability for children under three years of age will be increased, enabling their parents to participate in the labour market, and further promoting work-life balance. Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are also supported to adapt to ongoing challenges and increase their competitiveness.

Special attention will be given to promoting social inclusion measures, supporting a variety of social services, stepping up coordination between health and social care and these services’ accessibility for persons in need. This funding will support social enterprises and help people in difficult situations – such as those at risk of becoming homeless. The transformation of institutional facilities into outpatient and community-based services will help persons with disabilities to live more independently in their preferred environment.

The programme will support measures promoting social innovation. Activities will focus on the development of innovative approaches to advance gender equality, employment and social inclusion, such as the enhancement of measures aimed at raising awareness of change, projects promoting skills building and using public assets in novel innovative ways.

The programme will support projects offering food and material assistance, as well as measures for social and labour market inclusion. It will also expand school lunch programmes for children at risk of social exclusion.

Strategically, the programme will focus on addressing important cross-border needs that may not be included in national development priorities and are therefore not covered by national programmes. In this context, it will provide specific approaches and mechanisms, through the small projects fund, to promote local development.
Cross-border cooperation and jointly addressing challenges increases the area’s potential, mainly in education, environment and tourism.

The importance of cross-border cooperation lies in the implementation of activities which contribute to regional development. In this context, the following have been identified as key programme areas:

The programme addresses the most important cross-border cooperation challenges along the Saxony-Czechia border, in line with the four policy objectives and Interreg-specific objective of cohesion policy 2021-2027. The programme will focus on four priorities. These are divided into a further seven specific objectives. Within this framework, the programme supports cross-border cooperation between public institutions, the private sector and civil society.

Strategically, the programme will promote cooperation between SMEs and research institutions, and technology transfer on both sides of the border to exploit the region’s economic potential. It will simultaneously address environmental issues, in particular biodiversity and climate change. It will protect and promote cultural heritage and tourism and increase investment in cross-border education and training.
Actions will be complemented by greater legal and administrative cooperation and people-to people projects, to build trust and create an integrated border region.

The new programme aims for a central Europe with less social and economic disparities, one which cooperates to become smarter, greener, and better connected. Its mission is to bring regions and cities together beyond borders to find fitting solutions for their citizens in a fair and equal way.

The chosen priorities include economic transition processes, climate change, and the long-term socio-economic consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic. The programme supports businesses to become more innovative; and communities - climate-neutral and resilient to climate change risks. It also fosters ideas on how to improve transport connections of rural and peripheral regions in central Europe.

In practice, the programme brings together public organisations, the private sector and civil society and finances transnational projects, which develop, test and implement solutions that are urgently needed to make central Europe more resilient and attractive. The programme supports these partnerships also with guidance and knowledge.

The Just Transition Programme intends to mitigate the adverse effects of the transition process to a climate-neutral economy in the most affected territories in Czech Republic. It covers three regions - Karlovarský kraj, Ústecký kraj a Moravskoslezký kraj.
The programme will finance economic diversification and modernization. The social dimension is also an important pillar of the intervention logic.

Half of the project allocation is planned for the operations of strategic importance. Those should be projects with significant transformational benefits for the regions. Operations of strategic importance are complex projects with different focus (employment, education, research, regeneration of brownfields, etc.).

Other type of planned interventions are overreaching projects (group of projects). The beneficiary will be the regional authorities that will administer the aid provided to small projects in the regions. It will provide administrative simplification for small-scale projects (aid of less than EUR 200 000).

In addition there will be thematic calls in the area of land rehabilitation and re-use after mining, support of SMEs, RDI and digital solutions, re-skilling, up-skilling and interventions in renewable energy sources including energy communities and circular economy.

The programme area covers approximately 3 million km² of the northernmost parts of Europe and North Atlantic. Territories encompass Finland, Ireland, Sweden, Faroe Islands, Greenland, Iceland and Norway, which are defined by harsh climate, sparse population and extreme peripherality. Such characteristics makes many traditional forms of cooperation difficult.

The programme supports the twin green and digital transition as well as recovery from the pandemic in this vast region. This way, the northern and arctic communities can cooperate and work together in a way that recognises their specificities.

Through the ERDF, the EU supports the generation of attractive, competitive, and sustainable communities by harnessing innovation and digital solutions. Through these interventions, EU funds support the expansion the capacity for climate change adaptation and resource sufficiency, seizing the unique growth opportunities in the region - including supporting indigenous Sámi and Inuit cultures, livelihoods and entrepreneurship - while taking into account ecosystem-based approaches.

The programme aims also to strengthen the organisational capacity among the communities to make best use of cooperation opportunities, and to boost the programme’s role in developing transnational territorial cooperation in the Arctic.
The Programme offers more than EU funding. It brings together cultures, perspectives and expertise to pool the best ideas and find joint solutions for the Baltic Sea region.

It creates opportunities for organisations to connect and work together regardless of borders. With the Programme support, transnational cooperation projects drive the transition to a green and resilient region under 4 priority that encompass:

The Programme is demand-driven and supports public authorities in meeting the needs of their target audiences, specifically, companies and communities. It puts the emphasis on transferring knowledge and bringing new solutions to use for the benefit of the people around the Baltic Sea.
On a macro-regional level, the Programme helps implement the objectives of the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region.

The Interreg Sweden-Norway cross-border programme supports the green transition, circular economy, the creation of a functional border region, and initiatives to make the region an attractive and sustainable place in which to live.

Nordic countries have a long tradition of cooperation and integration. The Interreg Sweden-Norway programme covers five Swedish and three Norwegian regions that encompass mountains, forests, rivers and lakes, some of which form part of  Natura 2000 sites. Although it is largely rural, there are also urban areas and agglomerations, particularly in the south.

The programme will support regional innovation systems and create cross-border networks in priority areas. Cross-border cooperation will encourage the development of larger innovation networks and bigger markets for industries, innovation hubs and businesses.
The programme supports innovations and joint solutions for welfare services in sparsely populated areas.
Support is also provided for development of a circular economy and cross-border preparedness to climate change.
A general population decline, together with an ageing population and emigration, requires investment in education and employment, to create opportunities for people in the border region.

The new Interreg VI-A Sweden-Finland-Norway (Aurora) programme merges the previous Interreg Nord and Interreg Botnia-Atlantica programmes. Its objective is to strengthen the area’s competitiveness, sustainability and attractiveness through social inclusion, digitalisation and the green transition.

The programme area is vast, being sparsely populated in the north, and more populated in the south. Although this poses certain challenges, the vast distances and cold climate provide opportunities for testing know-how and technology in Arctic conditions. Areas with potential include space technology, energy technology, hydropower, bioeconomy, the circular economy, and smart food. There is also enormous potential for innovative health services, in particular e-health.
The programme will support the green transition, with a focus on climate change adaptation, protection of nature and biodiversity, and sustainable urban mobility.

A specific feature of this programme is the Sápmi sub-area. The Sámi are the indigenous people of Finland, Norway, Sweden and north-western Russia. They have a common cultural and linguistic bond and a common identity that is, by definition, without (national) borders.
Interreg has been very important for Sámi cooperation to preserve cultural heritage, including
Sámi traditional handicraft, and Sámi languages. Interreg Aurora will continue to support these important topics, along with Sámi entrepreneurship and innovation based on traditional knowledge.

The programme addresses the most important cross-border cooperation challenges along the borders of four Member States, in line with the three policy objectives and Interreg- specific objective outlined in cohesion policy 2021-2027.

Strategically, the programme will support new business development in many sectors in the region. Start-ups have the potential to create numerous jobs, and cross-border mobility and networks are considered vital to their success.

At the same time, the programme will address environmental issues, in particular biodiversity and climate change. Environmental challenges require all countries to accelerate the introduction of circular economy policies and to reduce demand for natural resources. Digitalisation can help extend product lifespans and increase waste recycling. The region’s environment suffers from eutrophication of the sea and the effects of harmful substances, including greenhouse gases.

The Central Baltic is a highly educated region, and the number of people completing tertiary education exceeds the EU-27 average. Employment rates are above average in all countries, but youth unemployment is generally higher than the overall rates. The programme will support the access of vulnerable groups to the labour market.

Public administrations in the Central Baltic countries face administrative, regulatory, language and cultural barriers. These stem from different national legislation, incompatible administrative processes, or the lack of common territorial planning. The programme identifies an urgent need for improving public sector capacity.
The programme aims at supporting Sweden’s efforts to be climate neutral by 2045 and to alleviate the socio-economic impact of the transition.

Through the JTF, the EU will help the Swedish industry achieve climate neutrality, while maintaining competitiveness and sustaining economic and employment levels. As industrial emissions account for 32% of Sweden’s total greenhouse gas emissions, the transformation of the steel, mineral and metals industry, main greenhouse emitters, will have important socio-economic consequences. The JTF will help alleviate this impact by investing in research and innovation and in the retraining and reskilling of workers.

Because of the scale of the decarbonisation challenge, the JTF will also support targeted investments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in activities covered by the Emissions Trading System, such as steel and cement production. These investments are essential to maintain jobs in these sectors and will contribute to reducing CO2 emissions at regional, national and, by extension, global level if emissions targets from production and solutions are exported

The trilateral Sweden-Denmark-Norway border area is highly integrated, with small linguistic obstacles, large similarities among institutions and welfare systems, high innovation capacity and many universities. The programme area has almost 11 million inhabitants and is the most population-dense Nordic region. It is home to two capitals: Copenhagen (Denmark) and Oslo (Norway), along with other important cities such as Gothenburg and Malmö in Sweden, and Aarhus in Denmark.

Although the region already has strong innovation capacity, EU funds will support innovations for the green transition and sustainable development, as well as  stronger support systems for innovation.
The programme will test renewable energy solutions and create joint investment plans for renewable energy.

, with an established cross-border commuting network, requires integrated, sustainable transport systems. EU funds will support further integration and solutions to border obstacles related to employment, taxes and pension systems.

The ESF+ and ERDF Social Inclusion and Dignity Programme of Romania aims to improve essential social services for all, focusing on people from disadvantaged groups and people living in rural areas. The programme tackles the root causes of social disadvantages and inequality, providing significant financing for improving health, access to education and social services.

EU funding in Romania promotes social enterprises, support services and basic material assistance for vulnerable groups, including persons with disabilities, long-term unemployed, Roma and homeless people. The programme also implements the
by providing material, education and social aid to disadvantaged children and their families.
Programme activities will make the principles of the

a reality, working to achieve Romania’s 2030 social targets for increasing the country’s employment rate to nearly 75% and the number of adults in training every year to over 17%, while reducing the number of people at risk of poverty by over 2.5 million.

Access to health, social and educational services will be improved, thanks to EU investments in integrated community centres in rural areas. Measures will focus on responding to the needs of vulnerable groups, notably Roma people, including through the involvement of health or educational mediators. In addition, local action groups’ strategies for community-led development in rural areas and marginalised urban areas will contain targeted measures to address integration needs of local communities.

Dedicated measures will support children at risk of poverty and family re-integration, also through the development of specialised services, including tailor-made training for staff supporting children with behavioural challenges. Multifunctional sport and culture centres will be created for children from remote or disadvantaged areas.

Investments will ensure social housing is available for those in need. People living in informal settlements, which include unregulated or unsafe accommodation, will also benefit from integrated support measures, based on specific needs that are identified case by case.

The programme will also develop integrated services for social support and increase the financing for hiring specialised staff in rural areas. Promotion of social enterprises is also a priority in rural areas, where the programme will build and strengthen partnerships between local stakeholders to grow the social economy.

The multifund Social Inclusion and Dignity Programme will invest in an innovative partnership scheme between enterprises, non-governmental organisations and other stakeholders that will work to expand support for persons with disabilities. The provision of assistive technologies, personalised counselling and adaptive education schemes will promote autonomy and deinstitutionalisation and help persons with disabilities with opportunities to find jobs.

Funds will also enhance support for older people in vulnerable situations. Living conditions for individuals in social care will be improved, with specific attention given to meeting the long-term care needs of persons with reduced mobility and autonomy. Training offers to support the upskilling of workers in the healthcare and long-term care sectors will help tackle territorial disparities.

EU investments under the programme will also contribute to the integration of people from a migrant background, for both adults and children. Other vulnerable groups, such as survivors of domestic violence and human trafficking, persons released from prison, homeless people and victims of addiction will also benefit from specialised services, including temporary accommodation and specialised counselling. Staff providing these services will be supported through dedicated training.
The programme also allocates funding for material aid to vulnerable groups, including food and hot meals to children and care packages to newborns.

The investments focus on reducing the innovation gap with the rest of EU through increased private-sector R&I, incentivising academia-business collaboration, supporting the competitiveness of SMEs and digitalisation of public administration.

Targeted measures aim to boost the innovation and competitiveness of enterprises, including through creation of a national entrepreneurship hub for start-ups. Actions enhancing knowledge and technology transfer will strengthen academia-business collaboration.

The creation of thematic public-private consortia and support for national projects in advanced technologies aims to reduce fragmentation in R&I and will benefit all Romanian regions. Knowledge hubs will be created for smart specialisation, the industrial transition, and entrepreneurship.

The programme endeavors to achieve a resilient and connected cross-border region where sustainable development underpins economic growth, protects biodiversity, and ensures the social well-being of all inhabitants. The programme envisages joint cross-border actions to understand new needs and threats and improve the resilience and adaptability of people, organisations, and communities, by making the region greener and digital.

The main aim of the programme is to address environmental challenges linked to climate change and to the protection of nature and biodiversity. The programme will support preparation for and response to climate change in the cross-border area.

Support will be given to cross-border pilot activities for introducing and managing green infrastructure. It will protect and promote cultural heritage and tourism. This will include support for the diversification of services, in line with the emerging needs of tourists/visitors, by increasing investment in cross-border education and training.
Local SMEs will receive help in improving their competitiveness by adapting to the digital transition and supporting the green transition, especially in tourism.

The programme seeks to involve residents in finding solutions to social and territorial issues. In light of the COVID-19 pandemic, building trust and a positive mind-set, and having residents take responsibility for a better future in the cross-border region, is a must.

The programme supports the implementation of the EU Strategy for the Danube Region (EUSDR), fostering transnational actions across fourteen countries, including nine EU member states and five partner countries.
The programme region is characterized by its cultural diversity and territorial and socio-economic disparities. Therefore the Interreg programme aims at creating a shared ‘Danubian’ space.

The first objective of the programme is to make the Danube region smarter, with projects devoted to enhancing innovation and technology transfer. This will require efforts to develop new skills for industrial transition and smart specialisation. In addition the programme contributes to increase the use of renewable energies, preserve the biodiversity with ecological corridors and support joint actions on management of risks related to climate change.

Moreover, the programme allows EU Member States to work together with candidates and potential candidate countries, to reach common goals and to improve standards for an efficient public administration.

During development of the programme strategy, attention was paid to making links with the EU Strategy for the Adriatic and Ionian Region (EUSAIR).

One of the key results is a facility to help SMEs active in the blue economy, and that have a high growth potential that can be realised through innovation and skills development. This would be achieved through cooperation between SMEs/start-ups and by reducing the bureaucratic burden. The support will combine grants, access to services, and coaching.
The Adriatic-Ionian area aligns with the perimeter of the EU strategy of the Adriatic-Ionian Region (EUSAIR), embracing a unique mix of EU partner countries, Western Balkans and third countries.

The programme will facilitate the conditions for strong effective cooperation and good relations among partner countries. It will provide a constructive contribution to the EU enlargement process, reduce disparities and improve social cohesion with non-EU countries, as well as supporting the implementation of EUSAIR as such.

The programme aims at addressing the challenges that the countries of the Adriatic-Ionian region share. These range from the safeguard of biodiversity and climate change to sustainable transport. By way of innovative methods the programme will act as a pivotal instrument for the identification of common solutions and it will contribute to making the region smarter, greener and stronger in the face of economic shocks.
Its main objectives are:

The programme addresses the most important cooperation challenges along the South Baltic border, in line with the four policy objectives and the Interreg-specific objective defined in cohesion policy 2021-2027. The programme will focus on four priorities.
These are divided into a further seven specific objectives. Within this framework, the programme supports cross-border cooperation between public institutions, the private sector and civil society.

Strategically, the programme will promote digitisation and cooperation between SMEs and research institutions, and technology transfer to exploit the region’s economic potential. At the same time, it will address environmental issues and climate change. Particular attention will be paid to promoting renewable energy, sustainable water management and the transition to a circular and resource-efficient economy.
The programme will protect and promote cultural heritage and tourism. Actions will be complemented by closer cooperation between public authorities and stakeholders.
The programme will make a significant contribution to the implementation of the EU strategy for the Baltic Sea region.

Croatia's ESF+ Efficient Human Resources Programme will focus on creating employment opportunities and upskilling of people, modernising education and promoting lifelong learning and improving the matching of education and training systems to meet employers' needs. The programme will also promote social inclusion, as well as invest in healthcare and long-term care.

Projects funded under the programme will modernise and improve education programmes, from early childhood to higher education. Investments will also focus on adult learning and training, including lifelong learning of teachers and staff of educational institutions.

The ESF+ will encourage the expansion of social services in consideration of local needs, including the requirements for providing accessible, affordable and quality long-term care for persons with limited autonomy and with disabilities. The most deprived and those at risk of social exclusion, especially children, will benefit from dedicated measures.
ESF+ support in these policy areas will go hand in hand with ongoing reforms and EU investments under the Recovery and Resilience Plan.

The programme will implement active labour market policies including traineeships, support for employment and self-employment. The focus will be on helping vulnerable groups of people and women to integrate into the labour market.
Youth employment support is a key priority of the programme, which implements the

. Young people will be integrated into the labour market through new opportunities, such as transnational work mobility for disadvantaged young people, with a focus on supporting those who are not in employment, education or training through measures including the new
(Aim, Learn, Master, Achieve) initiative.

The programme will invest in re-integrating the unemployed, as well as supporting the continued career development of employed people with specific measures designed for both groups. Individual learning accounts will be introduced to encourage lifelong learning for better jobs.

ESF+ will support education reform by adapting curricula to match labour market needs and skills mapping, as well as forecasting and applying the Croatian qualification framework. Activities will also support whole-day schooling in primary schools, which can help improve children’s wellbeing, enhance their social skills and improve learning results.

The offer of vocational Education and Training (VET) will be expanded and enhanced by developing new methodologies, curricula and qualifications aligned with the Croatian Qualifications Framework. Activities will also promote further empowerment of regional VET competence centres and strengthening of work-based learning systems for vocational professions. Vulnerable pupils will be a particular focus of support through measures such as individual teaching assistants and professional communication mediators for children with disabilities. International exchanges will also be enhanced for students in tertiary education, with the development of high-quality digital education content and support for the training of young researchers.

ESF+ puts a particular emphasis on up- and reskilling the Croatian workforce to meet labour shortages and to adapt to new challenges of the green and digital transitions. Boosting adult learning is particularly important due to its low up-take in Croatia so far. The ESF+ programme will invest in building blocks for developing individual learning accounts.

Projects supported by the programme will fund community-based services to prevent social exclusion of vulnerable groups – particularly for children at risk of poverty, persons with disabilities and older persons in need of long-term care. Investments in health will focus on training medical workers.
Dedicated activities under the programme will provide basic material assistance, such as food and hot meals to at-risk individuals and families, including homeless and other vulnerable people.

The programme will encourage innovative solutions to key social policy challenges. Community centres will be established to empower the local population and advance the relationship between Roma and majority populations in the wider community. Development of innovative, non-institutional social services will be financed to support the continuation of the deinstitutionalisation, especially of long-term care for persons with disabilities and for older people.

programme_name: (Interreg VI-A) IPA CBC Croatia-Bosnia and Herzegovina- Montenegro
programme_description: The programme mission is to strengthen the social, economic and territorial development of the cross-border area and to support cross-border cooperation in the fields of innovation and competitive entrepreneurship, environment protection and risk management, accessible health services, and sustainable tourism and culture.

The programme focuses on fostering SME growth and supporting their digital transformation, and on improving the capacity of research organizations contributing to social development and economic growth, with emphasis on environment and climate change related issues. Furthermore, key accent is put on energy efficiency, biodiversity in the context of climate change resilience and circular economy concepts.

In addition, by investing in equipment, new services and protocols, as well as strengthening the human resources, the aim is to modernize the health system and make the health care more efficient and responsive.

Finally, the programme supports the diversification of tourism by investing in lesser-known destinations and diverse forms of tourism, as well as the social innovation models and practices in cultural and tourism sector, that simultaneously meet social needs and create new collaborations between public, civil society and private organisations.

The programme will help to address main regional imbalances and contribute to reducing disparities in the development of the involved regions. It is designed as a mechanism that will foster cooperation in the fields of innovation, environment, health and sustainable tourism.

That will be achieved by building cross-sectoral capacities and increasing the innovation potential. It will also contribute to accessibility and effectiveness of the health care and social care system by improving infrastructure, skills and organisation of health care and social care system. It will support the specific, innovative, sustainable, green, digital and smart forms of tourism and culture. Supporting the goals of the EU Green Deal, the programme will focus its attention on sustainability and resilience. The proposed actions will contribute to greener, smarter and more inclusive Europe. Special attention will be given to ensuring vibrant cooperation between universities, scientific communities and industry, including citizens and their representatives, in order to bridge the gaps between territories, generations and regional cultures, especially caring for the needs of the young in shaping Europe’s future.

The programme will help Croatia in facing its challenges in its adaptation to a greener and more digital economy, while achieving major EU policy objectives. The programme seeks to increase regional economic competitiveness by improving the lives of citizens through better services and better infrastructure, along with support to the development of businesses. Among its areas of intervention, the programme has four priorities:

Firstly, it aims at improving the country’s competitiveness by investing in research and development. This will entail the digitalisation of businesses and an increase in the availability and quality of e-services. Particular attention will also be paid to supporting small and medium enterprises to become stronger competitors within the global market while assisting workers in adapting their skills.

Secondly, the programme will help Croatia join the common effort for a greener, lower carbon and more resilient Europe. Funds will target improving energy efficiency, increasing the share of renewables in energy production. The EU's support will ensure the development of smart energy systems, encourage circular economy approaches and assist sustainable waste and water management. Such measure will contribute to Coratia's resilience to climate change, by protecting biodiversity and managing risks.

Thirdly, the programme will improve connectivity and mobility by improving transport. This will carried out through a range of much-needed improvements to the national rail infrastructure and further development of maritime infrastructure coherently with the needs of Croatia's coastal areas and islands.

Finally, with an eye at making both Europe and Croatia more inclusive, the programme will further children's participation in kindergartens and day school by raising their overall quality. Substantial funding will be devoted to upgrading social services and healthcare for the most vulnerable people.

The objective pursued is to prepare school and university audiences, apprentices, for work life using innovative communication tools.

Programme activities will include accompanying measures supporting their social inclusion.
This programme complements actions implemented at national level as part of the

, National Nutrition Health Programme and National Poverty Prevention and Reduction Strategy. Support from the ESF+ also complements the traditional sources of supply (e.g. food donations, distribution of unsold food) provided by national associations.

Activities financed by the ESF+ programme will foster equal opportunities for people who belong to vulnerable groups.  These measures aim to mitigate the ongoing social impacts of the coronavirus pandemic, which resulted in an almost forty per cent increase in people using distribution centres, including new groups accessing food aid such as students. The programme will also support activities that significantly reduce the number of people at risk of poverty and social exclusion.

Food aid will reach the entire French metropolitan territory and the outermost regions of Guadeloupe, Martinique and Réunion, and will be distributed by authorised national associations. A paper and/or electronic voucher scheme will be implemented in Mayotte.

Beyond the urgency to meeting and complementing essential food needs, food aid is a lever for social and professional integration. Food aid, whether direct or indirect, will be complemented by social accompanying measures, including information on relevant social support tailored to the individual needs of beneficiaries.

programme_description: The programme provides support for unemployed and self-employed people, and for social enterprises. Its priorities include reducing the risk of early school leaving and promoting lifelong learning and vocational training.

All jobseekers, particularly young people, can be supported by the programme. This is done through measures to promote self-employment, social entrepreneurship, and business creation. The programme’s focus is on the social economy and solidarity, and on promoting social innovation.

The programme also works to anticipate future employment needs, the skills required for these jobs, and to promote the integration of the most disadvantaged groups into the labour market. This includes persons with disabilities, the long-term unemployed, and young people not in education, training, or employment.

In line with recommendations to ensure equal opportunities for all, funded projects promote equal access to and completion of quality and inclusive education and training, from early childhood education and care through general and vocational education and training, including at adult age. Specific measures aim to reduce the risk of young people dropping out of school and provide support for returning to school or for obtaining sufficient education or training.

To better adapt the skills of working and non-working people to the needs of a dynamic labour market, and to help them make career transitions, especially to jobs in the green and digital economy, funding will be used to increase opportunities for lifelong learning and professional mobility. Job seekers will receive support with improving their qualifications, shortening the length of time they spend in unemployment, and finding suitable jobs in sectors with existing labour shortages in Île-de-France.

programme_description: Since the industrial revolution, North-West Europe has been at the vanguard of industrialisation and economic development in Europe. However, this century of growth came at a great cost: for the environment, for people, for territorial inequalities. The programme is looking for ways to contribute to compensate for such costs.

The overall aim of the programme and of its actions is to contribute to a balanced development across the North-West Europe programme area, regardless of the type of territory, helping to make it greener, more innovative, and more inclusive.

Through the programme, the EU supports the North-West Europe regions to be more resilient to climate change, to strengthen ecological connectivity, to reduce pollution and CO2 emissions, to transit towards greener solutions, such as renewable energy and circular economy. At the same time the EU will accompany both public and private players in the region while they develop their capacity for innovation capacity.

The programme contributes also to a more effective, inclusive, and quality labour market. In fact, it helps vulnerable groups, and it supports the emergence of available, accessible, inclusive, and resilient healthcare systems for all citizens.
Finally, it contributes to strengthen economic development, social inclusion and social innovation enhancing the role of culture and sustainable tourism.

The intensification of outermost regions’ (OR) cooperation with neighbouring countries has been a key pillar of the EU strategy for these regions since 2004. Thus, the Caribbean programme aims at enhancing regional integration of Guadeloupe, Martinique, French Guiana and Saint Martin into a geographical area covering 40 third countries.

In the area of cooperation, the programme identifies the following commonly shared challenges: high exposure to natural hazards, climate change, dependence on fossil fuels, circular economy, insufficient quality and high costs of digital services, weak maritime and air connections, biodiversity conservation, waste management, extension of chronic pathologies and limited access to employment for young people.

Considering these challenges, the programme introduces new key investment priorities in the cooperation dynamic: research and innovation, renewable energies, waste management and a better connectivity for the Caribbean area.
Another noticeable novelty is the continuation of the cooperation between the French and Dutch sides of the island of Saint Martin within a specific territorial axis.

The thematic coverage of the Caribbean programme paves the way for potential complementarities with the new EU's "Global Europe" - Neighborhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument (NDICI).

programme_description: The programme aims to make the region more attractive, innovative, green and inclusive. To that end, investments into the green and digital transition will play a key role to ensure quality of life in both urban and rural areas.

The EU support will transform the region’s economy through support for research and innovation as well as for the sustainable development of small and medium enterprises. Investments in energy efficiency, sustainable urban mobility and renewable energy will help the region’s “green transition”.

For people, the programme supports lifelong learning and career transitions in order to adapt skills to new needs arising. Through a participative mechanism of local partnerships, the programme also wants to ensure that every area develops suitable solutions for its specific needs.

Finally, the EU support will accompany the territories most impacted by the green transition, especially those with carbon intensive industries. To this end, specific investments will encourage recycling materials, increasing the use of renewable energy and industrial innovation. Such investments will match the upskilling and reskilling of workers with the aim of ensuring a just transition.

programme_description: The Guiana Shield is a plural cooperation area, which is marked by a strong geographical and natural coherence, while being fragmented from a political and institutional point of view. Guyane is a French overseas region, and an outermost European region. Suriname and Guyana are two independent states. A former Dutch colony, Suriname is independent since 1975. A former British colony, Guyana is a country independent of the British crown since 1966 and member of the Commonwealth. Amapá, Amazonas and Pará are three federated states of Brazil.

The cooperation area brings together territories with different official languages: French, Dutch, Portuguese and English. The cooperation territory also brings together territories with different legal systems. Moreover, the political borders of the cooperation space do not correspond to its ethnocultural borders: within the different territories of the cooperation area there is a strong ethnic, linguistic, religious and cultural diversity and these communities are sometimes common to different states and territories. The cooperation area has more than 30 different ethnic and cultural groups

The Amazonia Territorial Cooperation Programme is the main instrument for promoting the regional integration of the Guiana Shield into their geographical unity, highlighting the importance of regional cooperation and good neighbourly relations in fostering sustainable economic development and strengthening political stability.

The overall aim of the programme is to enhance sustainable growth and competitiveness in the Guiana Shield, as well as helping the region to be more resilient to climate change, better equipped for disaster risk prevention. Boosting the transition to a circular and resource-efficient economy and preservation of nature, biodiversity and green infrastructures are other programme’s aims. The programme reinforces the cooperation in the health sector to fight together against common pathologies (malaria, HIV, dengue fever) and to improve cross border mobility of patients. The cooperation area suffers from a significant deficiency in the supply of care, and from limited access to care due to the isolation of the territories.
Improving equal access to inclusive and quality services in education is another objective of the programme, together with the promotion of the socioeconomic inclusion of marginalised communities.

A novelty for this programming period is the Amazonia programme strategical alignment with the Atlantic Maritime Strategy. This functions as a support to research and investments in marine renewable energies, costal protection. Moreover, it helps combating marine pollution by supporting green shipping; and job creation by supporting cooperation between EU training centres and businesses.

Finally, the programme pays special attention to governance matters, to reinforce the institutional capacity of public actors in order to strengthen and improve coordination processes between the new ERDF program and the new Instrument for Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation (NDICI).

The programme aims to support projects for citizens of rural areas facing demographic challenges like ageing and depopulation. These two phenomena create imbalances along the urban/rural areas divide as well as on the littoral/interior divide, as citizens move away from the countryside and coasts to concentrate in large urban areas.

Rural areas are particularly affected by the struggle to find skilled labour force while providing quality of life and basic services, like internet access, transport and healthcare. The programme aims to experiment with joint solutions to favour social or local innovation. Areas of interventions will likely be social economy, silver economy
development based on local resources or collaborative governance between the countries of the region.

Another of the programme's main objectives is the promotion of cooperation projects attempting to mitigate the consequences of climate change. Among the most alarming consequences of climate change are the increased intensity and frequency of certain natural hazards (drought, fires, rainfalls) affecting both the environment and economic activities.

The programme area of South West Europe has strengths allowing for actions that draw from its own resources and ecosystems: extensive forest mass, connectivity of Natura 2000 network sites, high number of protected natural areas and habitats, good relative groundwater and surface water quality, previous experience in the efficient use of water resources, but also knowledge centres experienced in analyzing and finding solutions tailored to each territory. These strengths need to be combined through the INTERREG projects to respond to territorial needs.

programme_description: The programme fosters fair and sustainable cooperation between 7 EU Member States and 8 partner countries in the Southern Neighbourhood (i.e. Algeria, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, Tunisia and Türkiye). The participating countries jointly developed the programme based on the principle of equal footing. There is a strong and shared understanding that many of today’s challenges in the Mediterranean Sea Basin are common across the countries in the region and that there is an urgent need to find common solutions.

The largest part of EU funding (42%) will be allocated to projects that address climate change and environmental challenges. these include energy efficiency measures, sustainable water use, climate change adaptation, circular economy as well as risk prevention.

Secondly, the programme aims to create a more competitive and smarter Mediterranean by providing support and improving conditions for SMEs. Such actions should pave the way for greater internationalisation, transnational research-business cooperation as well as reducing disparities and gaps in research and innovation across the Mediterranean.

The third aim is to foster a more social and inclusive Mediterranean by providing better quality and access to education and training. This will concern young people and disadvantaged groups in particular. Health represents a key factor in the reduction of economic and social inequalities. Therefore, project partners will focus on developing innovative digital and services that improve the delivery and efficiency of health services.

Finally, the programme aims to improve the cooperation governance across the Mediterranean through a number of tools, including joint capacity building actions for public authorities as well as transnational cooperation between citizens, civil society actors and public institutions based on bottom-up and participatory approaches.
The programme has a particular focus on young people and it will ensure a strong system of complementarities and synergies with other EU funding streams operating in the Mediterranean.

programme_description: Romania’s national ESF+ programme for education and employment invests in the development of the country’s human capital. It supports improved access to quality education and training in every stage of life, and an inclusive labour market. The aim is to ensure that no one is left behind in an era of rapid economic and social change, empowering people across the country with the skills needed for the digital and green transitions.
The programme will implement the principles of the

by promoting equal opportunities and access to jobs, fair working conditions, social protection and inclusion. It will also support Romania’s commitment to achieve its 2030 social targets of increasing the employment rate to nearly 75% and the number of adults in training every year to over 17%, while reducing the number of people at risk of poverty by over 2.5 million.

Public employment services (PES) will be supported to hire more staff and expand training resources. ESF+ investments will ensure that these services remain relevant in a changing labour market, meeting both employers’ and jobseekers’ needs.
The ESF+ Education and Employment programme will strengthen social dialogue and partnerships for employment and training, stepping up the involvement of civil society organisations.

Young people, particularly those who are not in education, employment or training, will receive support from a youth network funded by ESF+. This network coordinates activities between the PES and stakeholders, helping young people to find a job or continue their education.
Romania’s national ESF+ programme will implement the new

initiative for international mobility, providing disadvantaged young people with opportunities for short-term work placements abroad. ESF+ investments will also support the development of youth entrepreneurship and social enterprises helping disadvantaged young people with social and professional integration.

Dedicated measures will focus on the integration of women, persons with disabilities, and those from minority communities into the labour market, particularly in regions with the most pressing labour shortages. Employers will be supported to create facilities, engage in partnerships, expand childcare services for young children (0-6 years old) and adapt to more flexible forms of work, promoting work-life balance and gender equality.

The programme will invest in training and counselling for entrepreneurs, in grants for start-ups and in further support. The social economy sector will be strengthened through combined financial support, using both grants and financial instruments, including for labour market inclusion of disadvantaged workers, and the development of collaborative/participatory instruments.

Investments in early childhood education aim at improving both its quality and accessibility. Among other measures, staff will receive additional training, and the quality assurance system will be enhanced – with new standards established.

Disadvantaged children and families will benefit from socio-educational assistance and material support, encouraging participation in formal education from an early age. ESF+ measures will prevent early school leaving by supporting at-risk students. These measures will focus on helping children from disadvantaged backgrounds, including children with disabilities and/or special needs, Roma, and children from rural areas.

Financing from the ESF+ will ensure vocational education and training (VET) remains relevant to the labour market needs, building the quality of VET through work-based learning, as well as upskilling educational staff. The programme will also fund the development of a system for the recognition of excellence in VET, particularly for skills supporting the digital and green professions.

Tertiary education will be strengthened, making post-secondary education more accessible and relevant. Funds will be used to develop a quality assurance system for adult learning and encourage people to take part in such schemes by increasing the offer for micro-credential certifications, implementing a pilot project on individual learning accounts and expanding ‘second chance’ educational programmes for young people and adults who have not completed formal education.
More than 1.5 million people are expected to benefit from Romania’s national ESF+ programme, including:

This will cover actions aimed at increasing preparedness for natural and human-made threats, but also address the protection of natural habitats and mapping pollution sources from air, soil and water. Another important element will be investing in information campaigns concerning the sustainable use of natural resources.
The programme will also help to identify and test cooperative approaches to cultural activities and tourism-related services. This will be done by involving youth and educating it on cultural values.
Finally, the programme is designed to enhance the cooperation of public authorities when it concerns legal and administrative burdens that make cooperation across borders difficult.
The programme is Romania’s main instrument to address environmental and climate challenges. It aims to ensure a green, net zero-carbon economy and resilient Europe.
This includes support for water management, circular economy, climate change mitigation and adaptation, natural disasters risk prevention and management, and the energy transition

Water management projects will focus on improving drinking water quality and wastewater treatment, and increase the population’s access to distribution networks. Investments will reduce water losses, connect the population to compliant water supply systems, provide systems for collecting and treating wastewater, and monitor water quality at national level.
A circular economy will be supported through investments in the separation of waste streams, waste recovery and treatment, and adaptation of existing waste treatment facilities.

The programme aims to boost investments in key sectors for the benefit of the people and businesses in the region. It will contribute to making the region and Europe greener, more social and inclusive, and closer to citizens and their needs.

Through the funds of European Territorial Cooperation and the Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance, the EU supports the region to reduce energy emissions through the promotion of renewable energy and to enhance the protection and preservation of biodiversity and the environment. Conditions for a more social and inclusive region will be fostering the improvement of skills and trainings for enhanced employability and better access to and resilience of the health care system as well as investments in sustainable tourism as one of the biggest economic drivers for the region.

Finally, investments will target sustainable tourism as one of the biggest economic drivers for the region while diversifying and innovate offers to better attract and manage the tourist flows of the natural resources, cultural and historical sites in the region.

The programme aims to boost cross-border cooperation between Romania and the Republic of Moldova in order to address the vital needs of the border regions. This is particularly important now that the Moldovan population is highly impacted by the consequences of the Russian military aggression against Ukraine.

The principle of partnership is a key feature of this programme, as it enables Romania and Moldova to cooperate on an equal footing.Highly appreciated by all the stakeholders, it allows Moldova to gain experience with EU shared management.

The programme will provide financing for investments in climate change adaptation measures and disaster risk resilience of border regions. It also entails inclusive education and quality health care services. In particular, it will support joint solutions for preservation of nature, biodiversity, green infrastructure, protection of culture and tourism, and also improvement of border management.

By adopting this programme the Commission sends a strong signal of support to Moldova. Currents needs and future developments in the border area will inform and underpin adjustments to the programme priorities of the future.

The programme will invest in Romania’s West development region – in the counties of Arad, Timis, Caras-Severin and Hunedoara – in line with five cohesion policy objectives for the 2021-2027 programming period. EU funds will be used to both address regional development challenges, such as territorial disparities and climate change, and contribute to the EU objectives of a green transition and digital economy.
